## Dialogue: a new flat

{安娜|Ān nà} (安娜) comes to visit her friend {王芳|Wáng Fāng} (王芳), whose family has just
moved. The building's name, {北京|Běi jīng}{小区|xiǎo qū} ("Beijing Estate", {小区|xiǎo qū} being
a housing estate), is made up.

```dialogue
# A new flat
安娜: {喂|wèi}，{王芳|Wáng Fāng}，{我|wǒ}{到|dào}{了|le}，{在|zài}{你|nǐ}{家|jiā}{楼下|lóu xià}。{你|nǐ}{家|jiā}{在|zài}{几|jǐ}{楼|lóu}？
= Hi, Wang Fang, I'm here, at the bottom of your building. Which floor are you on?
王芳: {六|liù}{楼|lóu}，{六|liù}{零|líng}{二|èr}。
= The sixth floor, 602.
安娜: {你|nǐ}{家|jiā}{真|zhēn}{漂亮|piào liang}！{有|yǒu}{几|jǐ}{间|jiān}{房间|fáng jiān}？
= Your flat is lovely! How many rooms are there?
王芳: {三|sān}{间|jiān}。{这|zhè}{间|jiān}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{爸爸|bà ba}{妈妈|mā ma}{的|de}，{那|nà}{间|jiān}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{奶奶|nǎi nai}{的|de}。
= Three. This one is my parents', that one is my grandma's.
安娜: {你|nǐ}{的|de}{房间|fáng jiān}{呢|ne}？
= And your room?
王芳: {在|zài}{右边|yòu bian}。{你|nǐ}{看|kàn}，{里面|lǐ miàn}{很|hěn}{小|xiǎo}，{但|dàn}{很|hěn}{舒服|shū fu}。
= On the right. Look, it's small inside, but comfortable.
安娜: {床|chuáng}{下面|xià miàn}{是|shì}{什么|shén me}？{是|shì}{你|nǐ}{的|de}{猫|māo}{吗|ma}？
= What's that under the bed? Is it your cat?
王芳: {对|duì}，{它|tā}{很|hěn}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{在|zài}{下面|xià miàn}{睡觉|shuì jiào}。
= Yes, it loves sleeping under there.
安娜: {请问|qǐng wèn}，{洗手间|xǐ shǒu jiān}{在|zài}{哪儿|nǎr}？
= Where's the bathroom, please?
王芳: {在|zài}{外面|wài miàn}，{门|mén}{旁边|páng biān}。
= Outside, next to the door.
```

Notice: {六|liù}{零|líng}{二|èr} reads the flat number digit by digit, as with phone and room
numbers in HSK 1. {但|dàn} (but) is lesson 15's word; here it joins two short sentences.
{下面|xià miàn} on its own means "under there", since the bed was just named.

## Reading: my home

> {我|wǒ}{叫|jiào}{李明|Lǐ Míng}，{我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{在|zài}{北京|Běi jīng}。{我们|wǒ men}{家|jiā}{的|de}{楼|lóu}{很|hěn}{高|gāo}，{我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{在|zài}{十二|shí èr}{楼|lóu}。{家|jiā}{里|lǐ}{有|yǒu}{三|sān}{间|jiān}{房间|fáng jiān}{和|hé}{一|yí}{个|gè}{洗手间|xǐ shǒu jiān}。{我|wǒ}{的|de}{房间|fáng jiān}{在|zài}{左边|zuǒ bian}，{不|bú}{大|dà}，{里面|lǐ miàn}{有|yǒu}{床|chuáng}、{桌子|zhuō zi}{和|hé}{电脑|diàn nǎo}。{我|wǒ}{经常|jīng cháng}{在|zài}{床|chuáng}{上|shàng}{看|kàn}{书|shū}。{楼下|lóu xià}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{超市|chāo shì}，{超市|chāo shì}{旁边|páng biān}{是|shì}{地铁|dì tiě}{站|zhàn}。{外面|wài miàn}{有点儿|yǒu diǎnr}{吵|chǎo}，{但|dàn}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{我|wǒ}{家|jiā}。

({吵|chǎo}: noisy.)

Read it once for the gist, then again with the pinyin. Then answer:

1. Which floor does Li Ming live on?
2. What is in his room?
3. What is next to the supermarket?

<details>
<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. The twelfth ({十二|shí èr}{楼|lóu}).
2. A bed, a desk and a computer.
3. The metro station ({地铁|dì tiě}{站|zhàn}).

"My name is Li Ming and my home is in Beijing. Our building is very tall; we live on the twelfth
floor. At home there are three rooms and a bathroom. My room is on the left. It isn't big; in it
there's a bed, a desk and a computer. I often read in bed. Downstairs there's a supermarket, and
next to the supermarket is the metro station. It's a bit noisy outside, but I really like our
home."
</details>

## Say it

```speak
{里面|lǐ miàn}{有|yǒu}{人|rén}{吗|ma}？
= Is anyone in there?
{请问|qǐng wèn}，{洗手间|xǐ shǒu jiān}{在|zài}{哪儿|nǎr}？
= Excuse me, where's the toilet?
{你|nǐ}{家|jiā}{在|zài}{几|jǐ}{楼|lóu}？
= Which floor is your flat on?
{我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{有|yǒu}{三|sān}{间|jiān}{房间|fáng jiān}。
= Our flat has three rooms.
{外面|wài miàn}{很|hěn}{冷|lěng}。
= It's cold outside.
```

## Pronunciation

- {楼|lóu} rises; don't let it fall like English "low". Compare {六|liù}{楼|lóu}: a fall, then a rise.
- {床|chuáng}: *ch* with the tongue curled back and a puff of air, then *uang* as one glide, rising.
- In {里面|lǐ miàn} and {外面|wài miàn} the -{面|miàn} keeps its fourth tone in careful speech;
  in fast speech it can sound lighter, but it's written *miàn*.
- {洗手间|xǐ shǒu jiān} starts with two third tones: the first rises, so it's said *xí shǒu jiān*.

## Common mistakes

- A short form alone: ~~{里|lǐ}{有|yǒu}{人|rén}{吗|ma}？~~ Say {里面|lǐ miàn}{有|yǒu}{人|rén}{吗|ma}？,
  or put a noun first: {房间|fáng jiān}{里|lǐ}{有|yǒu}{人|rén}{吗|ma}？
- English order: ~~{在|zài}{上面|shàng miàn}{桌子|zhuō zi}~~ for "on top of the table". The
  position word follows the noun: {在|zài}{桌子|zhuō zi}{上面|shàng miàn}.
- ~~{第|dì}{五|wǔ}{楼|lóu}~~ or ~~{两|liǎng}{楼|lóu}~~ for a floor: {五|wǔ}{楼|lóu}, {二|èr}{楼|lóu}.
- Counting a British way: the street-level floor is {一|yī}{楼|lóu}.
- ~~{在|zài}{床|chuáng}{里|lǐ}~~ for "in bed": {在|zài}{床|chuáng}{上|shàng}.

## Key points

- {上面|shàng miàn}, {下面|xià miàn}, {里面|lǐ miàn}, {外面|wài miàn} stand alone or follow a noun;
  {上|shàng}, {下|xià}, {里|lǐ}, {外|wài} only follow a noun. -{面|miàn} = -{边|biān}.
- Number + {楼|lóu} is a floor (an ordinal without {第|dì}): {五|wǔ}{楼|lóu}, {二|èr}{楼|lóu},
  {一|yī}{楼|lóu} at street level; {几|jǐ}{楼|lóu}？ {楼上|lóu shàng} / {楼下|lóu xià}.
- {间|jiān} counts rooms: {三|sān}{间|jiān}{房间|fáng jiān}, {这|zhè}{间|jiān}.
- {洗手间|xǐ shǒu jiān} is the polite word for the toilet; {床|chuáng}{上|shàng} is "in bed".

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Bringing things up and taking them down: 上来, 下去, 拿出来
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

In lesson 09 you learned {进来|jìn lái}, {出去|chū qù}, {回来|huí lái} and the rest: a movement
plus {来|lái} (towards the speaker) or {去|qù} (away from the speaker). Lesson 11 put you in a
flat on the sixth floor. This lesson adds the movements that go with stairs and rooms: up
({上来|shàng lái}, {上去|shàng qù}), down ({下来|xià lái}, {下去|xià qù}), over
({过来|guò lái}, {过去|guò qù}) and up from bed or a chair ({起来|qǐ lái}).

Then comes the big step: putting these after another verb, so that you can say "bring it up",
"take it down", "walk over" and "take it out" ({拿|ná}{上来|shàng lái}, {拿|ná}{下去|xià qù},
{走|zǒu}{过来|guò lái}, {拿|ná}{出来|chū lái}). Two new verbs help: {拿|ná} (to take, to hold) and
{打开|dǎ kāi} (to open).

## {来|lái} and {去|qù}: where is the speaker?

Everything in this lesson depends on one question: is the movement towards the person speaking,
or away from them?

| | Towards the speaker | Away from the speaker |
|---|---|---|
| up | {上来|shàng lái} come up | {上去|shàng qù} go up |
| down | {下来|xià lái} come down | {下去|xià qù} go down |
| in | {进来|jìn lái} come in | {进去|jìn qù} go in |
| out | {出来|chū lái} come out | {出去|chū qù} go out |
| back | {回来|huí lái} come back | {回去|huí qù} go back |
| over, across | {过来|guò lái} come over | {过去|guò qù} go over |

You're on the sixth floor and your friend is in the street:

{你|nǐ}{上来|shàng lái}{吧|ba}！ — Come up!
{你|nǐ}{等|děng}{一下|yí xià}，{我|wǒ}{下去|xià qù}。 — Wait a moment, I'll come down.

English says "I'll come down" here, but Chinese uses {下去|xià qù}: you are moving away from
where you are now. Chinese measures from the speaker's own position (or the place the story is
told from). The exception from lesson 09 works here too: {我|wǒ}{下来|xià lái} is also heard, from your
friend's side, as {我|wǒ}{马上|mǎ shàng}{出来|chū lái} was. ({等|děng}, to wait, is lesson 20's word.)

Your friend, in the street, says the opposite:

{我|wǒ}{上去|shàng qù}{吧|ba}？ — Shall I come up?
{你|nǐ}{下来|xià lái}{吧|ba}，{我们|wǒ men}{去|qù}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}。 — You come down, and we'll go and eat.

*{过来|guò lái} and {过去|guò qù}*: over, across a space (a room, a street, a crowd):

{你|nǐ}{过来|guò lái}{一下|yí xià}。 — Come over here a moment.
{我|wǒ}{过去|guò qù}{看看|kàn kan}。 — I'll go over and have a look.

The {过|guò} here is the verb "to pass" (lesson 13 teaches it), not the experience particle
{过|guo} of lesson 10. {过去|guò qù} also means "the past" in HSK 3.

## {起来|qǐ lái}: get up

{起来|qǐ lái} is to get up: out of bed, or up from a chair or the floor.

{早上|zǎo shang}{七|qī}{点|diǎn}{起来|qǐ lái}。 — I get up at seven in the morning.
{快|kuài}{起来|qǐ lái}，{八|bā}{点|diǎn}{了|le}！ — Get up, it's eight o'clock! ({快|kuài}: quickly, lesson 14.)

{起床|qǐ chuáng} (HSK 1) is only "get out of bed"; {起来|qǐ lái} is the movement up from anywhere.
To stand up from a chair, Chinese adds {站|zhàn} "to stand" in front: {站|zhàn}{起来|qǐ lái}. That
{站|zhàn} is an HSK 3 word (lesson 08's {站|zhàn} is a station).

## {拿|ná}: take, hold

{拿|ná} is to take something in your hand, pick it up, carry it, or hold it:

{你|nǐ}{拿|ná}{着|zhe}{什么|shén me}？ — What have you got there?
{他|tā}{手|shǒu}{里|lǐ}{拿|ná}{着|zhe}{一|yì}{本|běn}{书|shū}。 — He's holding a book. ({着|zhe} for a lasting state, lesson 03)

On its own it's a little bare; most of the time {拿|ná} comes with a direction, as below.

## Compound direction complements

Put the words from the table after a verb of movement, and you have a
**[[compound direction complement]]**: verb + direction ({上|shàng} {下|xià} {进|jìn} {出|chū} {回|huí} {过|guò} {起|qǐ}) + {来|lái} / {去|qù}.
The first part says which way the thing moves; the second says whether it comes towards the
speaker or goes away.

| Verb | + {上来|shàng lái} / {上去|shàng qù} | + {下来|xià lái} / {下去|xià qù} | + {出来|chū lái} / {出去|chū qù} | + {过来|guò lái} / {过去|guò qù} |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| {走|zǒu} walk | {走|zǒu}{上来|shàng lái} walk up (here) | {走|zǒu}{下去|xià qù} walk down (there) | {走|zǒu}{出去|chū qù} walk out | {走|zǒu}{过来|guò lái} walk over (here) |
| {拿|ná} take | {拿|ná}{上去|shàng qù} take up | {拿|ná}{下来|xià lái} bring down | {拿|ná}{出来|chū lái} take out | {拿|ná}{过来|guò lái} bring over |

The same works with {进|jìn}, {回|huí} and {起|qǐ}: {走|zǒu}{进来|jìn lái} (walk in),
{拿|ná}{回去|huí qù} (take back), {拿|ná}{起来|qǐ lái} (pick up).

{妈妈|mā ma}{走|zǒu}{过来|guò lái}{了|le}。 — Mum came over (to me).
{你|nǐ}{的|de}{东西|dōng xi}{在|zài}{楼上|lóu shàng}，{我|wǒ}{拿|ná}{下来|xià lái}{吧|ba}。 — Your things are upstairs; I'll bring them down.
{他|tā}{拿|ná}{起来|qǐ lái}{看|kàn}{了|le}{看|kan}。 — He picked it up and had a look.

Note the last one: {看|kàn}{了|le}{看|kan} is verb reduplication (module 1) with {了|le} in the
middle, "had a quick look".

*How they sound.* After a verb, {来|lái} and {去|qù} are usually light, and so is the
direction word before them: *ná chu lai*, *zǒu guo qu*. Dictionaries and this course
write the full tones, but listen for the light ending. When the words stand alone as verbs
({你|nǐ}{上来|shàng lái}{吧|ba}), {来|lái} and {去|qù} keep more of their tone.

### Where does the object go?

*A place* always goes before {来|lái} / {去|qù}, never after them:

{他|tā}{走|zǒu}{进|jìn}{房间|fáng jiān}{来|lái}{了|le}。 — He walked into the room. (towards me)
{我们|wǒ men}{走|zǒu}{上|shàng}{楼|lóu}{去|qù}{吧|ba}。 — Let's walk upstairs. (I'm downstairs)
~~{我们|wǒ men}{走|zǒu}{上去|shàng qù}{楼|lóu}~~ is wrong.

*A thing* can go in the same place, before {来|lái} / {去|qù}. Learn this order first:

{你|nǐ}{拿|ná}{一|yì}{杯|bēi}{水|shuǐ}{来|lái}。 — Bring a glass of water. (here, to me)
{他|tā}{拿|ná}{出|chū}{一|yì}{本|běn}{书|shū}{来|lái}。 — He took out a book.

You'll also hear the thing at the very end, after the whole complement, when the action has
happened: {他|tā}{拿|ná}{出来|chū lái}{一|yì}{本|běn}{书|shū}。 Both are correct; just never put a
place there.

Often there's no object at all, because it's clear what is meant: {拿|ná}{出来|chū lái}{吧|ba}
("take it out").

## {打开|dǎ kāi}: open

{打开|dǎ kāi} is "to open" for anything that is closed: a door, a book, a box, a bag, a file. It
also switches on a phone, a computer or a TV.

{请|qǐng}{打开|dǎ kāi}{书|shū}。 — Please open your books. (a classroom instruction)
{你|nǐ}{打开|dǎ kāi}{门|mén}{看看|kàn kan}。 — Open the door and have a look.
{我|wǒ}{打开|dǎ kāi}{电脑|diàn nǎo}，{看|kàn}{了|le}{一下|yí xià}。 — I turned on the computer and had a look.

{开|kāi} (HSK 1) can do most of this too: {开门|kāi mén}, {开|kāi}{电视|diàn shì}. {打开|dǎ kāi}
is the fuller verb for the act of opening, and the one you need for books, boxes and bags
({开|kāi}{书|shū} isn't said). The opposite is {关|guān} (to close, switch off: HSK 3).

In {打开|dǎ kāi} the {开|kāi} says what happens to the thing: it ends up open. You'll meet many
verbs built like this in module 4.

## Characters
{=

| Character | Meaning | Pinyin | Radical | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 拿 | take, hold | ná | 手 | 10 | {拿|ná}, {拿|ná}{出来|chū lái}, {拿|ná}{下去|xià qù} |

拿 is the same in traditional script. The other words of the lesson use characters you know
(上 下 过 起 来 去 打 开).

- 拿 is 合 ("join, bring together", HSK 3) over 手 (hand). The usual explanation is the obvious
  one: hands brought together to take hold of something. It's one of the few characters with
  the whole of 手 at the bottom instead of the side form 扌.

Radical review: 手 and its side form 扌, "hand". As a radical on the left it's 扌, three strokes
(a horizontal, a vertical hook, a rising stroke): 打 and 找 (HSK 1). At the bottom, in 拿, it's
the full 手. Hand radicals mean actions done with the hands.

### Stroke order

- 拿: 合 first, from the top: the roof (left-falling, then right-falling), the short horizontal,
  then 口. Then 手: the short left-falling stroke at the top, the two horizontals, and last the
  vertical with a hook. 6 + 4 = 10 strokes.

```trace
拿
```

=}

## Dialogue: up and down

{李明|Lǐ Míng} (李明) brings some things to the flat of his friend {王芳|Wáng Fāng} (王芳). He
calls from the street.

```dialogue
# Up and down
李明: {王芳|Wáng Fāng}，{我|wǒ}{在|zài}{楼下|lóu xià}。{你|nǐ}{下来|xià lái}{一下|yí xià}{吧|ba}。
= Wang Fang, I'm downstairs. Could you come down for a moment?
王芳: {你|nǐ}{上来|shàng lái}{吧|ba}，{我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{在|zài}{六|liù}{楼|lóu}。
= You come up, we're on the sixth floor.
李明: {东西|dōng xi}{很|hěn}{多|duō}，{你|nǐ}{能|néng}{下来|xià lái}{拿|ná}{一下|yí xià}{吗|ma}？
= There's a lot of stuff. Can you come down and take some?
王芳: {好|hǎo}，{我|wǒ}{下去|xià qù}。
= OK, I'm coming down.
李明: {这|zhè}{是|shì}{你|nǐ}{妈妈|mā ma}{的|de}{书|shū}{和|hé}{衣服|yī fu}，{她|tā}{昨天|zuó tiān}{在|zài}{我|wǒ}{家|jiā}，{没|méi}{拿|ná}{回去|huí qù}。
= These are your mum's books and clothes. She was at our place yesterday and didn't take them back.
王芳: {谢谢|xiè xie}！{你|nǐ}{拿|ná}{书|shū}，{我|wǒ}{拿|ná}{衣服|yī fu}。{我们|wǒ men}{走|zǒu}{上|shàng}{楼|lóu}{去|qù}{吧|ba}。
= Thanks! You take the books, I'll take the clothes. Let's walk up.
李明: {你|nǐ}{家|jiā}{真|zhēn}{热|rè}！
= It's really warm in your flat!
王芳: {你|nǐ}{坐|zuò}，{我|wǒ}{去|qù}{拿|ná}{两|liǎng}{杯|bēi}{水|shuǐ}{过来|guò lái}。{你|nǐ}{打开|dǎ kāi}{电视|diàn shì}{看看|kàn kan}{吧|ba}。
= Sit down; I'll go and get us two glasses of water. Turn on the TV if you like.
```

Notice:
- {我|wǒ}{下去|xià qù}: Wang Fang goes down to Li Ming, so from where she is it's {下去|xià qù}.
  Li Ming, below, asked her to {下来|xià lái}.
- {没|méi}{拿|ná}{回去|huí qù}: "didn't take them back (home)"; {没|méi} negates the completed action,
  as in HSK 1.
- {我|wǒ}{去|qù}{拿|ná}{两|liǎng}{杯|bēi}{水|shuǐ}{过来|guò lái}: she'll go to the kitchen and bring the water
  over to where they are now, so {过来|guò lái}. {拿|ná}{两|liǎng}{杯|bēi}{水|shuǐ}{来|lái} would work too.

## Reading: a note on the table

{王芳|Wáng Fāng} leaves a note for her mother on the table.

> {妈妈|mā ma}：{我|wǒ}{今天|jīn tiān}{六|liù}{点|diǎn}{就|jiù}{起来|qǐ lái}{了|le}。{早饭|zǎo fàn}{在|zài}{桌子|zhuō zi}{上|shàng}。{你|nǐ}{的|de}{书|shū}{和|hé}{衣服|yī fu}，{李明|Lǐ Míng}{昨天|zuó tiān}{拿|ná}{过来|guò lái}{了|le}，{我|wǒ}{拿|ná}{到|dào}{你|nǐ}{的|de}{房间|fáng jiān}{里|lǐ}{去|qù}{了|le}。{我|wǒ}{现在|xiàn zài}{出去|chū qù}，{下午|xià wǔ}{四|sì}{点|diǎn}{回来|huí lái}。{门口|mén kǒu}{的|de}{东西|dōng xi}{是|shì}{楼下|lóu xià}{张|Zhāng}{奶奶|nǎi nai}{的|de}，{你|nǐ}{出门|chū mén}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}{请|qǐng}{拿|ná}{下去|xià qù}{给|gěi}{她|tā}。{谢谢|xiè xie}！{王芳|Wáng Fāng}

({就|jiù}: already, as early as; lesson 18. {张|Zhāng}{奶奶|nǎi nai}: "Grandma Zhang", the friendly
way to name an older neighbour.)

1. When did Wang Fang get up?
2. Where did she put her mother's things?
3. When will she be back?

<details>
<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. At six ({六|liù}{点|diǎn}{就|jiù}{起来|qǐ lái}{了|le}).
2. In her mother's room ({拿|ná}{到|dào}{你|nǐ}{的|de}{房间|fáng jiān}{里|lǐ}{去|qù}{了|le}: "took them into your room").
3. At four in the afternoon.

"Mum: I was up at six today. Breakfast is on the table. Li Ming brought your books and clothes
over yesterday, and I took them to your room. I'm going out now and I'll be back at four this
afternoon. The things by the door are Grandma Zhang's from downstairs: when you go out, please
take them down to her. Thanks! Wang Fang"
</details>

## Say it

```speak
{你|nǐ}{上来|shàng lái}{吧|ba}！
= Come up!
{我|wǒ}{下去|xià qù}。
= I'll come down.
{你|nǐ}{过来|guò lái}{一下|yí xià}。
= Come over here a moment.
{请|qǐng}{打开|dǎ kāi}{书|shū}。
= Please open your books.
{我|wǒ}{拿|ná}{一|yì}{杯|bēi}{水|shuǐ}{过来|guò lái}。
= I'll bring a glass of water over.
```

## Pronunciation

- {拿|ná} rises, and it's *n*, not *l*: say {拿|ná} and {那|nà} (that) one after the other to hear
  the tone carry the difference.
- {起来|qǐ lái}: *q* is a puff of air with the tongue tip down behind the lower teeth, like the *ch*
  of "cheese" but further forward. Third tone, then a rise.
- {打开|dǎ kāi}: the *a* is open in both syllables, like "ah". A third tone before a first tone is
  said low and stays low ("half third tone").
- After a verb the complement is light: *ná chu lai*, *zǒu guo qu*.

## Common mistakes

- Using English "come" for every move towards the listener: when you go down to a friend waiting
  below, the safe choice is {我|wǒ}{下去|xià qù} ("I'm coming down" in English). {我|wǒ}{下来|xià lái} is heard
  too, measured from your friend's side (lesson 09), but don't use {来|lái} for every "come".
- A place after the complement: ~~{走|zǒu}{进来|jìn lái}{房间|fáng jiān}~~ → {走|zǒu}{进|jìn}{房间|fáng jiān}{来|lái}.
- ~~{开|kāi}{书|shū}~~ for "open the book": {打开|dǎ kāi}{书|shū}.
- Mixing up {起来|qǐ lái} and {起床|qǐ chuáng}: you can {起来|qǐ lái} from a chair, but you
  {起床|qǐ chuáng} only from bed.
- Writing 拿 with 扌 at the bottom: it's the full 手, with its first stroke a short left-falling
  stroke.

## Key points

- {来|lái}: towards the speaker; {去|qù}: away from the speaker. Measure from where the speaker is.
- {上来|shàng lái} / {上去|shàng qù}, {下来|xià lái} / {下去|xià qù}, {过来|guò lái} / {过去|guò qù},
  {起来|qǐ lái}: verbs on their own, and complements after another verb.
- Compound direction complement: verb + {上|shàng} / {下|xià} / {进|jìn} / {出|chū} / {回|huí} / {过|guò} / {起|qǐ} + {来|lái} / {去|qù}:
  {拿|ná}{下来|xià lái}, {走|zǒu}{过去|guò qù}, {拿|ná}{起来|qǐ lái}.
- A place goes before {来|lái} / {去|qù}: {走|zǒu}{上|shàng}{楼|lóu}{去|qù}. A thing can go there too:
  {拿|ná}{出|chū}{一|yì}{本|běn}{书|shū}{来|lái}.
- {拿|ná}: take, hold, carry; {打开|dǎ kāi}: open, switch on.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Birthdays: 送, 告诉, 准备
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Birthdays are one of the level-2 topics, and they bring a handful of everyday verbs with them:
{过|guò} (to spend, to celebrate a day), {送|sòng} (to give as a present), {告诉|gào su} (to tell)
and {准备|zhǔn bèi} (to prepare). Two of them take two objects, like {给|gěi} and {问|wèn} in
HSK 1: {送|sòng}{她|tā}{花|huā} (give her flowers), {告诉|gào su}{我|wǒ}{你|nǐ}{的|de}{生日|shēng rì}
(tell me your birthday). You'll also learn {生日快乐|shēng rì kuài lè}, the little particle
{啊|a} that makes speech sound warm, and how to write a short invitation.

## {生日|shēng rì} and {生日快乐|shēng rì kuài lè}

{生日|shēng rì} is a birthday: the "born day". Dates go big to small, as you learned in HSK 1:

{你|nǐ}{的|de}{生日|shēng rì}{是|shì}{几|jǐ}{月|yuè}{几|jǐ}{号|hào}？ — When is your birthday?
{我|wǒ}{的|de}{生日|shēng rì}{是|shì}{三|sān}{月|yuè}{八|bā}{号|hào}。 — My birthday is the eighth of March.
{今天|jīn tiān}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{妈妈|mā ma}{的|de}{生日|shēng rì}。 — Today is my mum's birthday.

The greeting is {生日快乐|shēng rì kuài lè}！ (Happy birthday!), often with {祝|zhù} (to wish)
in front: {祝|zhù}{你|nǐ}{生日快乐|shēng rì kuài lè}！ The birthday song in Chinese is just
those words, sung to the tune you know.

{快乐|kuài lè} or {高兴|gāo xìng}? Both are "happy", but they're used differently:

| | {快乐|kuài lè} | {高兴|gāo xìng} (HSK 1) |
|---|---|---|
| What it is | happiness as a state; joy | glad, pleased (about something now) |
| Typical use | wishes: {生日快乐|shēng rì kuài lè}, {新年|xīn nián}{快乐|kuài lè} | {认识|rèn shi}{你|nǐ}{很|hěn}{高兴|gāo xìng}, {我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{高兴|gāo xìng} |
| Example | {孩子|hái zi}{们|men}{很|hěn}{快乐|kuài lè}。 The children are happy. | {她|tā}{今天|jīn tiān}{很|hěn}{高兴|gāo xìng}。 She's in a good mood today. |

For your mood today, say {高兴|gāo xìng}. {快乐|kuài lè} is for wishes and for a happy life or
childhood. ({新年|xīn nián}, the New Year, is an HSK 3 word.)

## {过|guò}: to spend, to celebrate

{过|guò} is "to pass": you met it in {过来|guò lái} and {过去|guò qù}. With a day or a festival it
means to spend it, to celebrate it:

{你|nǐ}{生日|shēng rì}{怎么|zěn me}{过|guò}？ — How are you spending your birthday?
{我们|wǒ men}{给|gěi}{奶奶|nǎi nai}{过|guò}{生日|shēng rì}。 — We're having a birthday party for Grandma.
{你们|nǐ men}{在|zài}{哪儿|nǎr}{过年|guò nián}？ — Where are you spending the New Year?

{过生日|guò shēng rì} is to have (or celebrate) a birthday; {给|gěi} + person + {过生日|guò shēng rì}
is to celebrate someone else's. {过年|guò nián} is to celebrate the New Year, and in China that
means the Spring Festival, the lunar New Year (honors lesson 15h1). People greet each other with
{过年好|guò nián hǎo}！ (Happy New Year!).

*Two kinds of {过|guò}.* Don't mix this {过|guò} with the experience particle {过|guo} of lesson 10:

| | {过|guò} "to spend" (this lesson) | {过|guo} "have done" (lesson 10) |
|---|---|---|
| Tone | fourth | neutral |
| Where | the main verb, with its object after it | after another verb |
| Example | {我|wǒ}{在|zài}{北京|Běi jīng}{过年|guò nián}。 I'm spending New Year in Beijing. | {我|wǒ}{去|qù}{过|guo}{北京|Běi jīng}。 I've been to Beijing. |

## Two objects: {送|sòng} and {告诉|gào su}

In HSK 1, {给|gěi} and {问|wèn} took two objects: the person first, then the thing. {送|sòng} and
{告诉|gào su} work the same way. This is the **[[double object]]** sentence:

| Subject | Verb | Person | Thing |
|---|---|---|---|
| {我|wǒ} | {送|sòng} | {她|tā} | {一|yì}{本|běn}{书|shū}。 |
| {妈妈|mā ma} | {送|sòng}{了|le} | {我|wǒ} | {一|yí}{块|kuài}{手表|shǒu biǎo}。 |
| {你|nǐ} | {告诉|gào su} | {我|wǒ} | {你|nǐ}{的|de}{生日|shēng rì}。 |
| {他|tā} | {告诉|gào su}{了|le} | {老师|lǎo shī} | {一|yí}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}。 |

I'll give her a book. · Mum gave me a watch. · Tell me your birthday. · He told the teacher something.

{送|sòng} is to give as a present (to give in the sense of hand over is {给|gěi}). You'll also
hear {送给|sòng gěi} + person: {我|wǒ}{送给|sòng gěi}{她|tā}{一|yì}{本|běn}{书|shū}, with the same
meaning. When you hand over a present, {送|sòng}{你|nǐ}！ is "This is for you!"

{送|sòng} has a second meaning: to see someone off, or take them somewhere:

{我|wǒ}{送|sòng}{你|nǐ}{回家|huí jiā}。 — I'll see you home.
{爸爸|bà ba}{送|sòng}{我|wǒ}{去|qù}{机场|jī chǎng}。 — Dad's taking me to the airport.

{告诉|gào su} is to tell someone something. The "thing" can be a whole sentence:

{告诉|gào su}{你|nǐ}，{明天|míng tiān}{是|shì}{王芳|Wáng Fāng}{的|de}{生日|shēng rì}。 — Let me tell you: tomorrow is Wang Fang's birthday.
{他|tā}{没|méi}{告诉|gào su}{我|wǒ}{他|tā}{去|qù}{哪儿|nǎr}。 — He didn't tell me where he was going.

{说|shuō} (to say) can't take the person as an object: ~~{说|shuō}{我|wǒ}~~ isn't "tell me". Use
{告诉|gào su}{我|wǒ}, or put the person before {说|shuō} with {跟|gēn} (with), lesson 14's word:
{跟|gēn}{我|wǒ}{说|shuō}.

Either object can drop out when it's clear: {我|wǒ}{告诉|gào su}{他|tā}{了|le} (I've told him),
{你|nǐ}{送|sòng}{什么|shén me}？ (What are you giving?).

## {花|huā}: flowers

{花|huā} is a flower, or flowers:

{她|tā}{很|hěn}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{花|huā}。 — She loves flowers.
{我|wǒ}{送|sòng}{妈妈|mā ma}{花|huā}。 — I'm giving Mum flowers.
{这些|zhè xiē}{花|huā}{真|zhēn}{漂亮|piào liang}！ — These flowers are lovely!

Without counting, no measure word is needed. (A bunch is {一|yí}{束|shù}{花|huā}, one flower
{一|yì}{朵|duǒ}{花|huā}: words beyond HSK 3.) The same character, with the same sound, is also a
verb, "to spend" (money or time): that's lesson 23.

## {准备|zhǔn bèi}: to prepare, to plan to

{准备|zhǔn bèi} + a noun is to prepare something, get it ready:

{妈妈|mā ma}{在|zài}{准备|zhǔn bèi}{晚饭|wǎn fàn}。 — Mum is getting dinner ready.
{你|nǐ}{准备|zhǔn bèi}{生日|shēng rì}{礼物|lǐ wù}{了|le}{吗|ma}？ — Have you got a birthday present ready? ({礼物|lǐ wù}: present, HSK 3)

{准备|zhǔn bèi} + a verb is to plan to, to be going to:

{我|wǒ}{准备|zhǔn bèi}{明年|míng nián}{去|qù}{中国|Zhōng guó}。 — I'm planning to go to China next year.

And as a set phrase, {准备|zhǔn bèi}{好|hǎo}{了|le}{吗|ma}？ is "Are you ready?" ({好|hǎo} after a
verb means "done properly": module 4.) Answer {准备|zhǔn bèi}{好|hǎo}{了|le}！ or just {好|hǎo}{了|le}！

## {啊|a}: warmth at the end of a sentence

{啊|a} at the end of a sentence adds feeling. It has no meaning you can translate, but speech
without it can sound flat:

| Use | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| agreeing warmly | {好|hǎo}{啊|a}！ | Sure! Great! |
| exclaiming | {这些|zhè xiē}{花|huā}{真|zhēn}{漂亮|piào liang}{啊|a}！ | These flowers are so lovely! |
| softening a question | {你|nǐ}{去|qù}{不|bu}{去|qù}{啊|a}？ | So are you coming? |
| confirming | {是|shì}{啊|a}。 | Yes, that's right. |

It's always neutral, *a*. After some sounds it blends with the syllable before and is written
differently: {呀|ya} (as in {好|hǎo}{呀|ya}) or {哇|wa}. They're the same particle; just recognise
them. The character 啊 is taught in lesson 14, so here it keeps its pinyin.

At the start of a sentence, {啊|à} or {啊|ā} is an exclamation of surprise ("Oh!"), with a tone.

## Characters
{=

| Character | Meaning | Pinyin | Radical | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 告 | tell, announce | gào | 口 | 7 | {告诉|gào su} |
| 诉 (traditional 訴) | tell, relate | sù (light in {告诉|gào su}) | 讠 | 7 | {告诉|gào su} |
| 快 | fast; glad | kuài | 忄 | 7 | {快乐|kuài lè}, {快|kuài} (fast, lesson 14) |
| 乐 (traditional 樂) | happy, joyful; music | lè (and yuè) | 丿 | 5 | {快乐|kuài lè}, {音乐|yīn yuè} (music, HSK 3) |
| 送 | give (a present); see off | sòng | 辶 | 9 | {送|sòng}, {送给|sòng gěi} |
| 花 | flower; spend | huā | 艹 | 7 | {花|huā} |
| 准 (traditional 準) | accurate, standard; allow | zhǔn | 冫 | 10 | {准备|zhǔn bèi} |
| 备 (traditional 備) | prepare, get ready | bèi | 夂 | 8 | {准备|zhǔn bèi} |

### New radical: 夂

夂 ({折文|zhé wén}, also called {冬字头|dōng zì tóu}, "the top of 冬"). Three strokes: a short
left-falling stroke, a stroke that goes across and then sweeps down to the left, and a long
right-falling stroke. It's usually explained as a drawing of a foot. You've seen its shape on top of 条 in
{面条儿|miàn tiáor}, and it's the radical of 备 here; two HSK 3 characters, 处 and 务, have it
too. In 备 it means nothing today; it's part of the form.

### How the characters are built

- 快: 忄 (heart) and 夬 (*guài*), which gives the sound. Its first meaning was "pleased, at ease":
  a feeling, hence the heart. "Fast" came later. Both meanings survive in {快乐|kuài lè} (happy)
  and {快|kuài} (fast).
- 乐: traditional 樂 is usually explained as a drawing of a musical instrument on a wooden stand (木 at the bottom). Music,
  *yuè*, was the first meaning; joy, *lè*, came from it. Simplified 乐 is based on the cursive
  handwritten form.
- 花: 艹 (plants) and 化 (*huà*) for the sound.
- 准: simplified Chinese writes two words with this character. Traditional script keeps them
  apart: 準 (standard, accurate, as in {准备|zhǔn bèi} → 準備) and 准 (to allow). So
  {准备|zhǔn bèi} switches to 準備 in traditional script.
- 备: traditional 備 has 亻 (person) on the left; the simplified form drops it and reshapes the
  right side as 夂 over 田.
- 告 has 口 (mouth) at the bottom: telling is done with the mouth. Read that as a memory aid:
  scholars disagree about what the top part first was.
- 诉 has 讠 (speech), like {说|shuō}, {话|huà} and {请|qǐng}.
- 送 has 辶 (movement), like {这|zhè}, {还|hái}, {过|guò} and {进|jìn}: you take something, or
  someone, somewhere.

Radical review: 讠 "speech" (诉 joins 说, 话, 语, 请, 谢 and more), 辶 "walking, movement" (送 joins
这, 还, 边, 过, 进, 远, 近) and 艹 "grass, plants" (花 joins 茶, 菜, 苹, 药).

### Stroke order

- 送: the top part first (two short dots, two horizontals, the left-falling and right-falling
  strokes), then 辶 last, as in every character with 辶: the dot, the bent stroke, and the long
  flat sweep under everything.
- 快 and 慢 (next lesson): 忄 is the left dot, then the right dot, then the long vertical.
- 乐: the short left-falling stroke at the top, then a vertical that turns right, then the long
  vertical with a hook, and last the two dots (left, then right).
- 告: the vertical comes before the long horizontal, because it stops on it; then 口.
- 准: 冫 is a dot and a rising stroke, both on the left; then the right side from the top.

```trace
告诉快乐
```

```trace
送花准备
```

=}

## Dialogue: a surprise

{大卫|Dà wèi} (大卫) and {王芳|Wáng Fāng} (王芳) plan a birthday for their friend
{安娜|Ān nà} (安娜).

```dialogue
# A surprise
王芳: {大卫|Dà wèi}，{下|xià}{个|gè}{星期|xīng qī}{三|sān}{是|shì}{安娜|Ān nà}{的|de}{生日|shēng rì}，{你|nǐ}{知道|zhī dào}{吗|ma}？
= David, next Wednesday is Anna's birthday. Did you know?
大卫: {不|bù}{知道|zhī dào}{啊|a}！{她|tā}{没|méi}{告诉|gào su}{我|wǒ}。
= No! She didn't tell me.
王芳: {我们|wǒ men}{给|gěi}{她|tā}{过|guò}{生日|shēng rì}{吧|ba}。
= Let's throw her a birthday party.
大卫: {好|hǎo}{啊|a}！{我们|wǒ men}{准备|zhǔn bèi}{什么|shén me}？
= Great! What shall we get ready?
王芳: {我|wǒ}{准备|zhǔn bèi}{晚饭|wǎn fàn}，{你|nǐ}{去|qù}{买|mǎi}{一|yí}{个|gè}{蛋糕|dàn gāo}。
= I'll make dinner, and you go and buy a cake.
大卫: {我|wǒ}{送|sòng}{她|tā}{什么|shén me}{呢|ne}？
= And what shall I give her?
王芳: {她|tā}{很|hěn}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{花|huā}，{你|nǐ}{送|sòng}{她|tā}{花|huā}{吧|ba}。{不要|bú yào}{告诉|gào su}{她|tā}！
= She loves flowers; give her flowers. Don't tell her!
大卫: {好|hǎo}，{我|wǒ}{不|bú}{告诉|gào su}{她|tā}。
= OK, I won't tell her.
大家: {安娜|Ān nà}，{生日快乐|shēng rì kuài lè}！
= Happy birthday, Anna!
安娜: {谢谢|xiè xie}{你们|nǐ men}！{这些|zhè xiē}{花|huā}{真|zhēn}{漂亮|piào liang}{啊|a}！
= Thank you, everyone! These flowers are so lovely!
```

{蛋糕|dàn gāo} is a cake (HSK 3). {大家|dà jiā} in the speaker's place means "everyone".

## Reading: an invitation

{艾米|Ài mǐ} (Amy, the classmate of lesson 01, who lives with her family near the school) writes in
the class chat group.

> {大家|dà jiā}{好|hǎo}！{这|zhè}{个|gè}{星期|xīng qī}{六|liù}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{生日|shēng rì}，{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{请|qǐng}{大家|dà jiā}{来|lái}{我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}。{我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{在|zài}{学校|xué xiào}{旁边|páng biān}，{三|sān}{号|hào}{楼|lóu}{五|wǔ}{楼|lóu}{五|wǔ}{零|líng}{二|èr}。{晚上|wǎn shang}{六|liù}{点|diǎn}{开始|kāi shǐ}。{我|wǒ}{妈妈|mā ma}{准备|zhǔn bèi}{饺子|jiǎo zi}，{我|wǒ}{准备|zhǔn bèi}{水果|shuǐ guǒ}{和|hé}{茶|chá}。{你们|nǐ men}{不用|bú yòng}{送|sòng}{我|wǒ}{东西|dōng xi}，{人|rén}{来|lái}{就|jiù}{好|hǎo}！{能|néng}{来|lái}{的|de}{同学|tóng xué}{请|qǐng}{告诉|gào su}{我|wǒ}。{艾米|Ài mǐ}

({开始|kāi shǐ}: to start, lesson 20. {不用|bú yòng}: there's no need to. {人|rén}{来|lái}{就|jiù}{好|hǎo}:
"just come, that's enough", a set phrase.)

1. What day is the party, and at what time?
2. Where exactly does Amy live?
3. What does she ask the guests to do?

<details>
<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. This Saturday, at six in the evening.
2. Next to the school: building 3, fifth floor, flat 502 ({三|sān}{号|hào}{楼|lóu} is "building
   number 3"; {五|wǔ}{楼|lóu} the fifth floor).
3. To tell her if they can come; they don't need to bring presents.

"Hello everyone! This Saturday is my birthday, and I'd like to invite you all to my place for a
meal. I live next to the school: building 3, fifth floor, 502. It starts at six in the evening.
My mum is making dumplings, and I'm getting fruit and tea ready. You don't need to give me
anything; just come! If you can make it, please let me know. Amy"
</details>

The address goes from big to small, like a date: building, floor, flat.

## Say it

```speak
{生日快乐|shēng rì kuài lè}！
= Happy birthday!
{祝|zhù}{你|nǐ}{生日快乐|shēng rì kuài lè}！
= Wishing you a happy birthday!
{你|nǐ}{的|de}{生日|shēng rì}{是|shì}{几|jǐ}{月|yuè}{几|jǐ}{号|hào}？
= When is your birthday?
{这|zhè}{是|shì}{送|sòng}{你|nǐ}{的|de}。
= This is for you.
{告诉|gào su}{我|wǒ}{吧|ba}！
= Go on, tell me!
{过年|guò nián}{好|hǎo}！
= Happy New Year!
```

## Pronunciation

- {生日|shēng rì}: *sh* and *r* are both made with the tongue tip curled back; *ri* is a buzzing
  *r*, not "ree". First tone, then a fall.
- {快乐|kuài lè}: two falling tones. Keep the *l* of {乐|lè} clear; the *e* is the back vowel of
  {喝|hē}.
- {告诉|gào su}: the second syllable is light, almost swallowed: *gào su*.
- {准备|zhǔn bèi}: *zh* with the tongue curled back; *un* after *zh* is *uen*. Third tone, then a
  fall: the third tone stays low.
- {送|sòng} ends in *-ng*, but its vowel is the *oo* of "book", not the *o* of English "song"; the
  tone falls. Compare {生|shēng} and {送|sòng}: *sh* curled back, *s* flat.
- {花|huā} is high and level; the *h* is breathier than English *h*, made further back.

## Common mistakes

- English order with {送|sòng}: ~~{我|wǒ}{送|sòng}{一|yì}{本|běn}{书|shū}{她|tā}~~. The person comes
  first: {我|wǒ}{送|sòng}{她|tā}{一|yì}{本|běn}{书|shū}.
- ~~{说|shuō}{我|wǒ}~~ for "tell me": {告诉|gào su}{我|wǒ}.
- {快乐|kuài lè} for today's mood: ~~{今天|jīn tiān}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{快乐|kuài lè}~~ isn't wrong but
  sounds like a diary or a song; {我|wǒ}{今天|jīn tiān}{很|hěn}{高兴|gāo xìng} is everyday speech.
- {过|guò} "celebrate" read *guo*: it's the main verb, fourth tone.
- {啊|a} said with a tone at the end of a sentence: it's light.

## Key points

- {生日快乐|shēng rì kuài lè}！ {祝|zhù}{你|nǐ}…: wishes take {快乐|kuài lè}; today's mood takes
  {高兴|gāo xìng}.
- {过|guò}: spend, celebrate ({过生日|guò shēng rì}, {过年|guò nián}); not the particle {过|guo}.
- Double objects: {送|sòng} / {告诉|gào su} + person + thing, like {给|gěi} and {问|wèn}.
- {送|sòng} is also "see off, take someone somewhere"; {花|huā} is a flower.
- {准备|zhǔn bèi} + noun (prepare) or + verb (plan to); {准备|zhǔn bèi}{好|hǎo}{了|le}{吗|ma}？
- {啊|a} adds warmth: {好|hǎo}{啊|a}！ {是|shì}{啊|a}。
- New radical: 夂 (a foot). Traditional: 訴, 樂, 準備.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Comparing: 比 and 最
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

So far you've described one thing at a time: {他|tā}{很|hěn}{高|gāo}, {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}{很|hěn}{贵|guì}.
This lesson lets you compare: "he's taller than me", "this one is a bit more expensive", "the
metro is the fastest". The key word is {比|bǐ} (than), with {最|zuì} (most) beside it. You'll also
learn the words people compare with most ({快|kuài} fast, {慢|màn} slow, {不错|bú cuò} pretty good,
{错|cuò} wrong, {坏|huài} bad or broken) and {跟|gēn}, a spoken way to say "with".

## A {比|bǐ} B + adjective

A **[[comparison sentence]]** puts {比|bǐ} and the thing compared with before the adjective:

| A | {比|bǐ} | B | Adjective |
|---|---|---|---|
| {哥哥|gē ge} | {比|bǐ} | {我|wǒ} | {高|gāo}。 |
| {今天|jīn tiān} | {比|bǐ} | {昨天|zuó tiān} | {冷|lěng}。 |
| {地铁|dì tiě} | {比|bǐ} | {公交车|gōng jiāo chē} | {快|kuài}。 |
| {这个|zhè ge} | {比|bǐ} | {那个|nà ge} | {贵|guì}。 |

My brother is taller than me. · Today is colder than yesterday. · The metro is faster than the
bus. · This one is more expensive than that one.

English changes the adjective ("tall" → "taller") or adds "more"; Chinese doesn't change anything.
{比|bǐ} + B sits before the adjective, just as {在|zài} + place sits before a verb.

*No {很|hěn} inside.* In a {比|bǐ} sentence the adjective stands alone. Don't put {很|hěn},
{非常|fēi cháng}, {真|zhēn} or {太|tài} before it:

~~{哥哥|gē ge}{比|bǐ}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{高|gāo}。~~ → {哥哥|gē ge}{比|bǐ}{我|wǒ}{高|gāo}。

This is the commonest mistake with {比|bǐ}, because English says "much taller" and HSK 1 taught
you to put {很|hěn} before adjectives. {很|hěn} gives an absolute degree ("tall"); {比|bǐ} already
does the work of comparing.

### How much more?

Say how big the difference is *after* the adjective:

{这个|zhè ge}{比|bǐ}{那个|nà ge}{贵|guì}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}。 — This one is a little more expensive than that one.
{哥哥|gē ge}{比|bǐ}{我|wǒ}{大|dà}{三|sān}{岁|suì}。 — My brother is three years older than me.
{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{比|bǐ}{那|nà}{件|jiàn}{便宜|pián yi}{五十|wǔ shí}{块|kuài}。 — This one is fifty yuan cheaper than that one.

For age, Chinese compares with {大|dà} (older) and {小|xiǎo} (younger), as in {多大|duō dà}. A
number + measure word after the adjective gives the exact difference. HSK 3 adds {多了|duō le}
and {得多|de duō} for "much more".

### Questions and the negative

Ask with {吗|ma}, or with a question word in the A or B slot:

{今天|jīn tiān}{比|bǐ}{昨天|zuó tiān}{热|rè}{吗|ma}？ — Is today hotter than yesterday?
{谁|shéi}{比|bǐ}{你|nǐ}{高|gāo}？ — Who is taller than you?

A negative with {不比|bù bǐ} exists, but it's used to contradict someone ("he's no taller than
you"): {他|tā}{不|bù}{比|bǐ}{你|nǐ}{高|gāo}。 The everyday "not as tall as" uses {没有|méi yǒu}
({他|tā}{没有|méi yǒu}{你|nǐ}{高|gāo}): you'll learn that in HSK 3. For now, compare the other way
round: {你|nǐ}{比|bǐ}{他|tā}{高|gāo}。

## {最|zuì}: the most

{最|zuì} (most) is an adverb, so it goes right before the adjective, or before a verb of feeling:

{我们|wǒ men}{家|jiā}{我|wǒ}{最|zuì}{高|gāo}。 — In our family I'm the tallest.
{哪个|nǎ ge}{最|zuì}{便宜|pián yi}？ — Which one is the cheapest?
{你|nǐ}{最|zuì}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{什么|shén me}{颜色|yán sè}？ — What's your favourite colour?

{最|zuì}{喜欢|xǐ huan} is how Chinese says "favourite": there's no separate word. {最|zuì}{好|hǎo} is
"best". Like {比|bǐ}, {最|zuì} takes no {很|hěn}: ~~{很|hěn}{最|zuì}{高|gāo}~~.

The group can come first, as a topic: {我们|wǒ men}{班|bān}… (in our class), {这|zhè}{三|sān}{个|gè}{里|lǐ}…
(of these three). ({班|bān}, a class, is lesson 16's word.)

## {快|kuài} and {慢|màn}: fast and slow

{地铁|dì tiě}{很|hěn}{快|kuài}。 — The metro is fast.
{他|tā}{走路|zǒu lù}{很|hěn}{慢|màn}。 — He walks slowly.
{走路|zǒu lù}{比|bǐ}{坐|zuò}{车|chē}{慢|màn}。 — Walking is slower than going by car.

The second sentence is a topic-comment sentence (module 1): "him, walking is slow". Chinese often
says how someone does something this way; module 4 adds another pattern.

{快|kuài} can also go before a verb, meaning "quick(ly)": {快|kuài}{来|lái}！ (Come quick!),
{快|kuài}{走|zǒu}{吧|ba} (Let's get going). {快|kuài}{点儿|diǎnr}！ is "Hurry up!"

{慢|màn} gives two polite phrases:
- {慢慢|màn màn}{吃|chī} / {慢慢|màn màn}{说|shuō}: "take your time (eating / talking)", with the
  adjective doubled for a gentle, vivid tone (module 1).
- {慢|màn}{走|zǒu}！: said by a host to a guest who is leaving: "take care", literally "walk slowly".

When you don't follow someone: {请|qǐng}{慢|màn}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}{说|shuō}。 (Please speak a bit more
slowly.)

## Good and bad: {不错|bú cuò}, {错|cuò}, {坏|huài}

{错|cuò} is "wrong", the opposite of {对|duì} (right):

{你|nǐ}{错|cuò}{了|le}。 — You're wrong. / You've got it wrong.
{对|duì}{不|bu}{对|duì}？——{不|bú}{对|duì}，{错|cuò}{了|le}。 — Is that right? — No, it's wrong.

{不错|bú cuò} looks like "not wrong", but it's praise: "pretty good, not bad at all". It's one
of the commonest compliments:

{这个|zhè ge}{饭店|fàn diàn}{不错|bú cuò}。 — This restaurant is pretty good.
{你|nǐ}{的|de}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{很|hěn}{不错|bú cuò}！ — Your Chinese is really good!

{不|bù} is said *bú* here, rising before the fourth tone of {错|cuò}, and the course writes it that way.

{坏|huài} is "bad", the opposite of {好|hǎo}, and "broken, gone off" with {了|le} (a change):

{他|tā}{不|bú}{是|shì}{坏|huài}{人|rén}。 — He isn't a bad person.
{我|wǒ}{的|de}{手机|shǒu jī}{坏|huài}{了|le}。 — My phone has broken.

## {跟|gēn}: with

{跟|gēn} + person, before the verb, is "with" in speech:

{我|wǒ}{跟|gēn}{妈妈|mā ma}{去|qù}{超市|chāo shì}。 — I'm going to the supermarket with Mum.
{你|nǐ}{跟|gēn}{谁|shéi}{去|qù}？ — Who are you going with?
{我|wǒ}{跟|gēn}{朋友|péng you}{一起|yì qǐ}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}。 — I'm eating with friends.

{一起|yì qǐ} (together) is lesson 20's word; {跟|gēn}…{一起|yì qǐ} is the full form of "with"
and very common. {和|hé} (HSK 1) works the same way here; {跟|gēn} is a little more spoken.

{跟|gēn} has two more everyday uses:
- {跟|gēn} + person + {说|shuō}: to tell someone, to talk to them: {你|nǐ}{跟|gēn}{他|tā}{说|shuō}{吧|ba}。
  (You tell him.) {我|wǒ}{跟|gēn}{你|nǐ}{说|shuō}… ("Listen, let me tell you…")
- "to follow": {跟|gēn}{我|wǒ}{来|lái}。 (Come with me / This way.) {跟|gēn}{我|wǒ}{读|dú}。 (Repeat
  after me: a classroom instruction.)

HSK 3 adds {跟|gēn}…{一样|yí yàng} (the same as…).

## Characters
{=

| Character | Meaning | Pinyin | Radical | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 啊 | (particle of feeling) | a | 口 | 10 | {啊|a} (lesson 13) |
| 比 ✎ | compare; than | bǐ | 比 | 4 | {比|bǐ}, {比较|bǐ jiào} (fairly, HSK 3) |
| 跟 | heel; follow; with | gēn | 足 | 13 | {跟|gēn} |
| 最 | most | zuì | 曰 | 12 | {最|zuì}, {最好|zuì hǎo} (best) |
| 慢 | slow | màn | 忄 | 14 | {慢|màn}, {慢慢|màn màn} |
| 错 (traditional 錯) | wrong; mistake | cuò | 钅 | 13 | {错|cuò}, {不错|bú cuò} |
| 坏 (traditional 壞) | bad; broken | huài | 土 | 7 | {坏|huài} |

- 比 shows two people side by side, both facing right: a picture of comparing one with the
  other. It's its own radical. It's one of the handwriting characters.
- 跟 has the foot radical 足 on the left (lesson 07: {路|lù}): its first meaning was the heel,
  and "follow" (walk at someone's heels) came from it. 艮 (*gěn*) on the right gives the sound.
- 最 is 曰 (a radical meaning "say", wider than 日) over 取 (*qǔ*, take). The table follows
  Make Me a Hanzi; many dictionaries file 最 under 日.
- 慢 and 快 (lesson 13) are opposites with the same radical, 忄 (heart): 曼 (*màn*) gives 慢 its
  sound.
- 错 has 钅 (metal) and 昔 (*xī*); its oldest sense was inlaying or plating metal, a long way from "wrong".
- 坏: traditional 壞 is a very different, complex form; simplified 坏 is 土 (earth) + 不 (not).
  Think of it as "not sound ground" (a memory aid, not the history).
- 啊: 口 (mouth: a sound word) + 阿 (*ā*), which gives the sound.

Radical review: 忄 "heart" (standing heart, the side form of 心): 忙 (HSK 1), 快, 慢. 钅 "metal"
(the side form of 金): 钟, 钱, 铁 (lesson 08), 错. 足 "foot" on the left: 路, 跟; next come 跑, 踢,
跳 (module 4).

### Stroke order

- 比 (write it by hand): the short horizontal first, then the vertical that turns up to the right
  (one stroke). Then the right half: the short left-falling stroke and, last, the vertical that
  bends right and ends with a hook up. Don't write both verticals first.
- 最: 曰 on top. Underneath, the long horizontal comes first; then the two verticals and two
  short horizontals of 耳 and its rising stroke; then 又 on the right.
- 跟: on the left, 足 becomes narrow: 口, then a short vertical and horizontal, and the bottom
  becomes a vertical with a rising stroke. Then 艮.
- 坏: 土 on the left ends with a rising stroke instead of a long horizontal; then 不.

```trace
啊比跟最
```

```trace
慢错坏
```

Write it: 比 is one of the characters to know by hand. Write it three times on paper or the pad
from memory, then check its four strokes against the pad.

=}

## Dialogue: a new phone

{安娜|Ān nà} (安娜) goes phone shopping with {李明|Lǐ Míng} (李明).

```dialogue
# A new phone
安娜: {我|wǒ}{的|de}{手机|shǒu jī}{坏|huài}{了|le}，{你|nǐ}{跟|gēn}{我|wǒ}{去|qù}{买|mǎi}{一|yí}{个|gè}{新|xīn}{的|de}{吧|ba}。
= My phone's broken. Come with me to buy a new one.
李明: {好|hǎo}{啊|a}。{你|nǐ}{看|kàn}，{这个|zhè ge}{怎么样|zěn me yàng}？
= Sure. Look, how about this one?
安娜: {不错|bú cuò}。{那个|nà ge}{呢|ne}？
= Not bad. And that one?
李明: {那个|nà ge}{比|bǐ}{这个|zhè ge}{大|dà}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}，{也|yě}{比|bǐ}{这个|zhè ge}{快|kuài}。
= That one's a bit bigger than this one, and faster too.
安娜: {哪个|nǎ ge}{贵|guì}？
= Which one is more expensive?
李明: {大|dà}{的|de}{比|bǐ}{小|xiǎo}{的|de}{贵|guì}{五百|wǔ bǎi}{块|kuài}。
= The big one is five hundred yuan more than the small one.
安娜: {太|tài}{贵|guì}{了|le}！{这|zhè}{里|lǐ}{哪个|nǎ ge}{最|zuì}{便宜|pián yi}？
= That's too expensive! Which is the cheapest one here?
李明: {左边|zuǒ bian}{那个|nà ge}{最|zuì}{便宜|pián yi}，{但|dàn}{很|hěn}{慢|màn}。
= The one on the left is the cheapest, but it's slow.
安娜: {慢|màn}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}{没关系|méi guān xi}。{那|nà}{我|wǒ}{买|mǎi}{左边|zuǒ bian}{那个|nà ge}{吧|ba}，{不|bú}{贵|guì}，{也|yě}{不|bú}{错|cuò}。
= A bit slow doesn't matter. Then I'll take the one on the left: it's not expensive, and it's not bad.
```

Notice {新|xīn}{的|de}, {大|dà}{的|de}, {小|xiǎo}{的|de}: adjective + {的|de} stands for a noun ("the big
one"), as you learned with colours in lesson 03. {慢|màn}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}{没关系|méi guān xi}: the familiar
{没关系|méi guān xi} (it doesn't matter) with a subject in front, "a bit slow is fine".

## Reading: my family

> {我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{有|yǒu}{五|wǔ}{口|kǒu}{人|rén}：{爸爸|bà ba}、{妈妈|mā ma}、{哥哥|gē ge}、{妹妹|mèi mei}{和|hé}{我|wǒ}。{哥哥|gē ge}{比|bǐ}{我|wǒ}{大|dà}{三|sān}{岁|suì}，{也|yě}{比|bǐ}{我|wǒ}{高|gāo}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}。{爸爸|bà ba}{最|zuì}{高|gāo}，{妹妹|mèi mei}{最|zuì}{小|xiǎo}，{今年|jīn nián}{八|bā}{岁|suì}。{妹妹|mèi mei}{说话|shuō huà}{最|zuì}{快|kuài}，{爸爸|bà ba}{说话|shuō huà}{最|zuì}{慢|màn}。{我们|wǒ men}{都|dōu}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{吃|chī}{妈妈|mā ma}{做|zuò}{的|de}{饭|fàn}。{妈妈|mā ma}{说|shuō}{饭店|fàn diàn}{的|de}{菜|cài}{比|bǐ}{她|tā}{做|zuò}{的|de}{好吃|hǎo chī}，{我|wǒ}{觉得|jué de}{她|tā}{错|cuò}{了|le}！

1. How much older is the writer's brother?
2. Who in the family talks the most slowly?
3. What does the writer think about Mum's opinion?

<details>
<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. Three years ({比|bǐ}{我|wǒ}{大|dà}{三|sān}{岁|suì}).
2. Dad ({爸爸|bà ba}{说话|shuō huà}{最|zuì}{慢|màn}).
3. That she's wrong: the writer thinks Mum's cooking is better than the restaurant's.

"There are five of us in my family: Dad, Mum, my older brother, my younger sister and me. My
brother is three years older than me, and a little taller. Dad is the tallest; my sister is the
youngest, eight this year. My sister talks the fastest and Dad the slowest. We all love Mum's
cooking. Mum says restaurant food is tastier than hers, but I think she's wrong!"
</details>

## Say it

```speak
{他|tā}{比|bǐ}{我|wǒ}{高|gāo}。
= He's taller than me.
{这个|zhè ge}{比|bǐ}{那个|nà ge}{贵|guì}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}。
= This one is a bit more expensive than that one.
{哪个|nǎ ge}{最|zuì}{好|hǎo}？
= Which one is the best?
{你|nǐ}{的|de}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{很|hěn}{不错|bú cuò}！
= Your Chinese is really good!
{你|nǐ}{跟|gēn}{我|wǒ}{来|lái}。
= Come with me.
{慢|màn}{走|zǒu}！
= Take care! (to a guest leaving)
```

## Pronunciation

- {比|bǐ}: a low dipping tone. In {比|bǐ}{我|wǒ} two third tones meet, so {比|bǐ} rises: *bí wǒ*.
- {最|zuì}: spelled *zui*, said *zuei*, with the tone mark on the *i*. *z* is like "ds" in "kids".
- {错|cuò}: *c* is "ts" with a puff of air. {不错|bú cuò}: *bú* rises before the fourth tone.
- {快|kuài} and {坏|huài} rhyme and both fall: keep *k* (a puff of air) and *h* (breathy) apart.
- {慢|màn} falls; {跟|gēn} is high and level, with *-en* like the end of "taken".

## Common mistakes

- {很|hěn} inside a {比|bǐ} sentence: ~~{他|tā}{比|bǐ}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{高|gāo}~~ → {他|tā}{比|bǐ}{我|wǒ}{高|gāo}.
- The difference before the adjective: ~~{他|tā}{比|bǐ}{我|wǒ}{三|sān}{岁|suì}{大|dà}~~ →
  {他|tā}{比|bǐ}{我|wǒ}{大|dà}{三|sān}{岁|suì}.
- {比|bǐ} after the adjective, English-style: ~~{他|tā}{高|gāo}{比|bǐ}{我|wǒ}~~.
- For people's ages, compare with {大|dà} / {小|xiǎo}: {他|tā}{比|bǐ}{我|wǒ}{大|dà}. ({老|lǎo}, old, is for elderly
  people and old things.)
- Taking {不错|bú cuò} as faint praise: it's a real compliment.
- Writing 比 with both verticals first: horizontal, vertical-rise, left-falling, then the hook.

## Key points

- A {比|bǐ} B + adjective (+ {一点儿|yì diǎnr} / number + measure word); no {很|hěn} or {非常|fēi cháng} inside.
- {最|zuì} + adjective or verb of liking: {最|zuì}{贵|guì}, {最|zuì}{喜欢|xǐ huan} (favourite).
- {快|kuài} / {慢|màn}; {快|kuài}{来|lái}！ {慢慢|màn màn}{说|shuō}, {慢|màn}{走|zǒu}！
- {错|cuò} wrong, {不错|bú cuò} pretty good, {坏|huài} bad, broken ({坏|huài}{了|le}).
- {跟|gēn} + person: with ({跟|gēn}…{一起|yì qǐ}); {跟|gēn}…{说|shuō}; {跟|gēn}{我|wǒ}{来|lái}.

lessons.title: Why? 为什么, 虽然…但是
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

In lesson 05 you gave reasons with {因为|yīn wèi}…{所以|suǒ yǐ}. This lesson asks for them:
{为什么|wèi shén me} (why). Then it adds the other half of explaining yourself, "although…, (but)…"
with {虽然|suī rán}…{但是|dàn shì}, and three set phrases built on {意思|yì si} (meaning):
{有意思|yǒu yì si} (interesting), {没意思|méi yì si} (boring) and {不好意思|bù hǎo yì si}, the
everyday "sorry" and "excuse me" that you'll hear many times a day in China.

## {为什么|wèi shén me}: why

{为什么|wèi shén me} goes where most adverbs go: after the subject, before the verb. It can also
open the sentence.

{你|nǐ}{为什么|wèi shén me}{学|xué}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}？ — Why are you learning Chinese?
{他|tā}{为什么|wèi shén me}{不|bù}{来|lái}？ — Why isn't he coming?
{为什么|wèi shén me}{你|nǐ}{不|bú}{告诉|gào su}{我|wǒ}？ — Why didn't you tell me? / Why won't you tell me?

Answer with {因为|yīn wèi} (because), and add {所以|suǒ yǐ} if you repeat the result:

{你|nǐ}{为什么|wèi shén me}{没|méi}{去|qù}{上课|shàng kè}？——{因为|yīn wèi}{我|wǒ}{生病|shēng bìng}{了|le}。
— Why didn't you go to class? — Because I was ill.

{为|wèi} means "for", so {为什么|wèi shén me} is literally "for what". On its own,
{为什么|wèi shén me}？ is a complete question: "Why?"

{为什么|wèi shén me} or {怎么|zěn me}? {怎么|zěn me} (HSK 1, "how") can also ask "how come",
with surprise: {你|nǐ}{怎么|zěn me}{没|méi}{来|lái}？ (How come you didn't come?). {为什么|wèi shén me}
is the neutral question that really wants a reason.

## {虽然|suī rán}…{但是|dàn shì}: although

To say that something is true and yet something else is true, Chinese uses both
{虽然|suī rán} (although) and {但是|dàn shì} (but), one in each half. This is **[[concession]]**:

{虽然|suī rán}{很|hěn}{累|lèi}，{但是|dàn shì}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{高兴|gāo xìng}。 — Although I'm tired, I'm happy.
{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}{虽然|suī rán}{很|hěn}{贵|guì}，{但是|dàn shì}{很|hěn}{漂亮|piào liang}。 — This piece of clothing is expensive, but it's beautiful.
{虽然|suī rán}{他|tā}{是|shì}{美国|Měi guó}{人|rén}，{但是|dàn shì}{他|tā}{很|hěn}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{吃|chī}{中国|Zhōng guó}{菜|cài}。 — Although he's American, he loves Chinese food.

({美国|Měi guó}: the United States.)

The rules:
- *Both words, usually.* English uses "although" or "but", never both. Chinese normally uses
  both. {但是|dàn shì} alone is fine (like English "but"); {虽然|suī rán} alone sounds unfinished.
- *{但是|dàn shì} starts the second half*, before its subject: {但是|dàn shì}{我|wǒ}…, never
  ~~{我|wǒ}{但是|dàn shì}…~~
- *{虽然|suī rán} goes before or after the subject* of the first half: {虽然|suī rán}{他|tā}{很|hěn}{忙|máng}
  or {他|tā}{虽然|suī rán}{很|hěn}{忙|máng}. When both halves have the same subject, either place is fine;
  when the subjects differ, {虽然|suī rán} goes before the subject of the first half.

Compare the three ways of linking you now know:

| Link | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {因为|yīn wèi}…{所以|suǒ yǐ}… | because…, so… | {因为|yīn wèi}{下雨|xià yǔ}{了|le}，{所以|suǒ yǐ}{我|wǒ}{没|méi}{去|qù}。 |
| {虽然|suī rán}…{但是|dàn shì}… | although…, (but)… | {虽然|suī rán}{下雨|xià yǔ}{了|le}，{但是|dàn shì}{我|wǒ}{去|qù}{了|le}。 |
| …，{但是|dàn shì}… | …, but… | {我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{去|qù}，{但是|dàn shì}{没有|méi yǒu}{时间|shí jiān}。 |

It rained, so I didn't go. · Although it rained, I went. · I'd like to go, but I haven't got time.

### {但|dàn} and {但是|dàn shì}

{但|dàn} is the short form of {但是|dàn shì}, with the same meaning. You'll see it in writing and
hear it in quick speech, especially between short phrases: {很|hěn}{小|xiǎo}，{但|dàn}{很|hěn}{舒服|shū fu}
(small but comfortable). {但是|dàn shì} is the safe choice in speech; both go with {虽然|suī rán}.

## {意思|yì si}: meaning

{意思|yì si} is the meaning of a word or of what someone says. The question every learner needs:

{这个|zhè ge}{字|zì}{是|shì}{什么|shén me}{意思|yì si}？ — What does this character mean?
“{慢走|màn zǒu}”{是|shì}{什么|shén me}{意思|yì si}？ — What does "màn zǒu" mean?
{我|wǒ}{的|de}{意思|yì si}{是|shì}…… — What I mean is…

Careful with {你|nǐ}{是|shì}{什么|shén me}{意思|yì si}？ said to a person: like "What do you mean
by that?", it can sound annoyed.

## {有意思|yǒu yì si} and {没意思|méi yì si}

{有意思|yǒu yì si} is "having meaning", so: interesting, fun. {没意思|méi yì si} is the opposite:
boring, no fun. They work like adjectives and take degree words in front:

{这|zhè}{本|běn}{书|shū}{很|hěn}{有意思|yǒu yì si}。 — This book is really interesting.
{北京|Běi jīng}{太|tài}{有意思|yǒu yì si}{了|le}！ — Beijing is so much fun!
{这个|zhè ge}{电影|diàn yǐng}{没意思|méi yì si}。 — This film is boring.

The negative is {没意思|méi yì si}, never ~~{不|bù}{有意思|yǒu yì si}~~: {有|yǒu} is negated with
{没|méi}, as you learned in HSK 1. {没|méi}{什么|shén me}{意思|yì si} (not much fun) is a softer way to
say it.

## {不好意思|bù hǎo yì si}: sorry, excuse me

{不好意思|bù hǎo yì si} literally says "not good meaning", but it's a feeling: a little
embarrassed, awkward about bothering someone. It's the everyday light apology and "excuse me":

| Situation | What you say |
|---|---|
| you're a bit late | {不好意思|bù hǎo yì si}，{我|wǒ}{来|lái}{晚|wǎn}{了|le}。 Sorry I'm late. |
| you stop a stranger to ask | {不好意思|bù hǎo yì si}，{请问|qǐng wèn}{地铁|dì tiě}{站|zhàn}{在|zài}{哪儿|nǎr}？ Excuse me, where's the metro station? |
| you bump into someone, or need to get past | {不好意思|bù hǎo yì si}！ Sorry! / Excuse me! |
| you ask a favour | {不好意思|bù hǎo yì si}，{你|nǐ}{能|néng}{等|děng}{我|wǒ}{一下|yí xià}{吗|ma}？ Sorry, could you wait a moment for me? |
| someone praises you or gives you a present | {不好意思|bù hǎo yì si}…… I'm embarrassed… / You shouldn't have… |

({等|děng}, to wait, is lesson 20's word.)

{对不起|duì bu qǐ} (from the pinyin course) is a real apology, for something you did wrong:
breaking something, forgetting an appointment, hurting someone. {不好意思|bù hǎo yì si} is
lighter and far more frequent. For small things, {对不起|duì bu qǐ} can sound too heavy.

It's also an adjective, "embarrassed, shy": {他|tā}{很|hěn}{不好意思|bù hǎo yì si} (he felt
embarrassed), {我|wǒ}{不好意思|bù hǎo yì si}{问|wèn} (I'm too shy to ask).

The answer to both is {没关系|méi guān xi} or {没事|méi shì}.

## Characters
{=

| Character | Meaning | Pinyin | Radical | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 但 | but; only | dàn | 亻 | 7 | {但|dàn}, {但是|dàn shì} |
| 虽 (traditional 雖) | although | suī | 虫 | 9 | {虽然|suī rán} |
| 然 | so, like that | rán | 灬 | 12 | {虽然|suī rán}, {然后|rán hòu} (then, HSK 3) |
| 意 | meaning, idea, wish | yì | 心 | 13 | {意思|yì si}, {有意思|yǒu yì si}, {不好意思|bù hǎo yì si} |
| 思 | think | sī (light in {意思|yì si}) | 心 | 9 | {意思|yì si}, {没意思|méi yì si} |

- 但: 亻 (person) and 旦 (*dàn*, dawn), which gives the sound.
- 虽: traditional 雖 has 隹 on the right. Its oldest meaning was a kind of lizard, hence 虫
  ("insect, creature"); the word was borrowed for "although" because of its sound. Simplified
  虽 keeps 口 over 虫.
- 然: the top left is a form of 肉 (meat), the top right 犬 (dog), and 灬 is fire. Its first
  meaning was "to burn"; when 然 was borrowed for "so, like that", a new character with an extra
  火 was made for "burn": 燃 (*rán*, beyond HSK 3).
- 意: 音 (sound, HSK 3's {音乐|yīn yuè}) over 心 (heart). The old explanation is "what the heart
  says": an idea, an intention, a meaning.
- 思: 心 (heart) under a part that looks like 田 (field) but was once 囟, the soft top of a baby's
  skull. Thinking was placed in the head and the heart.

Radical review: 亻 "person" (但 joins 你, 他, 们, 作, 住, 休, 位, 体 and more); 心 "heart" at the bottom
(意 and 思 join 您, 想, 怎, 息); 灬 "fire" at the bottom (然 joins 点 and 热).

### Stroke order

- 意 and 思: 心 at the bottom is written last: the left dot, the long curved stroke with its hook,
  then the two dots.
- 虽: 口 first, then 虫: the small box (a vertical, a turning stroke, a horizontal), the long
  vertical through it, the rising stroke at the bottom and the dot on the right.
- 然: the top-left part first (four strokes, like 夕 with an extra dot), then 犬 with its dot last,
  then the four dots of 灬 from left to right.

```trace
但虽然意思
```

=}

## Dialogue: late for the film

{李明|Lǐ Míng} (李明) is meeting {安娜|Ān nà} (安娜) at the cinema.

```dialogue
# Late for the film
李明: {不好意思|bù hǎo yì si}，{我|wǒ}{来|lái}{晚|wǎn}{了|le}！
= Sorry I'm late!
安娜: {没关系|méi guān xi}。{你|nǐ}{为什么|wèi shén me}{来|lái}{晚|wǎn}{了|le}？
= That's OK. Why were you late?
李明: {因为|yīn wèi}{地铁|dì tiě}{上|shàng}{人|rén}{太|tài}{多|duō}{了|le}，{我|wǒ}{没|méi}{上去|shàng qù}。
= Because the metro was too crowded; I couldn't get on.
安娜: {你|nǐ}{为什么|wèi shén me}{不|bù}{打车|dǎ chē}？
= Why didn't you take a taxi?
李明: {虽然|suī rán}{打车|dǎ chē}{比|bǐ}{坐|zuò}{地铁|dì tiě}{快|kuài}，{但是|dàn shì}{太|tài}{贵|guì}{了|le}。
= Although a taxi is faster than the metro, it's too expensive.
安娜: {好|hǎo}{吧|ba}。{我们|wǒ men}{快|kuài}{进去|jìn qù}{吧|ba}。
= Fair enough. Let's go in quickly.
```

After the film:

```dialogue
# After the film
安娜: {这个|zhè ge}{电影|diàn yǐng}{真|zhēn}{有意思|yǒu yì si}！{你|nǐ}{觉得|jué de}{呢|ne}？
= That film was really good! What did you think?
李明: {虽然|suī rán}{很|hěn}{漂亮|piào liang}，{但|dàn}{太|tài}{长|cháng}{了|le}，{有点儿|yǒu diǎnr}{没意思|méi yì si}。
= It was beautiful, but too long, a bit boring.
安娜: {最后|zuì hòu}{那个|nà ge}{人|rén}{说|shuō}“{慢走|màn zǒu}”，{是|shì}{什么|shén me}{意思|yì si}？
= At the end someone said "màn zǒu": what does it mean?
李明: {意思|yì si}{是|shì}“take care”，{是|shì}{送|sòng}{客人|kè rén}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}{说|shuō}{的|de}。
= It means "take care". You say it when you see a guest out.
```

Notes: {有点儿|yǒu diǎnr} (a bit) goes before {没意思|méi yì si} as before any adjective.
{最后|zuì hòu} is "at the end, last" (HSK 3: {最|zuì} + {后|hòu}). {客人|kè rén} is a guest (HSK 3), and
{送|sòng} here is "to see off", lesson 13's second meaning.

## Reading: a message to the teacher

> {王|Wáng}{老师|lǎo shī}，{您|nín}{好|hǎo}！{不好意思|bù hǎo yì si}，{今天|jīn tiān}{我|wǒ}{不|bù}{能|néng}{去|qù}{上课|shàng kè}{了|le}。{因为|yīn wèi}{我|wǒ}{昨天|zuó tiān}{晚上|wǎn shang}{生病|shēng bìng}{了|le}，{头|tóu}{很|hěn}{疼|téng}，{身体|shēn tǐ}{也|yě}{不|bù}{舒服|shū fu}。{虽然|suī rán}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{想|xiǎng}{去|qù}，{但是|dàn shì}{医生|yī shēng}{说|shuō}{我|wǒ}{要|yào}{在|zài}{家|jiā}{休息|xiū xi}{两|liǎng}{天|tiān}。{我|wǒ}{在|zài}{家|jiā}{也|yě}{会|huì}{看|kàn}{书|shū}{学习|xué xí}。{您|nín}{能|néng}{告诉|gào su}{我|wǒ}{明天|míng tiān}{的|de}{课|kè}{学|xué}{什么|shén me}{吗|ma}？{谢谢|xiè xie}{您|nín}！{大卫|Dà wèi}

1. Why can't David go to class?
2. What did the doctor say?
3. What does he ask the teacher?

<details>
<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. He fell ill last night: a headache, and he doesn't feel well.
2. That he should rest at home for two days.
3. To tell him what tomorrow's class will cover.

"Hello, Ms Wang (or Mr Wang)! I'm sorry, I can't come to class today. I fell ill last night: I've
got a headache and I don't feel well. Although I'd really like to come, the doctor says I should
rest at home for two days. I'll read and study at home too. Could you tell me what we'll study in tomorrow's class? Thank you!
David"
</details>

{老师|lǎo shī} doesn't say whether the teacher is a man or a woman; the English needs to choose.
The message opens with {不好意思|bù hǎo yì si}: missing a class is a small thing to apologise for,
so the light phrase fits.

## Say it

```speak
{你|nǐ}{为什么|wèi shén me}{学|xué}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}？
= Why are you learning Chinese?
{这个|zhè ge}{字|zì}{是|shì}{什么|shén me}{意思|yì si}？
= What does this character mean?
{这|zhè}{本|běn}{书|shū}{很|hěn}{有意思|yǒu yì si}。
= This book is really interesting.
{不好意思|bù hǎo yì si}，{我|wǒ}{来|lái}{晚|wǎn}{了|le}。
= Sorry I'm late.
{虽然|suī rán}{很|hěn}{累|lèi}，{但是|dàn shì}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{高兴|gāo xìng}。
= Although I'm tired, I'm happy.
```

## Pronunciation

- {为什么|wèi shén me}: a fall, a rise, and a light *me*. Don't read {为|wèi} with a second tone
  here.
- {虽然|suī rán}: *sui* is said *suei*; *r* is the curled-back *r* of {日|rì}. A high level tone, then a rise.
- {意思|yì si}: the *si* is light and short, with the buzzing *-i* after *s* (not "see").
- {不好意思|bù hǎo yì si}: {不|bù} keeps its fourth tone before the third tone of {好|hǎo}.
  {有意思|yǒu yì si}: *yǒu* dips, then *yì* falls.
- {但是|dàn shì}: two falling tones; the *sh* is curled back.

## Common mistakes

- {虽然|suī rán} without {但是|dàn shì}: ~~{虽然|suī rán}{很|hěn}{累|lèi}，{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{高兴|gāo xìng}~~
  sounds unfinished. Add {但是|dàn shì}.
- {但是|dàn shì} after the subject: ~~{我|wǒ}{但是|dàn shì}{没有|méi yǒu}{时间|shí jiān}~~ →
  {但是|dàn shì}{我|wǒ}{没有|méi yǒu}{时间|shí jiān}.
- ~~{不|bù}{有意思|yǒu yì si}~~ → {没意思|méi yì si}.
- {对不起|duì bu qǐ} for every small thing: for bumping into someone or being five minutes late,
  {不好意思|bù hǎo yì si} is the natural word.
- {为什么|wèi shén me} at the end, English-style: ~~{你|nǐ}{学|xué}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{为什么|wèi shén me}~~ →
  {你|nǐ}{为什么|wèi shén me}{学|xué}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}？

## Key points

- {为什么|wèi shén me} + verb: why; answer with {因为|yīn wèi}. {怎么|zěn me} can mean "how come".
- {虽然|suī rán}…，{但是|dàn shì}…: use both halves; {但是|dàn shì} starts the second half;
  {但|dàn} is its short form.
- {意思|yì si}: meaning. …{是|shì}{什么|shén me}{意思|yì si}？
- {有意思|yǒu yì si} interesting, fun; {没意思|méi yì si} boring.
- {不好意思|bù hǎo yì si}: light sorry, excuse me, embarrassed; {对不起|duì bu qǐ}: a real apology.
