> {妈妈|mā ma}：{我|wǒ}{和|hé}{同学|tóng xué}{去|qù}{打|dǎ}{篮球|lán qiú}{了|le}，{晚上|wǎn shang}{七|qī}{点|diǎn}{回来|huí lái}。{别|bié}{等|děng}{我|wǒ}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}，{我|wǒ}{在|zài}{外面|wài miàn}{吃|chī}。{小明|Xiǎo Míng}

Check yourself: will Xiaoming eat at home? (No: {我|wǒ}{在|zài}{外面|wài miàn}{吃|chī}, "I'll eat out".) When will he be back?
(At seven in the evening.)

## A group chat

Chat messages are short and full of {吧|ba}, {啊|a} and {呢|ne}, the particles of speech. A message that answers
another one often has no subject at all.

> **{李明|Lǐ Míng}**：{大家|dà jiā}{好|hǎo}！{这个|zhè ge}{星期|xīng qī}{六|liù}{是|shì}{王芳|Wáng Fāng}{的|de}{生日|shēng rì}，{我们|wǒ men}{准备|zhǔn bèi}{给|gěi}{她|tā}{过|guò}{生日|shēng rì}，{大家|dà jiā}{有|yǒu}{时间|shí jiān}{吗|ma}？
>
> **{安娜|Ān nà}**：{有|yǒu}！{太|tài}{好|hǎo}{了|le}。{在|zài}{哪儿|nǎr}？{几|jǐ}{点|diǎn}？
>
> **{李明|Lǐ Míng}**：{晚上|wǎn shang}{六|liù}{点|diǎn}{半|bàn}，{在|zài}{学校|xué xiào}{旁边|páng biān}{的|de}{饭馆|fàn guǎn}。{从|cóng}{学校|xué xiào}{往|wǎng}{右|yòu}{走|zǒu}{五|wǔ}{分钟|fēn zhōng}{就|jiù}{到|dào}{了|le}。
>
> **{大卫|Dà wèi}**：{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{送|sòng}{她|tā}{花|huā}，{你们|nǐ men}{觉得|jué de}{怎么样|zěn me yàng}？
>
> **{安娜|Ān nà}**：{送|sòng}{花|huā}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}！{我们|wǒ men}{还是|hái shi}{一起|yì qǐ}{买|mǎi}{吧|ba}，{我|wǒ}{知道|zhī dào}{一|yí}{个|gè}{花|huā}{店|diàn}，{离|lí}{学校|xué xiào}{很|hěn}{近|jìn}。
>
> **{李明|Lǐ Míng}**：{好|hǎo}{啊|a}。{别|bié}{告诉|gào su}{王芳|Wáng Fāng}！
>
> **{大卫|Dà wèi}**：{收到|shōu dào}。{星期|xīng qī}{六|liù}{见|jiàn}！

{收到|shōu dào} (received) is an HSK 3 word; in a chat, {收到|shōu dào}！ means "Got it!". {花|huā}{店|diàn} is
{花|huā} (flower) + {店|diàn} (shop): a flower shop.

1. What is the dinner for, and when is it?
2. How do you get to the restaurant from the school?
3. What do Anna and David decide about the flowers?
4. What must nobody do?

<details>
<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. Wang Fang's birthday; this Saturday at half past six in the evening ({晚上|wǎn shang}{六|liù}{点|diǎn}{半|bàn}).
2. Walk to the right from the school for five minutes ({从|cóng}{学校|xué xiào}{往|wǎng}{右|yòu}{走|zǒu}{五|wǔ}{分钟|fēn zhōng}{就|jiù}{到|dào}{了|le}).
3. To buy them together, at a flower shop Anna knows near the school ({我们|wǒ men}{还是|hái shi}{一起|yì qǐ}{买|mǎi}{吧|ba}).
4. Tell Wang Fang ({别|bié}{告诉|gào su}{王芳|Wáng Fāng}！): it's a surprise.

Li Ming: Hi everyone! This Saturday is Wang Fang's birthday, and we're planning to celebrate it
for her. Are you all free?
Anna: Yes! Great. Where? What time?
Li Ming: Half past six in the evening, at the restaurant next to the school. From the school, go
right and you're there in five minutes.
David: I'd like to give her flowers. What do you think?
Anna: Flowers are a good idea! We'd better buy them together; I know a flower shop, it's close to
the school.
Li Ming: Good. Don't tell Wang Fang!
David: Got it. See you on Saturday!
</details>

The chat is about 125 characters; the longest reading texts at HSK 2 are about 200. Notice how much the
words of this course carry: {还是|hái shi}……{吧|ba} (lesson 26), {离|lí} and {往|wǎng} (lesson 07), {送|sòng} and {告诉|gào su} (lesson 13), {别|bié}
(lesson 21).

## A form

Forms ask for the same things everywhere: name, date of birth, phone number. You'll fill one in
yourself in lesson 29; here, read one.

> **{运动|yùn dòng}{班|bān}**
>
> | | |
> |---|---|
> | {姓名|xìng míng} | {安娜|Ān nà} |
> | {国籍|guó jí} | {美国|Měi guó} |
> | {生日|shēng rì} | 2008{年|nián}5{月|yuè}16{日|rì} |
> | {手机|shǒu jī} | 127 0000 2468 |
> | {爱好|ài hào} | {游泳|yóu yǒng}、{跑步|pǎo bù} |
> | {想|xiǎng}{学|xué} | {足球|zú qiú} |

{国籍|guó jí} (nationality) is a word you'll see only on forms. {美国|Měi guó} is the United States.
On a form, dates are written in full, year first, with {日|rì} for the day: 2008{年|nián}5{月|yuè}16{日|rì} is 16 May
2008. In speech you'd say {五|wǔ}{月|yuè}{十六|shí liù}{号|hào}.

Check yourself: what does Anna want to learn? (Football: {想|xiǎng}{学|xué}{足球|zú qiú}.) What does she already like
doing? (Swimming and running.)

## A timetable

> | {车次|chē cì} | {北京|Běi jīng} {开|kāi} | {上海|Shàng hǎi} {到|dào} |
> |---|---|---|
> | G101 | 07:00 | 11:30 |
> | G103 | 08:00 | 12:40 |
> | G105 | 10:00 | 14:30 |

{车次|chē cì} (train number) appears on every train ticket. {开|kāi} here means "leaves" and {到|dào}
"arrives". G101, G103 and G105 are real train numbers on the Beijing–Shanghai high-speed line, but
these times are made up for practice: check a real timetable before you travel.

Check yourself: which train do you take if you must be in Shanghai by one o'clock? (G101 or G103.)
Which one takes the longest? (G103: four hours forty minutes.)

## A menu

> **{咖啡馆|kā fēi guǎn}**
>
> | | {元|yuán} |
> |---|---|
> | {咖啡|kā fēi} | 25 |
> | {奶茶|nǎi chá} | 18 |
> | {红茶|hóng chá} / {绿茶|lǜ chá} | 15 |
> | {面包|miàn bāo} | 12 |
> | {每|měi}{天|tiān}{下午|xià wǔ}{三|sān}{点|diǎn}{到|dào}{五|wǔ}{点|diǎn}：{咖啡|kā fēi}{两|liǎng}{杯|bēi}40{元|yuán} | |

{咖啡馆|kā fēi guǎn} is a café: {咖啡|kā fēi} + {馆|guǎn} (as in {饭馆|fàn guǎn}). Prices are in {元|yuán}; you say {块|kuài} when you read them: 25{元|yuán} is
{二十五|èr shí wǔ}{块|kuài}. {两|liǎng}{杯|bēi} is "two cups": {杯|bēi} is the measure word for cups and glasses, from {杯子|bēi zi}.

Check yourself: two friends order two coffees at four in the afternoon. How much do they pay? (40
yuan: between three and five, two coffees cost 40 instead of 50.)

## Strategies for the reading questions

1. *Read the question first.* Decide what you're scanning for: a time, a place, a person, a
   number.
2. *Look at the shape.* A title in bold and a date at the bottom is a notice; names and colons on
   each line are a chat; two columns of words and numbers are a menu or a timetable.
3. *Don't stop at a new character.* Skip it, read on, and come back if the question needs it.
   Characters you know around it, or a radical inside it, often give enough.
4. *Read to the end of the sentence.* {别|bié}{忘|wàng}{了|le} is "don't forget", {还|hái}{没|méi}{开|kāi}{门|mén} "not open yet".
5. *Check numbers twice.* Is it {十|shí}{点|diǎn} or {四|sì}{点|diǎn}? {二十|èr shí}{多|duō} (twenty-something) or {十二|shí èr}?

## Common mistakes

- Answering from one word: {休息|xiū xi} on a shop's notice doesn't mean the staff are resting, it means
  the shop is closed.
- Reading {三|sān}{楼|lóu} as "three buildings": with a number in front, {楼|lóu} is the floor.
- Missing the negative: {别|bié}{等|děng}{我|wǒ} is "don't wait for me", the opposite of {等|děng}{我|wǒ}.
- Reading a date as month–day–year: Chinese order is always year, month, day.
- Reading every word slowly before looking at the question: with notices, skim first, then scan.

## Key points

- **[[Skimming]]** gives the type and the general idea; **[[scanning]]** finds the one fact the question
  asks for.
- Notices: {通知|tōng zhī} at the top, who and when at the bottom, {请|qǐng} / {别|bié} / {要|yào} for what to do.
- Messages and chats: the name of the person addressed first, short sentences, particles of speech.
- Forms: {姓名|xìng míng}, {生日|shēng rì}, {国籍|guó jí}, {手机|shǒu jī}; dates year–month–day with {日|rì}.
- Timetables and opening times: 24-hour clock, a dash for "from… to…".
- Menus: prices in {元|yuán}, read as {块|kuài}.

This lesson has no new words.

lessons.title: Listening and conversation
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

At HSK 1 people spoke slowly to you, in short sentences. At HSK 2 the listening texts are longer
(up to about 150 characters) and closer to normal speed: two people at a station, in a shop, on
the phone, making plans. This lesson is about getting the meaning from speech you can't hear
word by word: what to listen for, the question words that decide the answer, how numbers and times
sound, and what to say when you don't understand.

The dialogues here are for listening first. Press **Hide the words** on each one, play it, and
answer the questions under it; then show the words and play it again.

## How to listen

1. *Know what you're listening for.* Read the question and the choices before you listen. If the
   choices are times, listen for {点|diǎn} and {分|fēn}; if they're places, for {在|zài}, {去|qù} and {到|dào}; if they're
   people, for names and {谁|shéi}.
2. *Catch the key words, not every word.* At normal speed small words run together, and you won't
   hear each {的|de} and {了|le}. The nouns, verbs and numbers carry the meaning.
3. *Listen to the end.* The second speaker often changes the plan: {我们|wǒ men}{坐|zuò}{地铁|dì tiě}{吧|ba}。—{地铁|dì tiě}{太|tài}{慢|màn}{了|le}，{我们|wǒ men}{还是|hái shi}{打车|dǎ chē}{吧|ba}。
   The answer is the taxi.
4. *Listen for the turning words.* {不|bù}, {没|méi}, {别|bié}, {还|hái}{没|méi} and {已经|yǐ jīng} turn a sentence around; {但是|dàn shì} and {可是|kě shì}
   ({可是|kě shì}, but: HSK 3) bring a change; {还是|hái shi} offers a choice or a better plan; {因为|yīn wèi} gives
   the reason.
5. *Don't translate.* If you stop to put a sentence into English, you miss the next one. Picture
   what's happening: who is where, doing what.


## The question words that decide the answer

When the question is in the recording, its question word tells you what kind of answer to pick.

| You hear | It asks for | Listen for |
|---|---|---|
| {谁|shéi} | a person | a name, {老师|lǎo shī}, {妈妈|mā ma}, {我|wǒ}{朋友|péng you} |
| {什么|shén me}{时候|shí hou} / {几|jǐ}{点|diǎn} / {星期|xīng qī}{几|jǐ} / {几|jǐ}{号|hào} | a time | {点|diǎn}, {半|bàn}, {号|hào}, {星期|xīng qī}, {上午|shàng wǔ} / {下午|xià wǔ} |
| {在|zài}{哪儿|nǎr} / {去|qù}{哪儿|nǎr} | a place | {在|zài}, {到|dào}, {楼|lóu}, {门口|mén kǒu}, {旁边|páng biān} |
| {怎么|zěn me} + verb | how, by what means | {坐|zuò}{地铁|dì tiě}, {打车|dǎ chē}, {走路|zǒu lù} |
| {为什么|wèi shén me} | a reason | {因为|yīn wèi}……({所以|suǒ yǐ}) |
| {多少|duō shao} / {几|jǐ} + measure | a number | numbers, {块|kuài}, {个|gè}, {次|cì} |
| {怎么样|zěn me yàng} | an opinion | {不错|bú cuò}, {很|hěn}{好|hǎo}, {太|tài}……{了|le} |
| A {还是|hái shi} B | one of two | A or B, often in the reply |

{怎么|zěn me} and {怎么样|zěn me yàng} sound alike but ask different things: {你|nǐ}{怎么|zěn me}{去|qù}{机场|jī chǎng}？ asks how you get there
({打车|dǎ chē}{去|qù}), {机场|jī chǎng}{怎么样|zěn me yàng}？ what it's like ({很|hěn}{大|dà}).

## Numbers and times in speech

Numbers are where most listening points are lost. What to know:

- *{两|liǎng} or {二|èr}*: before a measure word it's {两|liǎng}: {两|liǎng}{个|gè}{人|rén}, {两|liǎng}{点|diǎn} (two o'clock), {两万|liǎng wàn} (20,000). Inside a
  number it's {二|èr}: {十二|shí èr}, {二十|èr shí}. At the start of a number, {两|liǎng} is usual before {百|bǎi}, {千|qiān} and {万|wàn}:
  {两百二十|liǎng bǎi èr shí} (220).
- *{一|yī} as yāo*: in phone numbers, room numbers and bus numbers, 1 is said *yāo* so it isn't confused
  with {七|qī}: 139 is *yāo sān jiǔ*, room 101 *yāo líng yāo*.
- *Big numbers are shortened*: {两万五千|liǎng wàn wǔ qiān} is often just {两万五|liǎng wàn wǔ} (25,000), and {三千八百|sān qiān bā bǎi} just {三千八|sān qiān bā}
  (3,800). The last unit is understood.
- *Approximate numbers* (lesson 22): {十|shí}{几|jǐ}{个|gè}{人|rén} (ten-odd people, between 11 and 19), {二十|èr shí}{多|duō}{块|kuài}
  (twenty-something yuan). When you hear {几|jǐ} or {多|duō} after a number, the exact figure isn't given.
- *Prices*: {二十八|èr shí bā}{块|kuài}{五|wǔ} is 28.50 yuan; the number after {块|kuài} is tenths of a yuan.
- *Times*: {三|sān}{点|diǎn}{半|bàn} (3:30), {九|jiǔ}{点|diǎn}{十|shí}{分|fēn} (9:10), {两|liǎng}{点|diǎn} (2:00, never {二|èr}{点|diǎn}). {半|bàn} can also be "half an hour":
  {一|yí}{个|gè}{半|bàn}{小时|xiǎo shí} (an hour and a half).
- *Sounds that are easy to mix up*: {四|sì} *sì* and {十|shí} *shí* (listen for the curled *sh*); {一|yī} *yī*
  and {七|qī} *qī*; {十四|shí sì} (14) and {四十|sì shí} (40), where the order of the two sounds is everything.

## Words that sound the same

Some words you know share their sound, and only the context tells them apart:

| Sound | Words |
|---|---|
| *jìn* | {近|jìn} (near), {进|jìn} (to enter) |
| *kuài* | {快|kuài} (fast), {块|kuài} (yuan; piece) |
| *huà* | {话|huà} (in {电话|diàn huà}, {说话|shuō huà}), {画|huà} (to draw) |
| *zài* | {在|zài} (at; in the middle of), {再|zài} (again) |
| *tā* | {他|tā}, {她|tā}, {它|tā} (he, she, it) |

Others differ only in the tone, so the tone matters: {买|mǎi} *mǎi* (buy) and {卖|mài} *mài* (sell); {有|yǒu} *yǒu*
(have) and {右|yòu} *yòu* (right).

## When you don't understand

Asking is normal and polite. These phrases keep a conversation going when you've lost the thread:

```speak
{对不起|duì bu qǐ}，{我|wǒ}{没|méi}{听|tīng}{懂|dǒng}。
= Sorry, I didn't understand.
{请|qǐng}{再|zài}{说|shuō}{一下|yí xià}。
= Please say it again.
{请|qǐng}{慢|màn}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}{说|shuō}。
= Please speak a little more slowly.
{你|nǐ}{说|shuō}{什么|shén me}？
= What did you say?
“{门票|mén piào}”{是|shì}{什么|shén me}{意思|yì si}？
= What does "menpiao" mean?
{你|nǐ}{是|shì}{说|shuō}{星期|xīng qī}{六|liù}{吗|ma}？
= Do you mean Saturday?
```

- {没|méi}{听|tīng}{懂|dǒng} is {听|tīng} + {懂|dǒng}, a result complement (lesson 17): you listened but didn't understand. {没|méi}{听见|tīng jiàn}
  would be "didn't hear".
- {你|nǐ}{说|shuō}{什么|shén me}？ is fine among friends; with a teacher or a stranger, {对不起|duì bu qǐ}，{请|qǐng}{再|zài}{说|shuō}{一下|yí xià} is politer.
- To check one detail, repeat it with {吗|ma}: {你|nǐ}{是|shì}{说|shuō}{三|sān}{点|diǎn}{吗|ma}？ The other person only needs to say {对|duì} or
  correct you.

## Dialogue 1: which way to the metro?

The speakers are {安娜|Ān nà} and a man: {男|nán} is the label for a man's voice, {女|nǚ} for a woman's, as on
listening papers. Listen first with the words hidden. Then answer: How far is the station? Which way do you go?

```dialogue
# Which way to the metro?
安娜: {请问|qǐng wèn}，{地铁|dì tiě}{站|zhàn}{离|lí}{这儿|zhèr}{远|yuǎn}{吗|ma}？
= Excuse me, is the metro station far from here?
男: {不|bù}{远|yuǎn}。{你|nǐ}{往|wǎng}{前|qián}{走|zǒu}，{到|dào}{了|le}{路口|lù kǒu}{往|wǎng}{左|zuǒ}{走|zǒu}，{地铁|dì tiě}{站|zhàn}{就|jiù}{在|zài}{银行|yín háng}{旁边|páng biān}。
= Not far. Go straight on, turn left at the crossing, and the station is right next to the bank.
安娜: {对不起|duì bu qǐ}，{我|wǒ}{没|méi}{听|tīng}{懂|dǒng}。{请|qǐng}{慢|màn}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}{说|shuō}。
= Sorry, I didn't understand. Please speak a little more slowly.
男: {往|wǎng}{前|qián}{走|zǒu}，{到|dào}{了|le}{路口|lù kǒu}{往|wǎng}{左|zuǒ}{走|zǒu}。{走路|zǒu lù}{十|shí}{分钟|fēn zhōng}{就|jiù}{到|dào}{了|le}。
= Go straight ahead and turn left at the crossing. It's ten minutes on foot.
安娜: {往|wǎng}{前|qián}{走|zǒu}，{往|wǎng}{左|zuǒ}{走|zǒu}……{谢谢|xiè xie}{您|nín}！
= Straight ahead, then left… Thank you!
男: {不客气|bú kè qi}。
= You're welcome.
```

{路口|lù kǒu} (crossing) and {银行|yín háng} (bank) are HSK 3 words.

<details>
<summary>Answers</summary>

Ten minutes on foot ({走路|zǒu lù}{十|shí}{分钟|fēn zhōng}). Straight ahead, then left at the crossing: the station is next to
the bank.
</details>

## Dialogue 2: in a phone shop

Listen for the numbers. How much is the phone? How much does Li Ming pay in the end?

```dialogue
# In a phone shop
李明: {这个|zhè ge}{手机|shǒu jī}{多少|duō shao}{钱|qián}？
= How much is this phone?
女: {两千八|liǎng qiān bā}。
= Two thousand eight hundred.
李明: {太|tài}{贵|guì}{了|le}。{那个|nà ge}{黑色|hēi sè}{的|de}{呢|ne}？
= Too expensive. What about that black one?
女: {黑色|hēi sè}{的|de}{比|bǐ}{这个|zhè ge}{便宜|pián yi}，{两千二|liǎng qiān èr}。
= The black one is cheaper than this one: two thousand two hundred.
李明: {白色|bái sè}{的|de}{有没有|yǒu mei yǒu}？
= Do you have it in white?
女: {有|yǒu}，{白色|bái sè}{的|de}{也|yě}{是|shì}{两千二|liǎng qiān èr}。
= Yes, the white one is also two thousand two hundred.
李明: {好|hǎo}，{我|wǒ}{要|yào}{白色|bái sè}{的|de}。
= OK, I'll take the white one.
```

<details>
<summary>Answers</summary>

The first phone is {两千八|liǎng qiān bā} (2,800 yuan); Li Ming buys the white one for {两千二|liǎng qiān èr} (2,200). {两千八|liǎng qiān bā} is
short for {两千八百|liǎng qiān bā bǎi}.
</details>

## Dialogue 3: making plans

Listen for the time, the place and what they decide. What are they going to do, and when?

```dialogue
# Saturday plans
王芳: {大卫|Dà wèi}，{这个|zhè ge}{星期|xīng qī}{六|liù}{你|nǐ}{有|yǒu}{时间|shí jiān}{吗|ma}？
= David, are you free this Saturday?
大卫: {上午|shàng wǔ}{我|wǒ}{要|yào}{去|qù}{游泳|yóu yǒng}，{下午|xià wǔ}{有|yǒu}{时间|shí jiān}。{怎么|zěn me}{了|le}？
= In the morning I'm going swimming, but I'm free in the afternoon. Why?
王芳: {我们|wǒ men}{一起|yì qǐ}{去|qù}{看|kàn}{电影|diàn yǐng}，{还是|hái shi}{去|qù}{商场|shāng chǎng}？
= Shall we go to see a film or go to the shopping centre?
大卫: {看|kàn}{电影|diàn yǐng}{吧|ba}，{我|wǒ}{很久|hěn jiǔ}{没|méi}{看|kàn}{电影|diàn yǐng}{了|le}。
= Let's see a film. I haven't seen one for ages.
王芳: {好|hǎo}{啊|a}。{电影|diàn yǐng}{是|shì}{三|sān}{点|diǎn}{半|bàn}{的|de}，{我们|wǒ men}{三|sān}{点|diǎn}{在|zài}{电影院|diàn yǐng yuàn}{门口|mén kǒu}{见|jiàn}{吧|ba}。
= Great. The film's at half past three: let's meet at the cinema entrance at three.
大卫: {三|sān}{点|diǎn}，{电影院|diàn yǐng yuàn}{门口|mén kǒu}。{不见不散|bú jiàn bú sàn}！
= Three o'clock, cinema entrance. See you there!
```

{很久|hěn jiǔ} (a long time: {久|jiǔ} is HSK 3) and {不见不散|bú jiàn bú sàn} ("we won't
leave until we've met", a set phrase for "see you there") are glossed. {怎么|zěn me}{了|le}？ is "what's up?",
"why do you ask?".

<details>
<summary>Answers</summary>

They're going to see a film ({看|kàn}{电影|diàn yǐng}{吧|ba}) on Saturday afternoon; the film is at 3:30 and they'll meet
at three at the cinema entrance. David can't in the morning because he's going swimming.
</details>

## Dialogue 4: on the phone

Listen for the phone number. Which number does Wang Fang give, and which part does Li Ming check?

```dialogue
# A phone number
李明: {喂|wèi}，{王芳|Wáng Fāng}，{你|nǐ}{妈妈|mā ma}{的|de}{手机号|shǒu jī hào}{是|shì}{多少|duō shao}？
= Hello, Wang Fang, what's your mum's mobile number?
王芳: {一二九|yāo èr jiǔ}，{零零零零|líng líng líng líng}，{二四六八|èr sì liù bā}。
= One three nine, zero zero zero zero, two four six eight.
李明: {对不起|duì bu qǐ}，{请|qǐng}{再|zài}{说|shuō}{一下|yí xià}。{一二九|yāo èr jiǔ}……
= Sorry, please say it again. One three nine…
王芳: {一二九|yāo èr jiǔ}，{零零零零|líng líng líng líng}，{二四六八|èr sì liù bā}。
= One three nine, zero zero zero zero, two four six eight.
李明: {你|nǐ}{是|shì}{说|shuō}{二四六八|èr sì liù bā}{吗|ma}？{不|bú}{是|shì}{二四六七|èr sì liù qī}？
= You mean two four six eight? Not two four six seven?
王芳: {对|duì}，{是|shì}{二四六八|èr sì liù bā}。
= Right, it's two four six eight.
```

In phone numbers {一|yī} is said *yāo*: listen to how the voice reads {一二九|yāo èr jiǔ}. (Some voices read it
*yī*; people almost always say *yāo*.) The number is 129 0000 2468; Li Ming checks the last part
with {你|nǐ}{是|shì}{说|shuō}……{吗|ma}？

## Keeping a conversation going

Short replies show you're listening and give you time to think:

| Reply | Use it |
|---|---|
| {是|shì}{吗|ma}？ | Really? (polite interest) |
| {真|zhēn}{的|de}{吗|ma}？ | Really? (surprise) |
| {对|duì}。/ {对|duì}{啊|a}。 | Right. / Yes, that's right. |
| {我|wǒ}{也|yě}{是|shì}。 | Me too. |
| {太|tài}{好|hǎo}{了|le}！ | Great! |
| {还|hái}{有|yǒu}{呢|ne}？ | And what else? |
| {为什么|wèi shén me}？ | Why? |

## Common mistakes

- Listening for every word and losing the sentence. Catch the key words and the turning words.
- Answering after the first speaker: the plan often changes in the next line.
- Mixing up {四|sì} and {十|shí}, {十四|shí sì} and {四十|sì shí}, {买|mǎi} and {卖|mài}.
- Missing a {不|bù} or {没|méi} at normal speed: they're short, so listen for them just before the verb.
- Hearing {一|yī} *yāo* in a phone number and taking it for a new word.
- Saying {我|wǒ}{不|bù}{懂|dǒng} for "I didn't catch that": {我|wǒ}{没|méi}{听|tīng}{懂|dǒng} is about this sentence, {我|wǒ}{不|bù}{懂|dǒng} sounds like you
  don't understand the subject at all.

## Key points

- Read the question and the choices first; listen for what they ask about.
- Question words decide the kind of answer: {谁|shéi}, {什么|shén me}{时候|shí hou}, {在|zài}{哪儿|nǎr}, {怎么|zěn me}, {为什么|wèi shén me}, {多少|duō shao} / {几|jǐ}, {还是|hái shi}.
- Numbers: {两|liǎng} before measure words, {一|yī} *yāo* in phone numbers, shortened big numbers ({两万五|liǎng wàn wǔ}),
  approximate numbers with {几|jǐ} and {多|duō}.
- Same sound, different word: {近|jìn} / {进|jìn}, {快|kuài} / {块|kuài}, {话|huà} / {画|huà}, {在|zài} / {再|zài}; same syllable, different tone:
  {买|mǎi} / {卖|mài}, {有|yǒu} / {右|yòu}.
- When you don't understand: {我|wǒ}{没|méi}{听|tīng}{懂|dǒng}, {请|qǐng}{再|zài}{说|shuō}{一下|yí xià}, {请|qǐng}{慢|màn}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}{说|shuō}, {你|nǐ}{是|shì}{说|shuō}……{吗|ma}？

This lesson has no new words.

lessons.title: Writing forms and short notes
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

HSK 1 asked you only to read. At HSK 2 you start to write: the tasks of the level are filling in
a form, writing down a time, a place, a name or a quantity, and writing a short greeting or note.
These are also the first things you write in real life: your name on a form at a gym, a
message on the fridge, "happy birthday" on a card.

This lesson covers each task, with models to copy and change, and ends with a practice page of
the 100 characters HSK expects you to write by hand by the end of level 2. Lesson 30 says what
the exam asks for in writing.

## Two ways to write: by hand and by keyboard

- *By hand*, character by character, in the right stroke order. You can write all 100
  handwriting characters of levels 1–2 by the end of this lesson; the others you need only to
  read.
- *With a keyboard*: you type the pinyin and choose the character from a list. This is how
  most Chinese people write messages. It needs a Chinese keyboard on your device (on most
  computers and phones it's listed as something like "Chinese (Simplified), Pinyin"). Typing gets the strokes right
  for you, but you must still recognise the right character: {在|zài} and {再|zài} are both *zai*, {近|jìn} and {进|jìn}
  both *jin*.

The typed questions of this module ask for characters, so add a Chinese keyboard to your device
if you haven't yet.


## Filling in a form

Forms everywhere ask for the same things. The words you'll see most:

| On the form | Meaning | What you write |
|---|---|---|
| {姓名|xìng míng} | full name | surname first: {王芳|Wáng Fāng}, or your Chinese name |
| {性别|xìng bié} | sex | {男|nán} or {女|nǚ} |
| {国籍|guó jí} | nationality | {中国|Zhōng guó}, {美国|Měi guó}… |
| {生日|shēng rì} | date of birth | 2008{年|nián}5{月|yuè}16{日|rì} |
| {手机|shǒu jī} / {电话|diàn huà} | mobile / phone | digits: 125 0000 5678 |
| {地址|dì zhǐ} | address | big to small (see below) |
| {学校|xué xiào} / {班|bān} | school / class | {大明|Dà míng}{高中|gāo zhōng} {二|èr}{班|bān} |
| {爱好|ài hào} | hobbies | {游泳|yóu yǒng}、{跑步|pǎo bù} |
| {日期|rì qī} | date (of filling in) | today's date |

{性别|xìng bié}, {地址|dì zhǐ} and {日期|rì qī} are words you'll find on
forms; you don't need to learn them as vocabulary yet. {国籍|guó jí} was in lesson 27.

Here is a filled-in form for a swimming class. The school and the address are made up.

> **{游泳|yóu yǒng}{班|bān}**
>
> | | |
> |---|---|
> | {姓名|xìng míng} | {大卫|Dà wèi} |
> | {性别|xìng bié} | {男|nán} |
> | {国籍|guó jí} | {英国|Yīng guó} |
> | {生日|shēng rì} | 2007{年|nián}11{月|yuè}3{日|rì} |
> | {手机|shǒu jī} | 127 0000 2468 |
> | {地址|dì zhǐ} | {北京市|Běi jīng shì}{大明|Dà míng}{路|lù}15{号|hào}3{楼|lóu}302 |
> | {爱好|ài hào} | {跑步|pǎo bù}、{踢|tī}{足球|zú qiú} |
> | {日期|rì qī} | 2026{年|nián}9{月|yuè}1{日|rì} |

{英国|Yīng guó} is the United Kingdom. {北京市|Běi jīng shì} is the city of Beijing ({市|shì}: city).

### Rules for forms

- *Names*: surname first, given name after, no space: {王芳|Wáng Fāng}, {张小雨|Zhāng Xiǎo yǔ}. A foreign name in Chinese is
  usually written as its sound ({大卫|Dà wèi} for David, {安娜|Ān nà} for Anna); ask your teacher or a Chinese
  friend to help you choose one.
- *Dates*: year, month, day, with {年|nián}, {月|yuè} and {日|rì}: 2026{年|nián}12{月|yuè}13{日|rì}. Forms use {日|rì} (written); in speech
  people say {号|hào}. The year can be in digits or characters ({二|èr}〇{二六|èr liù}{年|nián}), but digits are usual on
  forms.
- *Addresses*: from big to small, the opposite of English: city, then the street and number,
  then the building, floor and room. {北京市|Běi jīng shì}{大明|Dà míng}{路|lù}15{号|hào}3{楼|lóu}302 is "Room 302, 3rd floor, No. 15 Daming
  Road, Beijing".
- *Numbers*: phone numbers, house numbers and room numbers are in digits.
- *Lists*: separate items with the list comma 、: {跑步|pǎo bù}、{游泳|yóu yǒng}.

## Times, places, names and quantities

Many short writing tasks ask for just one of these. Each has a set order.

| Write | Order | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| a time | big to small: day, part of day, hour | {明天|míng tiān}{上午|shàng wǔ}{九|jiǔ}{点|diǎn}, {星期|xīng qī}{六|liù}{下午|xià wǔ}{三|sān}{点|diǎn}{半|bàn} |
| a date | year, month, day | 2026{年|nián}12{月|yuè}13{日|rì}, 12{月|yuè}13{号|hào} |
| a place | the place, then the position | {学校|xué xiào}{门口|mén kǒu}, {教室|jiào shì}{里面|lǐ miàn}, {银行|yín háng}{旁边|páng biān}, {三|sān}{楼|lóu} |
| a name | surname first; title after | {王芳|Wáng Fāng}, {王老师|Wáng lǎo shī}, {李|Lǐ}{先生|xiān sheng} |
| a quantity | number + measure word + noun | {两|liǎng}{本|běn}{书|shū}, {三|sān}{杯|bēi}{咖啡|kā fēi}, {十|shí}{几|jǐ}{个|gè}{人|rén}, {一万|yí wàn}{块|kuài} |

Quantities are where most mistakes happen. The measure word is never left out (~~{三|sān}{书|shū}~~), and
before a measure word "two" is {两|liǎng}, not {二|èr} ({两|liǎng}{本|běn}{书|shū}, ~~{二|èr}{本|běn}{书|shū}~~). Lesson 22's approximate numbers work
in writing too: {二十|èr shí}{多|duō}{个|gè}{人|rén}.

{银行|yín háng} (bank) is an HSK 3 word.

## Short greetings

Greetings on cards and in messages are set phrases. Learn them whole:

| Greeting | Meaning | When |
|---|---|---|
| {生日|shēng rì}{快乐|kuài lè}！ | Happy birthday! | birthdays |
| {祝|zhù}{你|nǐ}{生日|shēng rì}{快乐|kuài lè}！ | Happy birthday (to you)! | a card |
| {新年|xīn nián}{快乐|kuài lè}！ | Happy New Year! | 1 January and the Spring Festival |
| {谢谢|xiè xie}{你|nǐ}！ / {谢谢|xiè xie}{您|nín}！ | Thank you! | anything |
| {明天|míng tiān}{见|jiàn}！ | See you tomorrow! | notes, messages |
| {欢迎|huān yíng}{你|nǐ}！ | Welcome! | a card or a sign for a guest |

{祝|zhù} (to wish) and {新年|xīn nián} (New Year) and {欢迎|huān yíng} (welcome) are HSK 3 words, but they appear in greetings everywhere, so learn the phrases now.
Lesson 30h2 has more greetings and messages.

## Short notes

A note has the same shape as a text message (lesson 27): who it's for, then a colon, the message,
and who wrote it, often with the time.

> {妈妈|mā ma}：{我|wǒ}{去|qù}{药店|yào diàn}{买|mǎi}{药|yào}{了|le}，{一会儿|yí huìr}{回来|huí lái}。{小明|Xiǎo Míng} {下午|xià wǔ}{四|sì}{点|diǎn}

> {王老师|Wáng lǎo shī}：{对不起|duì bu qǐ}，{我|wǒ}{今天|jīn tiān}{身体|shēn tǐ}{不|bù}{舒服|shū fu}，{不|bù}{能|néng}{去|qù}{上课|shàng kè}{了|le}。{李明|Lǐ Míng} 3{月|yuè}6{日|rì}

> {安娜|Ān nà}：{我|wǒ}{在|zài}{学校|xué xiào}{门口|mén kǒu}{等|děng}{你|nǐ}。{快|kuài}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}！{大卫|Dà wèi}

> {大家|dà jiā}：{明天|míng tiān}{的|de}{考试|kǎo shì}{从|cóng}{上午|shàng wǔ}{九|jiǔ}{点|diǎn}{开始|kāi shǐ}，{请|qǐng}{八|bā}{点|diǎn}{半|bàn}{到|dào}302{教室|jiào shì}。{别|bié}{忘|wàng}{了|le}{带|dài}{笔|bǐ}！{王老师|Wáng lǎo shī}

Notice what notes leave out: the subject when it's clear ({一会儿|yí huìr}{回来|huí lái} needs no {我|wǒ}), polite words
between friends. A note to a teacher keeps the politeness: {对不起|duì bu qǐ} at the start, the reason with
{因为|yīn wèi} or just stated ({身体|shēn tǐ}{不|bù}{舒服|shū fu}), and {您|nín} for "you".

{带|dài} (to bring) is an HSK 3 word.

### Write your own

Change the model to fit you, and write it on paper or in a message to yourself:

1. A note to a family member: where you've gone and when you'll be back.
2. A note to a teacher: you can't come tomorrow, and why.
3. A message to a friend: where and when to meet.
4. A birthday card for a friend.

## Dialogue: at the swimming pool

The speakers are a woman at the desk ({女|nǚ}) and {安娜|Ān nà}, who is joining the swimming class.

```dialogue
# Joining a class
女: {你好|nǐ hǎo}！{你|nǐ}{想|xiǎng}{学|xué}{游泳|yóu yǒng}{吗|ma}？{请|qǐng}{写|xiě}{一下|yí xià}{这个|zhè ge}{表|biǎo}。
= Hello! Would you like to learn to swim? Please fill in this form.
安娜: {好|hǎo}。{姓名|xìng míng}{写|xiě}{中文|Zhōng wén}{还是|hái shi}{英文|Yīng wén}？
= OK. Should I write my name in Chinese or English?
女: {都|dōu}{可以|kě yǐ}。{你|nǐ}{有|yǒu}{中文|Zhōng wén}{名字|míng zi}{吗|ma}？
= Either is fine. Do you have a Chinese name?
安娜: {有|yǒu}，{我|wǒ}{叫|jiào}{安美|Ān Měi}。{生日|shēng rì}{也|yě}{要|yào}{写|xiě}{吗|ma}？
= Yes, it's An Mei. Do I need to write my birthday too?
女: {要|yào}。{还|hái}{有|yǒu}{你|nǐ}{的|de}{手机号|shǒu jī hào}。
= Yes. And your mobile number.
安娜: {写|xiě}{好|hǎo}{了|le}。{什么|shén me}{时候|shí hou}{开始|kāi shǐ}{上课|shàng kè}？
= Done. When do the classes start?
女: {下|xià}{星期|xīng qī}{一|yī}{下午|xià wǔ}{五|wǔ}{点|diǎn}。{请|qǐng}{早|zǎo}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}{来|lái}。
= Next Monday at five in the afternoon. Please come a little early.
```

{表|biǎo} on its own is a form or table; in {手表|shǒu biǎo} it's a watch. {英文|Yīng wén} is
English (the language, written).

## Writing by hand: the 100 characters

HSK expects you to write these 100 characters by hand at levels 1–2. You've met all of them: 21 in
the pinyin course, 74 in HSK 1 and the last five in this course ({长|cháng}, {为|wèi}, {地|dì}, {过|guò}, {比|bǐ}). The
character list in the Study tools box has them all, with their meanings and stroke counts.

How to practise:

1. Trace each character once on the pad below, slowly, following the numbers.
2. Write it three times on paper from memory, in a square, saying its pinyin.
3. Check each stroke against the pad. Wrong stroke order? Trace it again.
4. Come back to a block a day later and write it from memory again.

Paper with a square for each character, divided by a dashed cross, helps you keep the proportions.

### From the pinyin course

```trace
一二三十人大四
```

```trace
五六七八九日月
```

```trace
中小口不你我好
```

### From HSK 1

```trace
是他她叫什么名
```

```trace
字吗很学生们国
```

```trace
汉语文说会也有
```

```trace
没的这那和家爸
```

```trace
妈哥姐几个百两
```

```trace
岁多少儿子女在
```

```trace
工作男今天年点
```

```trace
分半时现间上午
```

```trace
下去来要打茶书
```

```trace
对后边习写同可
```

```trace
以了爱还
```

### From HSK 2

```trace
长为地过比
```

Watch out for the pairs that look alike: {午|wǔ} and {牛|niú} (the vertical of {午|wǔ} doesn't go through the
top), {天|tiān} and {夫|fū} (in {夫|fū} the stroke falling to the left starts above the top line and goes through it), {人|rén} and {入|rù} (to enter), {己|jǐ} (in {自己|zì jǐ}) and {已|yǐ} (in {已经|yǐ jīng}), {日|rì} and {目|mù} (eye),
{大|dà} and {太|tài}. These pairs are written the same way in traditional characters.

{=
And for simplified {为|wèi}: the dot at the top left comes first, then the long falling stroke, then the
horizontal that bends down and hooks, and last the dot inside. (Traditional {為|wèi} is a different shape; trace it on the
pad with the switch on Traditional.)
=}

## Common mistakes

- Writing the given name first on a form: Chinese forms want {王芳|Wáng Fāng}, not ~~{芳王|Fāng Wáng}~~.
- Dates in English order: 5{月|yuè}16{日|rì} 2008{年|nián} is wrong; write 2008{年|nián}5{月|yuè}16{日|rì}.
- Addresses from small to big: on a Chinese form the city comes first.
- Leaving out the measure word (~~{两|liǎng}{书|shū}~~) or writing {二|èr} before it (~~{二|èr}{本|běn}{书|shū}~~): {两|liǎng}{本|běn}{书|shū}.
- Picking the wrong character from the keyboard list: {在|zài} (at) for {再|zài} (again), {进|jìn} (enter) for {近|jìn}
  (near). Read what you typed before you send it.
- Mixing up {己|jǐ} and {已|yǐ}, {午|wǔ} and {牛|niú}, {天|tiān} and {夫|fū} by hand.

## Key points

- Forms: {姓名|xìng míng} (surname first), {性别|xìng bié}, {国籍|guó jí}, {生日|shēng rì} (year–month–day), {手机|shǒu jī}, {地址|dì zhǐ} (big to small), {爱好|ài hào}.
- Times and dates go big to small; places put the position after the place ({学校|xué xiào}{门口|mén kǒu}); quantities
  are number + measure word + noun, with {两|liǎng} for "two".
- Greetings are set phrases: {生日|shēng rì}{快乐|kuài lè}, {新年|xīn nián}{快乐|kuài lè}, {谢谢|xiè xie}{你|nǐ}, {明天|míng tiān}{见|jiàn}.
- A note: who it's for and a colon, the message, who wrote it and when.
- Write the 100 handwriting characters from memory, in stroke order, and use a Chinese keyboard
  for messages.

This lesson has no new words.

lessons.title: The HSK 2 exam
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

This course covers the words and characters of the new HSK 2: 500 words and 371 characters with
HSK 1. This lesson explains what the exam is, what is known about how the level-2 paper is
built, gives strategies for each part, and ends with a short practice set written for this
course in the style of the exam's tasks. The questions after the lesson are more practice of the
same kind.

You don't need to take the exam to use the course, but a date in the calendar is a good reason
to review, and a pass shows schools and employers what you can do.

## The HSK and its new version

The **[[HSK]]** ({汉语水平考试|Hàn yǔ shuǐ píng kǎo shì}, Chinese proficiency test: {水平|shuǐ píng} is "level", an HSK 3 word)
is the official test of Chinese for people whose first language isn't Chinese. It's run by an
organisation under China's Ministry of Education and taken at test centres around the world, on
paper or on a computer depending on the centre.

The new version, often called **[[HSK 3.0]]**, has nine levels in three bands. Its exam syllabus was
published in November 2025 and has been in force since July 2026; the first official sitting was
announced for 13 December 2026, after trial sittings earlier in the year. Level 2 covers 500
words and 371 characters in all, and the topics and tasks this course has followed: appearance
and clothes, birthdays, travel, family life, festivals, names and forms of address, shopping,
eating out and feelings; filling in forms, writing times, places, names and quantities, and
reading notices and messages.

Many books and apps still describe the old HSK 2 (300 words) or the 2021 standard's level 2 (over
1,200 words). Both differ from the new exam, so check which one a resource means.

> Exam details change, and the organisers publish them on the official HSK website
> (chinesetest.cn), with sample papers. Before you register, check the format, the dates, the fee
> and the pass mark there. What follows comes from the syllabus and from reports on the sample
> papers and trial sittings, and some of it had not been officially confirmed when this lesson
> was written.

## How the new HSK 2 is built

Reports on the official sample paper of the new HSK 2 (from Chinese Testing International) agree on
the size and the parts:

| | |
|---|---|
| Questions | 60: listening 25, reading 25, writing 10 |
| Time | about 60 minutes in all, including time for your details and for copying answers |
| Parts | listening (about 17 minutes), reading (25 minutes), writing (10 minutes) |
| Speaking | none at level 2 |
| Pass mark | not yet published for the new version |

The *writing* part is new at this level: the old HSK 2 had listening and reading only, and a few
guides still describe the new one that way. The lesson follows the sample-paper reports, but these
are reports, not the official description of the real exam, so check the format on the official
site before you sit it. Everything in this course's character sections and handwriting practice is
what the writing part tests, and the practice set below includes both kinds of writing task.

### Listening

You hear short sentences and dialogues, at nearly normal speed. The reports describe three kinds of
task:

- *Sentence and picture.* You hear a short sentence and choose the photo that shows it.
- *Dialogue and picture.* You hear a short exchange and choose, from a group of photos, the one it
  goes with.
- *Dialogue and question.* Two people speak, then a voice asks about it: where they are, what
  one of them will do, when, how much. You choose the answer from three written choices.

Lesson 28's strategies are what you need: read the choices before the audio, listen for the
question word, the numbers and the turning words ({不|bù}, {没|méi}, {别|bié}, {还|hái}{没|méi}, {已经|yǐ jīng}, {但是|dàn shì}, {还是|hái shi}), and listen to
the end of the dialogue.

### Reading

- *Sentence and picture.* Read a sentence and choose the photo that matches it.
- *Fill the gap.* Choose the word that completes a sentence: a measure word, a complement
  ({完|wán}, {懂|dǒng}, {好|hǎo}), a particle ({的|de}, {得|de}, {地|de}, {了|le}, {过|guo}, {着|zhe}), a conjunction ({因为|yīn wèi}, {所以|suǒ yǐ}, {但是|dàn shì}).
- *Questions and answers.* Choose the sentence that answers or continues a line of a dialogue.
- *Short texts.* Read a sentence or a short text (a notice, a message, a short paragraph) and
  answer a question about it, from three choices (lesson 27). Read carefully: {他|tā}{比|bǐ}{我|wǒ}{高|gāo} tells you
  I'm shorter than him.

### Writing

- *Choose the component.* A word is shown with one character missing a part: choose the
  component (often a radical such as 亻, 氵, 讠, {口|kǒu} or {女|nǚ}) that completes it.
- *Write the character.* A sentence gives the pinyin of one character: write the character. The
  100 handwriting characters of lesson 29 are the ones to know. (The reports don't say how a
  computer-based test handles this task.)

## Scoring

The old HSK 2 gave up to 100 points for listening and 100 for reading and was passed with 120 of
200. For the new HSK, the sample papers reported so far give no score scale or pass mark, so don't
assume the old figures still apply: check the official site.


## Strategies

### Before the test

- *Do an official sample paper untimed* to learn what each task looks like. Then do this
  lesson's practice set and the module quizzes.
- *Review every word.* Your vocabulary reviews have all 500 words of HSK 1 and 2. In the last
  weeks, bring every word to at least Advanced, and spend most time on the ones you keep missing.
- *Read with pinyin off.* One report says the sample paper prints pinyin with the Chinese, as the
  old HSK 2 did, but that isn't confirmed for the real exam: practise as if it won't. Turn the
  pinyin switch off in the reviews and the lessons.
- *Listen every day.* Play the dialogues of lessons 26–28 with the words hidden.
- *Write by hand.* Ten minutes a day on the 100 characters of lesson 29.

### During the test

1. *Read the choices before the audio.* Times? Listen for {点|diǎn} and {半|bàn}. Places? {在|zài}, {到|dào}, {门口|mén kǒu}, {旁边|páng biān}.
2. *Answer every question.* On the old exam there was no penalty for a wrong answer. Cross out the
   choices you know are wrong, then choose.
3. *Let a missed item go.* In listening, the audio doesn't wait: get ready for the next one.
4. *Read to the end.* {他|tā}{还|hái}{没|méi}{来|lái} and {他|tā}{已经|yǐ jīng}{来|lái}{了|le} differ in one word; {比|bǐ} sentences turn on which
   person comes first.
5. *Check grammar words in gaps.* {的|de} before a noun ({我|wǒ}{的|de}{书|shū}), {得|de} after a verb ({说|shuō}{得|de}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}), {地|de} before
   a verb ({慢|màn}{慢|màn}{地|de}{说|shuō}).
6. *Manage the time.* In reading, do the items you find easy first and come back to the others.

## A short practice set

Try these, then check your answers below. They're written for this course in the style of the
exam's tasks, not copied from any paper.

### A. Listening

Play each line without looking at the words, and choose its meaning.

```speak
{我|wǒ}{是|shì}{坐|zuò}{飞机|fēi jī}{来|lái}{的|de}。
= 1. a) by train b) by plane c) by taxi
{他|tā}{比|bǐ}{他|tā}{哥哥|gē ge}{高|gāo}。
= 2. a) His brother is taller. b) He is taller. c) They are the same height.
{电影|diàn yǐng}{已经|yǐ jīng}{开始|kāi shǐ}{了|le}。
= 3. a) The film has started. b) The film is about to start. c) The film hasn't started yet.
```

### B. Questions and answers

Match each sentence to its reply.

| Sentence | Replies |
|---|---|
| 4. {你|nǐ}{吃|chī}{过|guo}{饺子|jiǎo zi}{吗|ma}？ | a) {打车|dǎ chē}{去|qù}{吧|ba}。 |
| 5. {我们|wǒ men}{怎么|zěn me}{去|qù}{机场|jī chǎng}？ | b) {吃|chī}{过|guo}，{很|hěn}{好吃|hǎo chī}！ |
| 6. {你|nǐ}{为什么|wèi shén me}{没|méi}{来|lái}{上课|shàng kè}？ | c) {一百二十|yì bǎi èr shí}{块|kuài}。 |
| 7. {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}{多少|duō shao}{钱|qián}？ | d) {因为|yīn wèi}{我|wǒ}{生病|shēng bìng}{了|le}。 |

### C. Fill the gap

Choose {得|de}, {过|guo}, {着|zhe} or {比|bǐ}.

8. {他|tā}{说|shuō}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{说|shuō}___ {很|hěn}{好|hǎo}。
9. {我|wǒ}{去|qù}___ {两|liǎng}{次|cì}{上海|Shàng hǎi}。
10. {她|tā}{穿|chuān}___ {一|yí}{件|jiàn}{红色|hóng sè}{的|de}{衣服|yī fu}。
11. {今天|jīn tiān}___ {昨天|zuó tiān}{冷|lěng}。

### D. A short text

> {小|xiǎo}{王|Wáng}：{明天|míng tiān}{上午|shàng wǔ}{十|shí}{点|diǎn}{我们|wǒ men}{在|zài}{学校|xué xiào}{门口|mén kǒu}{见|jiàn}，{一起|yì qǐ}{去|qù}{商场|shāng chǎng}{给|gěi}{李明|Lǐ Míng}{买|mǎi}{生日|shēng rì}{礼物|lǐ wù}。{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{送|sòng}{他|tā}{一|yì}{本|běn}{书|shū}，{你|nǐ}{觉得|jué de}{怎么样|zěn me yàng}？{你|nǐ}{有|yǒu}{时间|shí jiān}{吗|ma}？{晚上|wǎn shang}{给|gěi}{我|wǒ}{打电话|dǎ diàn huà}{吧|ba}。{安娜|Ān nà}

{礼物|lǐ wù} (present) is an HSK 3 word.

12. What are they going to buy, and for whom?
13. What does Anna ask Xiao Wang to do, and when?

### E. Writing

14. Which component completes the character? ___ {也|yě} (tā, she): 亻, {女|nǚ} or 氵?
15. Write the character: {我们|wǒ men}{明天|míng tiān} ___ (zài) {学校|xué xiào}{见|jiàn}。
16. Write the character: {下|xià} ___ (wǔ) {三|sān}{点|diǎn}。

<details>
<summary>Answers</summary>

1 b. 2 b (A {比|bǐ} B {高|gāo}: A is taller). 3 a. 4 b. 5 a. 6 d. 7 c. 8 {得|de}. 9 {过|guo}. 10 {着|zhe}. 11 {比|bǐ}.
12 A birthday present for Li Ming, perhaps a book. 13 To call her this evening ({晚上|wǎn shang}{给|gěi}{我|wǒ}{打电话|dǎ diàn huà}{吧|ba}). 14 {女|nǚ} ({她|tā}; {他|tā} has
亻, and {池|chí} "pool" has 氵). 15 {在|zài} (at; not {再|zài} "again"). 16 {午|wǔ}.

Translation of D: Xiao Wang: let's meet at the school gate at ten tomorrow morning and go to the
shopping centre together to buy Li Ming a birthday present. I'd like to give him a book; what do
you think? Are you free? Call me this evening. Anna

</details>

## A study plan for the last month

| Week | Do |
|---|---|
| 1 | One official sample paper, untimed. List the task types you found hard. Review words every day. |
| 2 | Lessons 26–27 again (patterns, reading). Module quizzes of modules 1–3. |
| 3 | Lessons 28–29 again (listening, writing). Module quizzes of modules 4–6. Pinyin off. |
| 4 | A second sample paper, timed. Review only the words and points you missed. Sleep well the night before. |

## Dialogue: after the exam

```dialogue
# After the exam
安娜: {你|nǐ}{觉得|jué de}{考试|kǎo shì}{怎么样|zěn me yàng}？
= What did you think of the exam?
大卫: {听力|tīng lì}{题|tí}{我|wǒ}{都|dōu}{听|tīng}{懂|dǒng}{了|le}，{阅读|yuè dú}{题|tí}{我|wǒ}{做|zuò}{得|de}{有点儿|yǒu diǎnr}{慢|màn}。
= I understood all the listening questions; I was a bit slow on the reading.
安娜: {我|wǒ}{跟|gēn}{你|nǐ}{一样|yí yàng}……{不|bú}{对|duì}，{我|wǒ}{读|dú}{得|de}{比|bǐ}{你|nǐ}{快|kuài}！{你|nǐ}{都|dōu}{做|zuò}{完|wán}{了|le}{吗|ma}？
= Same as you… no, wait, I read faster than you! Did you finish everything?
大卫: {做|zuò}{完|wán}{了|le}，{但是|dàn shì}{最|zuì}{后|hòu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{题|tí}{我|wǒ}{不|bù}{知道|zhī dào}{对|duì}{不|bu}{对|duì}。
= Yes, but I don't know if the last question was right.
安娜: {别|bié}{想|xiǎng}{了|le}！{我们|wǒ men}{已经|yǐ jīng}{考|kǎo}{完|wán}{了|le}，{去|qù}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}{吧|ba}。
= Stop thinking about it! We've finished the exam: let's go and eat.
大卫: {好|hǎo}{啊|a}，{我|wǒ}{请|qǐng}{你|nǐ}{喝|hē}{咖啡|kā fēi}！
= Great, I'll buy you a coffee!
```

{一样|yí yàng} (the same) is an HSK 3 word; {听力|tīng lì} (listening) and {阅读|yuè dú} (reading), the names of the exam
parts, are words for later levels. {请|qǐng} + person + verb is "to treat someone to":
{我|wǒ}{请|qǐng}{你|nǐ}{喝|hē}{咖啡|kā fēi} (my treat).

## Can you do this?

When you can do all of these, you're ready for HSK 2:

- talk about people, families, looks, clothes and feelings (module 1);
- ask for and give directions, and talk about trips you've made, with {过|guo} and {次|cì} (module 2);
- compare with {比|bǐ}, describe a home, and talk about birthdays and plans (module 3);
- say how well something is done with {得|de}, and talk about school, sport and hobbies (module 4);
- order food and drink, shop, talk about the weather, and use big and approximate numbers
  (module 5);
- use the patterns {已经|yǐ jīng}……{了|le}, {快要|kuài yào}……{了|le}, {都|dōu}……{了|le}, {还|hái}{没|méi}……{呢|ne} and {还是|hái shi}……{吧|ba} (lesson 26);
- read a notice, a message, a form and a timetable, and follow a short dialogue (lessons 27–28);
- fill in a form and write a short note, and write the 100 handwriting characters (lesson 29);
- recognise all 371 characters (the character list in the Study tools box).

## Common mistakes

- *Studying the wrong list.* The new HSK 2 has 500 words in all (200 new); older lists have 300,
  and the 2021 standard has far more.
- *Learning only with pinyin.* The characters carry the meaning; practise with pinyin off.
- *Leaving answers blank.* Choose something every time.
- *Stopping at the first speaker.* The second speaker often changes the plan.
- *Confusing {的|de}, {得|de} and {地|de}.* Before a noun {的|de}, after a verb {得|de}, before a verb {地|de}.

## Key points

- The new HSK 2 (HSK 3.0) has 60 questions in about 60 minutes: listening, reading and, new at
  this level, a short writing part (components, and characters from pinyin), as reported from
  the sample paper. There's no speaking test at this level.
- It covers 500 words and 371 characters; check the official site for the current format, dates,
  fee and pass mark.
- Listening: read the choices first, listen for the question word and the turning words, listen
  to the end.
- Reading: skim, then scan; read every sentence to the end; check the small grammar words.
- Writing: know the 100 handwriting characters and the common radicals.

This lesson has no new words. Congratulations on reaching the end of HSK 2!

lessons.title: A longer story
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

This is the longest text of the course: a story of about 430 characters, written for this course
with the words of HSK 1 and 2 and one glossed word. It's in four parts. Read each part
twice: once quickly for what happens (skimming), once slowly with the pinyin if you need it.
Then turn pinyin off and read the whole story again: that's the real test.

## Before you read

The story is about {小月|Xiǎo yuè} (Xiaoyue), a high school student, and her grandparents. One word
is new: {又|yòu} (again), an HSK 3 word for something that happens once more. And watch for
{什么|shén me}{都|dōu}{没有|méi yǒu}, "nothing at all": {什么|shén me} + {都|dōu} + a negative means "not anything". On a phone,
{点|diǎn} is "to tap", a new use of the {点|diǎn} you know from {点|diǎn}{菜|cài} (to order, lesson 21).

Watch for the grammar of this course as you read: {着|zhe} for a state ({拿|ná}{着|zhe}, {穿|chuān}{着|zhe}), {过|guo} for
experience, {得|de} for how something is done, {是|shì}……{的|de}, and the patterns of lesson 26 ({都|dōu}……{了|le}, {快要|kuài yào}……{了|le},
{还是|hái shi}……{吧|ba}).


## The story: {爷爷上网|yé ye shàng wǎng}

### Part 1

> {小月|Xiǎo yuè}{今年|jīn nián}{十六|shí liù}{岁|suì}，{是|shì}{高中|gāo zhōng}{学生|xué sheng}。{她|tā}{的|de}{爷爷|yé ye}{都|dōu}{七十|qī shí}{岁|suì}{了|le}，{但是|dàn shì}{身体|shēn tǐ}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}，{每|měi}{天|tiān}{早上|zǎo shang}{都|dōu}{去|qù}{跑步|pǎo bù}。{爷爷|yé ye}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{新|xīn}{手机|shǒu jī}，{但是|dàn shì}{他|tā}{还|hái}{没|méi}{上|shàng}{过|guo}{网|wǎng}。
>
> {奶奶|nǎi nai}{的|de}{生日|shēng rì}{快要|kuài yào}{到|dào}{了|le}。{爷爷|yé ye}{想|xiǎng}{给|gěi}{奶奶|nǎi nai}{买|mǎi}{一|yí}{件|jiàn}{红色|hóng sè}{的|de}{衣服|yī fu}，{但是|dàn shì}{他|tā}{不|bù}{想|xiǎng}{去|qù}{商场|shāng chǎng}，{因为|yīn wèi}{商场|shāng chǎng}{离|lí}{家|jiā}{太|tài}{远|yuǎn}{了|le}。
>
> {爷爷|yé ye}{问|wèn}{小月|Xiǎo yuè}：“{你|nǐ}{能|néng}{教|jiāo}{我|wǒ}{在|zài}{网上|wǎng shàng}{买|mǎi}{东西|dōng xi}{吗|ma}？”{小月|Xiǎo yuè}{笑|xiào}{着|zhe}{说|shuō}：“{好|hǎo}{啊|a}，{我|wǒ}{教|jiāo}{您|nín}！”

### Part 2

> {小月|Xiǎo yuè}{拿|ná}{着|zhe}{爷爷|yé ye}{的|de}{手机|shǒu jī}，{告诉|gào su}{他|tā}{怎么|zěn me}{上网|shàng wǎng}，{怎么|zěn me}{找|zhǎo}{衣服|yī fu}。“{您|nín}{看|kàn}，{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{红色|hóng sè}{的|de}{衣服|yī fu}{很|hěn}{漂亮|piào liang}，{比|bǐ}{那|nà}{件|jiàn}{便宜|pián yi}，{两百|liǎng bǎi}{块|kuài}。{您|nín}{想|xiǎng}{买|mǎi}，{就|jiù}{点|diǎn}{这儿|zhèr}。”
>
> {爷爷|yé ye}{看|kàn}{了|le}{很|hěn}{长|cháng}{时间|shí jiān}，{说|shuō}：“{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{不错|bú cuò}，{我|wǒ}{觉得|jué de}{奶奶|nǎi nai}{穿|chuān}{着|zhe}{很|hěn}{好看|hǎo kàn}。”
>
> {小月|Xiǎo yuè}{去|qù}{学校|xué xiào}{了|le}。{爷爷|yé ye}{一|yí}{个|gè}{人|rén}{在|zài}{家|jiā}，{他|tā}{点|diǎn}{了|le}{一下|yí xià}，{但是|dàn shì}{手机|shǒu jī}{上|shàng}{什么|shén me}{都|dōu}{没有|méi yǒu}。{他|tā}{觉得|jué de}{自己|zì jǐ}{没|méi}{点|diǎn}{好|hǎo}，{所以|suǒ yǐ}{又|yòu}{点|diǎn}{了|le}{一|yí}{次|cì}，{又|yòu}{点|diǎn}{了|le}{一|yí}{次|cì}……{他|tā}{点|diǎn}{了|le}{十|shí}{次|cì}。

### Part 3

> {过|guò}{了|le}{三|sān}{天|tiān}，{有|yǒu}{人|rén}{在|zài}{门口|mén kǒu}{说|shuō}：“{您|nín}{好|hǎo}，{您|nín}{的|de}{衣服|yī fu}{到|dào}{了|le}！”{爷爷|yé ye}{打开|dǎ kāi}{门|mén}，{看见|kàn jiàn}{那个|nà ge}{人|rén}{拿|ná}{着|zhe}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{包|bāo}。{一|yí}{个|gè}，{两|liǎng}{个|gè}，{三|sān}{个|gè}……{十|shí}{个|gè}！{十|shí}{件|jiàn}{红色|hóng sè}{的|de}{衣服|yī fu}！
>
> {奶奶|nǎi nai}{从|cóng}{房间|fáng jiān}{里|lǐ}{走|zǒu}{出来|chū lái}，{问|wèn}：“{这么|zhè me}{多|duō}{衣服|yī fu}！{是|shì}{谁|shéi}{买|mǎi}{的|de}？”
>
> {爷爷|yé ye}{不好意思|bù hǎo yì si}{地|de}{说|shuō}：“{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{在|zài}{网上|wǎng shàng}{买|mǎi}{的|de}。{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{在|zài}{你|nǐ}{生日|shēng rì}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}{送|sòng}{你|nǐ}{一|yí}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}，{但是|dàn shì}……”

### Part 4

> {奶奶|nǎi nai}{听|tīng}{了|le}，{笑|xiào}{得|de}{很|hěn}{高兴|gāo xìng}：“{太|tài}{好|hǎo}{了|le}！{我们|wǒ men}{家|jiā}{每|měi}{个|gè}{人|rén}{都|dōu}{有|yǒu}{新|xīn}{衣服|yī fu}{了|le}。”
>
> {奶奶|nǎi nai}{生日|shēng rì}{那|nà}{天|tiān}，{爷爷|yé ye}、{奶奶|nǎi nai}、{爸爸|bà ba}、{妈妈|mā ma}{和|hé}{小月|Xiǎo yuè}{都|dōu}{穿|chuān}{着|zhe}{红色|hóng sè}{的|de}{衣服|yī fu}，{一起|yì qǐ}{去|qù}{饭馆|fàn guǎn}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}。{饭馆|fàn guǎn}{里|lǐ}{的|de}{人|rén}{都|dōu}{看|kàn}{着|zhe}{他们|tā men}{笑|xiào}。
>
> {爷爷|yé ye}{说|shuō}：“{在|zài}{网上|wǎng shàng}{买|mǎi}{东西|dōng xi}{真|zhēn}{有意思|yǒu yì si}。{但是|dàn shì}{下|xià}{次|cì}，{我|wǒ}{还是|hái shi}{去|qù}{商场|shāng chǎng}{吧|ba}！”

<details>
<summary>Translation</summary>

**Grandpa goes online**

*Part 1.* Xiaoyue is sixteen this year, a high school student. Her grandpa is already seventy, but
he's in good health and goes running every morning. Grandpa has a new phone, but he's never been
online. Grandma's birthday is coming soon. Grandpa wants to buy Grandma a red top, but he doesn't
want to go to the shopping centre, because it's too far from home. Grandpa asks Xiaoyue: "Can you
teach me to buy things online?" Xiaoyue smiles and says: "Sure, I'll teach you!"

*Part 2.* Holding Grandpa's phone, Xiaoyue shows him how to go online and how to look for clothes.
"Look, this red top is very pretty, and it's cheaper than that one: two hundred yuan. If you want
it, just tap here." Grandpa looks for a long time and says: "This one's not bad. I think Grandma
will look lovely in it." Xiaoyue goes to school. Grandpa is at home alone. He taps once, but
nothing happens on the phone. He thinks he didn't tap properly, so he taps again, and again… He
taps ten times.

*Part 3.* Three days later, someone at the door says: "Hello, your clothes are here!" Grandpa
opens the door and sees the person holding lots of bags. One, two, three… ten! Ten red tops!
Grandma comes out of her room and asks: "So many clothes! Who bought them?" Grandpa says,
embarrassed: "I bought them online. I wanted to give you a top for your birthday, but…"

*Part 4.* Grandma listens and laughs happily: "Wonderful! Now everyone in our family has new
clothes." On Grandma's birthday, Grandpa, Grandma, Dad, Mum and Xiaoyue all wear red and go to a
restaurant together. Everyone in the restaurant looks at them and smiles. Grandpa says: "Buying
things online is really interesting. But next time, I think I'll go to the shopping centre!"
</details>

## Reading it again

Answer in your head, or out loud in Chinese if you can:

1. How old is Grandpa, and what does he do every morning?
2. Why doesn't he want to go to the shopping centre?
3. How much is the red top, and how does it compare with the other one?
4. Why does Grandpa tap ten times?
5. How does Grandma feel when she sees the clothes?
6. What does Grandpa decide at the end?

<details>
<summary>Answers</summary>

1. Seventy ({都|dōu}{七十|qī shí}{岁|suì}{了|le}: "already seventy"); he goes running ({每|měi}{天|tiān}{早上|zǎo shang}{都|dōu}{去|qù}{跑步|pǎo bù}).
2. It's too far from home ({商场|shāng chǎng}{离|lí}{家|jiā}{太|tài}{远|yuǎn}{了|le}).
3. Two hundred yuan, cheaper than the other one ({比|bǐ}{那|nà}{件|jiàn}{便宜|pián yi}).
4. Nothing seemed to happen, and he thought he hadn't tapped properly ({他|tā}{觉得|jué de}{自己|zì jǐ}{没|méi}{点|diǎn}{好|hǎo}).
5. Happy: she laughs ({笑|xiào}{得|de}{很|hěn}{高兴|gāo xìng}) and says everyone in the family now has new clothes.
6. Next time he'll go to the shopping centre ({我|wǒ}{还是|hái shi}{去|qù}{商场|shāng chǎng}{吧|ba}): {还是|hái shi}……{吧|ba}, "I'd better".
</details>

Find these in the story and say what each one does:

- {都|dōu}{七十|qī shí}{岁|suì}{了|le} — {都|dōu}……{了|le}: "already seventy", and that's a lot.
- {快要|kuài yào}{到|dào}{了|le} — {快要|kuài yào}……{了|le}: about to arrive.
- {拿|ná}{着|zhe}, {穿|chuān}{着|zhe} — {着|zhe}: a state that lasts (holding, wearing).
- {是|shì}{谁|shéi}{买|mǎi}{的|de}？{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{在|zài}{网上|wǎng shàng}{买|mǎi}{的|de} — {是|shì}……{的|de}: who and where, for something that has already happened.
- {笑|xiào}{得|de}{很|hěn}{高兴|gāo xìng} — {得|de}: how she laughs.
- {不好意思|bù hǎo yì si}{地|de}{说|shuō} — {地|de}: how he says it.
- {没|méi}{上|shàng}{过|guo}{网|wǎng} — {没|méi} + verb + {过|guo}: never done before.

## Key points

- Read a long text in passes: once for the story, once for the details, once with pinyin off.
- You don't need every word: {又|yòu} is new, but the story makes it clear.
- The grammar of the course works together in real texts: {着|zhe}, {过|guo}, {得|de}, {地|de}, {是|shì}……{的|de}, {比|bǐ}, and the
  fixed patterns of lesson 26.

This lesson has no new words.

lessons.title: Messages and greetings
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Most of the Chinese people write every day is in messages: chats with friends and family, a
quick thank-you, a greeting on a holiday. This lesson shows how those messages are written, which
greetings go with which day, how to thank and apologise in writing, and, for the old-fashioned
occasion, how to address an envelope in Chinese order.

## Text and chat messages

Chat messages are written as people speak, only shorter:

- *No subject when it's clear.* {到|dào}{了|le}！ (I'm here!) needs no {我|wǒ}.
- *Particles of speech*: {吧|ba} for suggestions, {啊|a} and {呢|ne} for a softer or warmer tone, {了|le} for news
  ({我|wǒ}{到|dào}{了|le}, {下雨|xià yǔ}{了|le}).
- *Short answers*: {好|hǎo}{的|de} (OK), {没问题|méi wèn tí} (no problem), {收到|shōu dào} (got it, lesson 27), {谢谢|xiè xie}！, {不客气|bú kè qi}.
  Many people feel that {好|hǎo}{的|de} sounds friendlier than a bare {好|hǎo}, which can read as curt.
- *Laughter* is written {哈哈|hā hā}.
- *Emoji and stickers* do a lot of the work: a smiling face after a sentence makes it warmer, a
  sticker of a thumbs-up or a bowing figure can stand for "OK" or "thank you". On their own they
  can be read in more than one way, so with a teacher or someone you don't know well, add the
  words too.

Here is a family chat. The stickers are described in square brackets.

> **{妈妈|mā ma}**：{小月|Xiǎo yuè}，{你|nǐ}{几|jǐ}{点|diǎn}{下课|xià kè}？
>
> **{小月|Xiǎo yuè}**：{五|wǔ}{点|diǎn}。{怎么|zěn me}{了|le}？
>
> **{妈妈|mā ma}**：{今天|jīn tiān}{爷爷|yé ye}{过|guò}{生日|shēng rì}，{我们|wǒ men}{晚上|wǎn shang}{在|zài}{饭馆|fàn guǎn}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}，{六|liù}{点|diǎn}{半|bàn}。
>
> **{小月|Xiǎo yuè}**：{好|hǎo}{的|de}！[a smiling face] {我|wǒ}{下课|xià kè}{就|jiù}{去|qù}。{在|zài}{哪个|nǎ ge}{饭馆|fàn guǎn}？
>
> **{妈妈|mā ma}**：{学校|xué xiào}{旁边|páng biān}{那个|nà ge}，{你|nǐ}{知道|zhī dào}{吧|ba}？
>
> **{小月|Xiǎo yuè}**：{知道|zhī dào}。{我|wǒ}{给|gěi}{爷爷|yé ye}{准备|zhǔn bèi}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{小|xiǎo}{礼物|lǐ wù}，{哈哈|hā hā}。
>
> **{妈妈|mā ma}**：{太|tài}{好|hǎo}{了|le}！[a thumbs-up]
>
> **{小月|Xiǎo yuè}**：{我|wǒ}{到|dào}{了|le}！{你们|nǐ men}{在|zài}{几|jǐ}{楼|lóu}？
>
> **{妈妈|mā ma}**：{二|èr}{楼|lóu}，{我们|wǒ men}{在|zài}{门口|mén kǒu}{等|děng}{你|nǐ}。

{礼物|lǐ wù} (present) is an HSK 3 word. {我|wǒ}{下课|xià kè}{就|jiù}{去|qù} is "I'll go straight after class": {就|jiù}
(lesson 18) says it happens right after.

<details>
<summary>Translation</summary>

Mum: Xiaoyue, what time do you finish class? — Xiaoyue: Five. Why? — Mum: It's Grandpa's birthday
today; we're having dinner at a restaurant this evening, at half past six. — Xiaoyue: OK! [a
smiling face] I'll go straight after class. Which restaurant? — Mum: The one next to the school,
you know it, right? — Xiaoyue: Yes. I've got a little present ready for Grandpa, ha ha. — Mum:
Great! [a thumbs-up] — Xiaoyue: I'm here! Which floor are you on? — Mum: The first floor up; we're
waiting for you at the door.
</details>

Floors in China are counted from the ground: {一|yī}{楼|lóu} is the ground floor, {二|èr}{楼|lóu} the one above it.


## Holiday greetings

The pattern is the day + {快乐|kuài lè} (happy), or {祝|zhù}{你|nǐ} + a wish:

| Greeting | Meaning | When |
|---|---|---|
| {生日|shēng rì}{快乐|kuài lè}！ | Happy birthday! | someone's birthday |
| {新年|xīn nián}{快乐|kuài lè}！ | Happy New Year! | 1 January; also at the Spring Festival |
| {春节|Chūn jié}{快乐|kuài lè}！ | Happy Spring Festival! | Chinese New Year |
| {节日|jié rì}{快乐|kuài lè}！ | Happy holiday! | any festival |
| {祝|zhù}{你|nǐ}{生日|shēng rì}{快乐|kuài lè}！ | (I wish you a) happy birthday! | a card or a longer message |
| {祝|zhù}{你|nǐ}{身体|shēn tǐ}{好|hǎo}！ | (I wish you) good health! | older people, at New Year |
| {祝|zhù}{你|nǐ}{考|kǎo}{好|hǎo}！ | Good luck in your exam! | before an exam |

{新年|xīn nián} (New Year), {春节|Chūn jié} (the Spring Festival), {节日|jié rì} (festival) and {祝|zhù} (to wish) are HSK 3 words, but you'll see them on every card and in every
holiday message, so learn the phrases whole.

A greeting message often adds a sentence of your own: {新年|xīn nián}{快乐|kuài lè}！{希望|xī wàng}{明年|míng nián}{我们|wǒ men}{能|néng}{一起|yì qǐ}{去|qù}{旅游|lǚ yóu}。 (Happy
New Year! I hope we can travel together next year.) {希望|xī wàng} (lesson 18) is a good word for that.

## Thanking in writing

| Message | Meaning |
|---|---|
| {谢谢|xiè xie}{你|nǐ}{的|de}{花|huā}！ | Thank you for the flowers! |
| {谢谢|xiè xie}{您|nín}{的|de}{帮忙|bāng máng}。 | Thank you for your help. (polite) |
| {太|tài}{谢谢|xiè xie}{你|nǐ}{了|le}！ | Thanks so much! |
| {谢谢|xiè xie}{你|nǐ}{送|sòng}{我|wǒ}{回|huí}{家|jiā}。 | Thanks for taking me home. |

The thing you're thanking for comes after {谢谢|xiè xie}{你|nǐ}: a noun with {的|de} ({谢谢|xiè xie}{你|nǐ}{的|de}{花|huā}) or a whole phrase
({谢谢|xiè xie}{你|nǐ}{送|sòng}{我|wǒ}{回|huí}{家|jiā}). To a teacher or an older person, write {您|nín}.

## Apologising in writing

| Message | Meaning |
|---|---|
| {对不起|duì bu qǐ}，{我|wǒ}{来|lái}{晚|wǎn}{了|le}。 | Sorry I'm late. |
| {不好意思|bù hǎo yì si}，{今天|jīn tiān}{我|wǒ}{不|bù}{能|néng}{去|qù}{了|le}。 | Sorry, I can't come today after all. |
| {真|zhēn}{不好意思|bù hǎo yì si}，{让|ràng}{你|nǐ}{等|děng}{了|le}{这么|zhè me}{长|cháng}{时间|shí jiān}。 | I'm so sorry I kept you waiting so long. |
| {对不起|duì bu qǐ}，{我|wǒ}{忘|wàng}{了|le}{你|nǐ}{的|de}{生日|shēng rì}。 | Sorry, I forgot your birthday. |

As in lesson 15, {对不起|duì bu qǐ} is a real apology for something you did wrong; {不好意思|bù hǎo yì si} is lighter:
sorry for a small trouble, or "excuse me". The usual reply is {没关系|méi guān xi} (never mind) or {没事|méi shì} (it's
nothing).

{让|ràng}{你|nǐ}{等|děng}{了|le}{这么|zhè me}{长|cháng}{时间|shí jiān} uses {让|ràng} (to make someone do something, lesson 18): "made you wait so long".

## Addressing an envelope

Letters are rare now, but the order of an address matters on forms and parcels too. On a
Chinese envelope:

- The address goes from *big to small*: city, road and number, building, room. That's the
  opposite of English.
- The *postcode* of the person you're writing to, six digits in mainland China, goes in the
  boxes at the top left.
- The *name* comes after the address, with a title if you like, and then {收|shōu}: "to be
  received by". {王芳|Wáng Fāng}{收|shōu} or {王芳|Wáng Fāng}（{女士|nǚ shì}）{收|shōu} is "To Wang Fang".
- Printed envelopes have boxes and lines for each part: follow them.

> □□□□□□ (the postcode)
>
> {北京市|Běi jīng shì}{大明|Dà míng}{路|lù}15{号|hào}3{楼|lóu}302
>
> {王芳|Wáng Fāng}（{女士|nǚ shì}）{收|shōu}

The road and the number are made up. Compare the English order: Ms Wang Fang,
Room 302, 3rd floor, 15 Daming Road, Beijing.

## Write your own

Write each one in a message to yourself, then read it with pinyin off:

1. A birthday message to a friend, with a wish of your own after {生日|shēng rì}{快乐|kuài lè}！
2. A New Year message to a teacher (with {您|nín}).
3. A thank-you for a present.
4. An apology: you'll be late, and why.
5. A chat with a friend to agree a time and a place to meet.

## Key points

- Messages are short spoken Chinese: no subject when it's clear, particles, short answers such as
  {好|hǎo}{的|de}, {没问题|méi wèn tí}, {收到|shōu dào}.
- Emoji and stickers soften a message; add the words when you write to a teacher or a stranger.
- Greetings: the day + {快乐|kuài lè} ({生日|shēng rì}{快乐|kuài lè}, {新年|xīn nián}{快乐|kuài lè}, {春节|Chūn jié}{快乐|kuài lè}), or {祝|zhù}{你|nǐ} + a wish.
- Thanks: {谢谢|xiè xie}{你|nǐ}{的|de}…… / {谢谢|xiè xie}{你|nǐ} + verb phrase; {您|nín} for older people and teachers.
- Apologies: {对不起|duì bu qǐ} for a real mistake, {不好意思|bù hǎo yì si} for a small trouble; replies {没关系|méi guān xi}, {没事|méi shì}.
- Envelopes: postcode at the top left, the address from big to small, the name and {收|shōu} last.

This lesson has no new words.

questions.stem: You meet a friend's grandfather for the first time and want to ask his family name. What do you say?
questions.explanation: {您|nín}{贵姓|guì xìng}？ is the polite question for an older person: {您|nín} plus {贵|guì} ("honoured"). {你|nǐ}{叫|jiào}{什么|shén me}？ is for classmates and children. {贵姓|guì xìng} already contains the question, so it takes no {什么|shén me}, and {姓|xìng} goes with the family name, not with {名字|míng zi}.

questions.stem: Which is the natural answer to "{您|nín}{贵姓|guì xìng}？"
questions.explanation: {姓|xìng} takes only the family name and {叫|jiào} the full name: {我|wǒ}{姓|xìng}{王|Wáng}，{叫|jiào}{王芳|Wáng Fāng}。 {贵|guì} honours the other person, so it's never used about yourself; {姓|xìng}{王芳|Wáng Fāng} puts the full name after {姓|xìng}; and {叫|jiào}{王|Wáng} sounds as if "Wang" were your whole name.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses {位|wèi} correctly?
questions.explanation: {位|wèi} is the polite measure word for other people: {那|nà}{位|wèi}{先生|xiān sheng} (that gentleman). It's never used about yourself ({我|wǒ}{是|shì}{学生|xué sheng}), and never for things or animals: {一|yì}{本|běn}{书|shū}, {两|liǎng}{只|zhī}{猫|māo}.

questions.stem: Read the notice: "{第一|dì yī}{名|míng}：{王芳|Wáng Fāng}　{第二|dì èr}{名|míng}：{李明|Lǐ Míng}　{第三|dì sān}{名|míng}：{安娜|Ān nà}" Who came second?
choices: nobody: it's a list of names
questions.explanation: {名|míng} after an ordinal counts places in a ranking: {第二|dì èr}{名|míng} is second place, Li Ming. Wang Fang was {第一|dì yī}{名|míng} (first) and Anna {第三|dì sān}{名|míng} (third).

questions.stem: Which is the doubled form of {介绍|jiè shào}, "introduce a little"?
choices: {介绍一介绍|jiè shào yi jiè shào}
questions.explanation: A two-syllable verb doubles as a whole word, ABAB: {介绍介绍|jiè shào jiè shào}, the same as {介绍|jiè shào}{一下|yí xià}. AABB ({介介绍绍|jiè jiè shào shào}) is the pattern for adjectives, and the A一A form ({看|kàn}{一|yi}{看|kàn}) is only for one-syllable verbs.

questions.stem: Which verb can't be doubled to mean "do it a little"?
questions.explanation: Only actions done on purpose double: {看看|kàn kan} (have a look), {问问|wèn wen} (ask), {想想|xiǎng xiang} (think it over). {喜欢|xǐ huan} is a state, liking, so {喜欢喜欢|xǐ huan xǐ huan} is wrong, like {是是|shì shì} and {有有|yǒu yǒu}.

questions.stem: Type the Chinese for "oneself", in pinyin with its tones or in characters: ___
questions.explanation: "Oneself" is 自己 zì jǐ (type zi4 ji3): {我|wǒ}{自己|zì jǐ} (myself), {介绍|jiè shào}{自己|zì jǐ} (introduce oneself). Both syllables keep their tones.

questions.stem: Match each character to its meaning.
questions.explanation: 姓 has 女 + 生 (born); 位 has 亻 (person); 自 began as a drawing of a nose; 介 is the "between" of {介绍|jiè shào}; 爷 has 父 (father) on top. "Already" is 已, the look-alike of 己, taught in lesson 18.

questions.stem: What is the pinyin of 姓 (family name)?
questions.explanation: 姓 is xìng, falling (fourth tone), with the back nasal -ng. {星期|xīng qī} has xīng (first tone), and {名|míng} rises.

questions.stem: Which pinyin is right for 爷爷 (grandpa)?
questions.explanation: 爷爷 is yé ye: a rising tone, then a light neutral syllable, like other doubled family words ({爸爸|bà ba}, {奶奶|nǎi nai}).

questions.stem: Which character completes {自|zì} ___ (zì jǐ, oneself)?
questions.explanation: Oneself is 自己, with 己 open at the top left. 已 (half closed) is "already", in {已经|yǐ jīng} (lesson 18); 巳 (closed) is a rare character for dates; 几 is "how many".

questions.stem: Which component do 爷 (grandfather) and 爸 (dad) share?
questions.explanation: Both have 父 (father) on top, their radical: 爸 = 父 + 巴 (the sound), {=爷 = 父 + 卩=}. The traditional form of {=爷=}, {+爷+}, has 耶 under 父.

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker's family name?
questions.explanation: You heard {我|wǒ}{姓|xìng}{李|Lǐ}，{叫|jiào}{李明|Lǐ Míng}: the family name, after {姓|xìng}, is Li. {李明|Lǐ Míng} is the full name and {明|Míng} the given name.

questions.stem: Listen. Where would you most likely hear this?
choices: at the door of a restaurant
questions.explanation: You heard {您好|nín hǎo}！{几|jǐ}{位|wèi}？ (Hello! How many of you?): a waiter's first question. {位|wèi} is the polite measure word for people, so {几|jǐ}{位|wèi} counts guests.

questions.stem: Listen. What are you asked to do?
questions.explanation: You heard {请|qǐng}{你|nǐ}{介绍介绍|jiè shào jiè shào}{你|nǐ}{自己|zì jǐ}: please tell us a little about yourself. {自己|zì jǐ} is "oneself", and the doubled verb makes the request light.

questions.stem: Listen to the question. Which is the best reply?
questions.explanation: The question was {您|nín}{贵姓|guì xìng}？ (your family name, please?). Answer with {姓|xìng} + family name: {我|wǒ}{姓|xìng}{张|Zhāng}. {贵|guì} is never used about yourself; {我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo} answers "how are you?".

questions.stem: Read: "{大家|dà jiā}{好|hǎo}！{我|wǒ}{姓|xìng}{陈|Chén}，{叫|jiào}{陈小雨|Chén Xiǎo yǔ}，{是|shì}{大学生|dà xué shēng}。{我|wǒ}{爷爷|yé ye}{奶奶|nǎi nai}{住|zhù}{在|zài}{北京|Běi jīng}，{外公|wài gōng}{外婆|wài pó}{住|zhù}{在|zài}{上海|Shàng hǎi}。{这|zhè}{位|wèi}{是|shì}{我们|wǒ men}{的|de}{新|xīn}{老师|lǎo shī}，{她|tā}{姓|xìng}{张|Zhāng}，{叫|jiào}{张文|Zhāng Wén}，{是|shì}{北京|Běi jīng}{人|rén}。{她|tā}{爷爷|yé ye}{也|yě}{是|shì}{老师|lǎo shī}。{张|Zhāng}{老师|lǎo shī}{说|shuō}：“{请|qǐng}{大家|dà jiā}{介绍|jiè shào}{介绍|jiè shào}{自己|zì jǐ}。”{我|wǒ}{也|yě}{给|gěi}{大家|dà jiā}{介绍|jiè shào}{一下|yí xià}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{好|hǎo}{朋友|péng you}{王芳|Wáng Fāng}。" Where do Xiaoyu's mother's parents live?
questions.explanation: Her mother's parents are {外公|wài gōng} and {外婆|wài pó}, and they live in Shanghai ({上海|Shàng hǎi}). {爷爷|yé ye} and {奶奶|nǎi nai}, in Beijing, are her father's parents.

questions.stem: Read: "{大家|dà jiā}{好|hǎo}！{我|wǒ}{姓|xìng}{陈|Chén}，{叫|jiào}{陈小雨|Chén Xiǎo yǔ}，{是|shì}{大学生|dà xué shēng}。{我|wǒ}{爷爷|yé ye}{奶奶|nǎi nai}{住|zhù}{在|zài}{北京|Běi jīng}，{外公|wài gōng}{外婆|wài pó}{住|zhù}{在|zài}{上海|Shàng hǎi}。{这|zhè}{位|wèi}{是|shì}{我们|wǒ men}{的|de}{新|xīn}{老师|lǎo shī}，{她|tā}{姓|xìng}{张|Zhāng}，{叫|jiào}{张文|Zhāng Wén}，{是|shì}{北京|Běi jīng}{人|rén}。{她|tā}{爷爷|yé ye}{也|yě}{是|shì}{老师|lǎo shī}。{张|Zhāng}{老师|lǎo shī}{说|shuō}：“{请|qǐng}{大家|dà jiā}{介绍|jiè shào}{介绍|jiè shào}{自己|zì jǐ}。”{我|wǒ}{也|yě}{给|gěi}{大家|dà jiā}{介绍|jiè shào}{一下|yí xià}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{好|hǎo}{朋友|péng you}{王芳|Wáng Fāng}。" Which is true of the new teacher?
questions.explanation: {她|tā}{姓|xìng}{张|Zhāng}，{叫|jiào}{张文|Zhāng Wén}: Zhang is the family name and Wen the given name. She is from Beijing, and her grandfather is a teacher too ({也|yě}{是|shì}{老师|lǎo shī}).

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese.
questions.prompt: Let me introduce you (to someone).
questions.explanation: {给|gěi} + the people being introduced comes before the verb, and {一下|yí xià} after it: {我|wǒ}{给|gěi}{你们|nǐ men}{介绍|jiè shào}{一下|yí xià}。 {位|wèi} isn't needed: it would go with a person, as in {这|zhè}{位|wèi}{是|shì}….

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese.
questions.prompt: My family name is Li; my name is Li Ming.
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{姓|xìng}{李|Lǐ}，{叫|jiào}{李明|Lǐ Míng}。 {姓|xìng} + family name, then {叫|jiào} + full name. {贵|guì} belongs only in the question {您|nín}{贵姓|guì xìng}？

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {姓名|xìng míng}, full name: a falling fourth tone, then a rising second (4+2). Both syllables end in the back nasal -ng.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {自己|zì jǐ}, oneself: a falling fourth tone, then a low third (4+3). The z syllable has the buzzing vowel; jǐ has a real "ee".

questions.stem: Which sentence means "He's tall."?
questions.explanation: A topic-comment sentence: {他|tā} (topic), then {个子|gè zi}{很|hěn}{高|gāo} (height very tall). No {是|shì} before an adjective comment; people are {高|gāo}, not {长|cháng}; and {很|hěn} goes right before the adjective.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
choices: {她|tā}{有|yǒu}{很|hěn}{大大|dà dà}{的|de}{眼睛|yǎn jing}。
{她|tā}{的|de}{眼睛|yǎn jing}{不|bú}{大大|dà dà}{的|de}。
{她|tā}{的|de}{眼睛|yǎn jing}{非常|fēi cháng}{大大|dà dà}{的|de}。
questions.explanation: A doubled adjective already says "very", so it takes no {很|hěn}, {非常|fēi cháng} or {不|bù}: {她|tā}{的|de}{眼睛|yǎn jing}{大大|dà dà}{的|de} (her eyes are nice and big). For "not big", use the plain adjective: {不|bú}{大|dà}.

questions.stem: What is the doubled form of {漂亮|piào liang} (pretty)?
questions.explanation: Two-syllable adjectives double each syllable in place, AABB: {漂漂亮亮|piào piào liàng liàng}{的|de}, and the light liang gets its tone back. ABAB ({漂亮漂亮|piào liang piào liang}) is the pattern for verbs, as in {介绍介绍|jiè shào jiè shào}.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese.
questions.prompt: This top is too long.
questions.explanation: {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}{太|tài}{长|cháng}{了|le}。 {这|zhè} + measure word {件|jiàn} + noun, then {太|tài}…{了|le} round the adjective. Clothes are long ({长|cháng}); {高|gāo} is for people and buildings.

questions.stem: Your friend's grandmother is visiting. Which question is a kind greeting to her?
questions.explanation: {您|nín}{身体|shēn tǐ}{好|hǎo}{吗|ma}？ (How are you keeping?) asks kindly about an older person's health: {身体|shēn tǐ} is "body" and "health". The others ask about height and eyes, odd things to ask a guest.

questions.stem: Read: "{我|wǒ}{哥哥|gē ge}{今年|jīn nián}{二十五|èr shí wǔ}{岁|suì}，{个子|gè zi}{很|hěn}{高|gāo}，{一|yì}{米|mǐ}{八|bā}{五|wǔ}。{他|tā}{女朋友|nǚ péng you}{个子|gè zi}{不|bù}{高|gāo}，{一|yì}{米|mǐ}{六|liù}{五|wǔ}，{头发|tóu fa}{长长|cháng cháng}{的|de}，{眼睛|yǎn jing}{大大|dà dà}{的|de}，{很|hěn}{漂亮|piào liang}。{他们|tā men}{都|dōu}{很|hěn}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{看|kàn}{电影|diàn yǐng}。{我|wǒ}{也|yě}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{她|tā}。{我|wǒ}{爷爷|yé ye}{今年|jīn nián}{八十|bā shí}{岁|suì}{了|le}，{身体|shēn tǐ}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}，{很|hěn}{少|shǎo}{生病|shēng bìng}。{他|tā}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{看|kàn}{书|shū}，{也|yě}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{做饭|zuò fàn}。" Who is taller, the brother or his girlfriend?
questions.explanation: The brother is {一|yì}{米|mǐ}{八|bā}{五|wǔ} (1.85 m) and his girlfriend {一|yì}{米|mǐ}{六|liù}{五|wǔ} (1.65 m), so he's taller; the text also says she isn't tall ({个子|gè zi}{不|bù}{高|gāo}). Heights are said in metres with {米|mǐ}, without {是|shì}.

questions.stem: Type the Chinese for "eye", in pinyin with its tones or in characters: ___
questions.explanation: "Eye" is 眼睛 yǎn jing (type yan3 jing5 or yan3 jing): a third tone and a light syllable. Both characters have 目 (eye) on the left.

questions.stem: Match each character to its meaning.
questions.explanation: 头 head, 手 hand, 眼 eye (with 目), 身 body, 长 long. "Tall" is 高, from {高兴|gāo xìng}, which you could already write.

questions.stem: How is 长 read in {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}{很|hěn}长 (this top is long)?
questions.explanation: "Long" is cháng, rising, with ch. The same character read zhǎng means "to grow" (HSK 3: {长大|zhǎng dà}); {唱|chàng} (to sing) and {张|Zhāng} (a family name) are other characters.

questions.stem: What is the pinyin of 身体 (body; health)?
questions.explanation: 身体 is shēn tǐ: level, then low. {身|shēn} ends in front -n, not -ng ({生|shēng} in {学生|xué sheng} has -ng).

questions.stem: Which character completes {身|shēn} ___ (shēn tǐ, body)?
questions.explanation: Body is 身体, with {=体 = 亻 + 本=} (the traditional form, {+体+}, is quite different). 休 (rest, in {休息|xiū xi}) has 木 without the short bottom stroke; 什 is the shén of {什么|shén me}; 本 alone has no 亻.

questions.stem: Which character completes {很|hěn} ___ (hěn cháng, very long)?
questions.explanation: Long is 长: four strokes, the third flicking up at the bottom. 张 (a family name) has 弓 on the left of a 长; 场 (lesson 08) and 头 (head) are different characters. 长 is one to know by hand.

questions.stem: Which radical do 眼 and 睛 share?
questions.explanation: Both have 目 (eye) on the left, as 看 and 睡 do. 日 (sun) has only one stroke inside; 青 is the sound part of 睛, and 艮 the right side of 眼.

questions.stem: Listen. What did you hear about him?
questions.explanation: You heard {他|tā}{个子|gè zi}{很|hěn}{高|gāo}: he's tall. "Short" would be {个子|gè zi}{不|bù}{高|gāo}; health is {身体|shēn tǐ}, hands {手|shǒu}.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker say about her grandmother?
questions.explanation: You heard {我|wǒ}{奶奶|nǎi nai}{身体|shēn tǐ}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}: my grandma is in good health. {身体|shēn tǐ}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo} is about health, not looks.

questions.stem: Listen. Which description did you hear?

audio.text: 她的头发长长的，眼睛大大的。

questions.explanation: You heard {她|tā}{的|de}{头发|tóu fa}{长长|cháng cháng}{的|de}，{眼睛|yǎn jing}{大大|dà dà}{的|de}: her hair is long and her eyes are big. Both adjectives are doubled for a vivid description.

questions.stem: Listen to the question. Which is the best reply?
questions.explanation: The question was {你|nǐ}{多|duō}{高|gāo}？ (How tall are you?), {多|duō} + adjective like {多大|duō dà}. Answer with a height: {我|wǒ}{一|yì}{米|mǐ}{七|qī} (1.70 m). {二十|èr shí}{岁|suì} answers {多大|duō dà}, and {很|hěn}{好|hǎo} answers "how are you?".

questions.stem: Read: "{我|wǒ}{哥哥|gē ge}{今年|jīn nián}{二十五|èr shí wǔ}{岁|suì}，{个子|gè zi}{很|hěn}{高|gāo}，{一|yì}{米|mǐ}{八|bā}{五|wǔ}。{他|tā}{女朋友|nǚ péng you}{个子|gè zi}{不|bù}{高|gāo}，{一|yì}{米|mǐ}{六|liù}{五|wǔ}，{头发|tóu fa}{长长|cháng cháng}{的|de}，{眼睛|yǎn jing}{大大|dà dà}{的|de}，{很|hěn}{漂亮|piào liang}。{他们|tā men}{都|dōu}{很|hěn}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{看|kàn}{电影|diàn yǐng}。{我|wǒ}{也|yě}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{她|tā}。{我|wǒ}{爷爷|yé ye}{今年|jīn nián}{八十|bā shí}{岁|suì}{了|le}，{身体|shēn tǐ}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}，{很|hěn}{少|shǎo}{生病|shēng bìng}。{他|tā}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{看|kàn}{书|shū}，{也|yě}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{做饭|zuò fàn}。" Which is true?
questions.explanation: {头发|tóu fa}{长长|cháng cháng}{的|de} is said of the girlfriend: she has long hair, and she isn't tall ({个子|gè zi}{不|bù}{高|gāo}). The brother is 1.85 m: {一|yì}{米|mǐ}{八|bā}{五|wǔ}.

questions.stem: Read: "{我|wǒ}{哥哥|gē ge}{今年|jīn nián}{二十五|èr shí wǔ}{岁|suì}，{个子|gè zi}{很|hěn}{高|gāo}，{一|yì}{米|mǐ}{八|bā}{五|wǔ}。{他|tā}{女朋友|nǚ péng you}{个子|gè zi}{不|bù}{高|gāo}，{一|yì}{米|mǐ}{六|liù}{五|wǔ}，{头发|tóu fa}{长长|cháng cháng}{的|de}，{眼睛|yǎn jing}{大大|dà dà}{的|de}，{很|hěn}{漂亮|piào liang}。{他们|tā men}{都|dōu}{很|hěn}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{看|kàn}{电影|diàn yǐng}。{我|wǒ}{也|yě}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{她|tā}。{我|wǒ}{爷爷|yé ye}{今年|jīn nián}{八十|bā shí}{岁|suì}{了|le}，{身体|shēn tǐ}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}，{很|hěn}{少|shǎo}{生病|shēng bìng}。{他|tā}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{看|kàn}{书|shū}，{也|yě}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{做饭|zuò fàn}。" What do we learn about Grandpa?
questions.explanation: {身体|shēn tǐ}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}，{很|hěn}{少|shǎo}{生病|shēng bìng}: he's in good health and seldom ill ({很|hěn}{少|shǎo} + verb = seldom). He's eighty ({八十|bā shí}), not eighteen ({十八|shí bā}), and he likes cooking.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese.
questions.prompt: My younger sister has big eyes.
questions.explanation: A topic-comment sentence: {我|wǒ}{妹妹|mèi mei} (topic), {眼睛|yǎn jing}{很|hěn}{大|dà} (comment). English "has" isn't translated: adding {有|yǒu} before {眼睛|yǎn jing} is a common mistake.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {身体|shēn tǐ}, body; health: a high level first tone, then a low third (1+3).

questions.stem: Listen. Which tone is it?
questions.explanation: {高|gāo}, tall: the first tone, high and level.

questions.stem: Which sentence describes what he has on: "He's wearing a red top."?
choices: {他|tā}{在|zài}{穿|chuān}{红色|hóng sè}{的|de}{衣服|yī fu}。
{他|tā}{着|zhe}{穿|chuān}{红色|hóng sè}{的|de}{衣服|yī fu}。
{他|tā}{穿|chuān}{红色|hóng sè}{着|zhe}{的|de}{衣服|yī fu}。
{他|tā}{穿|chuān}{着|zhe}{红色|hóng sè}{的|de}{衣服|yī fu}。
questions.explanation: {着|zhe} goes straight after the verb for a lasting state: {穿|chuān}{着|zhe}, having it on. {在|zài}{穿|chuān} is the action of putting it on ("he's getting dressed in red"), and {着|zhe} never comes before the verb or after the colour.

questions.stem: What does "{电视|diàn shì}{开|kāi}{着|zhe}。" mean?
questions.explanation: {开|kāi} (switch on) + {着|zhe}: the result lasts, so the TV is on. "Switch it on" would be {开|kāi}{电视|diàn shì}{吧|ba}, and the action in progress {我|wǒ}{在|zài}{开|kāi}{电视|diàn shì}.

questions.stem: How do you usually say "The TV isn't on."?
questions.explanation: The negative of a {着|zhe} state is {没|méi} + verb, usually without {着|zhe}: {电视|diàn shì}{没|méi}{开|kāi}. {不|bù}{开|kāi}{了|le} would mean "(I) won't switch it on any more".

questions.stem: You're saying what you'll wear tomorrow. Which sentence is right?
choices: {明天|míng tiān}{我|wǒ}{穿|chuān}{着|zhe}{白色|bái sè}{的|de}{衣服|yī fu}。
{明天|míng tiān}{我|wǒ}{穿|chuān}{白色|bái sè}{的|de}{衣服|yī fu}。
{我|wǒ}{穿|chuān}{白色|bái sè}{的|de}{衣服|yī fu}{明天|míng tiān}。
{明天|míng tiān}{我|wǒ}{在|zài}{穿|chuān}{白色|bái sè}{的|de}{衣服|yī fu}。
questions.explanation: For a plan, use the plain verb: {明天|míng tiān}{我|wǒ}{穿|chuān}{白色|bái sè}{的|de}{衣服|yī fu}。 {着|zhe} describes a state that is there now, so it isn't a future; {在|zài} + verb is an action in progress; and the time word goes before the verb, not at the end.

questions.stem: In a shop you want the black one. What do you say?
questions.explanation: Colour + {的|de} stands for the whole thing when the noun is clear: {黑色|hēi sè}{的|de}, "the black one". {的|de} comes after the colour, and {黑色|hēi sè} is one word, not split by {的|de}.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese.
questions.prompt: The black one is mine.
questions.explanation: {黑色|hēi sè}{的|de}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{的|de}。 Two {的|de} phrases: {黑色|hēi sè}{的|de} (the black one) and {我|wǒ}{的|de} (mine), linked by {是|shì}. {我|wǒ}{的|de}{是|shì}{黑色|hēi sè}{的|de} ("mine is the black one") is right too. {着|zhe} needs a verb in front of it.

questions.stem: Type the Chinese for "colour", in pinyin with its tones or in characters: ___
questions.explanation: "Colour" is 颜色 yán sè (type yan2 se4). Ask about it with {什么|shén me}{颜色|yán sè}？

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explanation: {红色|hóng sè} red, {白色|bái sè} white, {黑色|hēi sè} black, {绿色|lǜ sè} green, {裤子|kù zi} trousers. Yellow is {黄色|huáng sè}, an HSK 3 word.

questions.stem: What is the pinyin of 绿 (green)?
questions.explanation: 绿 is lǜ: the ü sound (written with two dots after l) and a falling tone. lù, without the dots, is another syllable: {路|lù}, road (lesson 07). Type lv4.

questions.stem: Which pinyin is right for 手表 (wristwatch)?
questions.explanation: 手表 is shǒu biǎo, two third tones: in speech the first rises (said shóu biǎo), but it's written with both third tones.

questions.stem: Which character completes ___ {子|zi} (kù zi, trousers)?
questions.explanation: Trousers are 裤子: 衤 (clothing) + 库, which gives the sound. 库 alone is a storehouse; 视 (in {电视|diàn shì}) has 礻, with one stroke fewer; 被 (a quilt, HSK 3) has 衤 too, but a different right side.

questions.stem: Which character has the clothing radical 衤?
questions.explanation: 裤 (trousers) has 衤, five strokes, with two short strokes at the bottom right. 视 has 礻, the look-alike with four; 红 has 纟 (silk), and 黑 is its own radical.

questions.stem: Which two characters share the silk radical 纟?
questions.explanation: 红 (red) and 绿 (green) both have 纟 on the left: dyed silk gave many colour words their radical. 颜 has 页, 表 衣, 裤 衤, and 黑 and 色 are their own radicals; {=着=} is filed under 目 (its traditional form, {+着+}, under 艹).

questions.stem: Listen. What is he wearing?
questions.explanation: You heard {他|tā}{穿|chuān}{着|zhe}{白色|bái sè}{的|de}{衣服|yī fu}: he's wearing a white top. Trousers would be {裤子|kù zi}.
