questions.stem: Listen to the question. Which is the best reply?
questions.explanation: The question was {你|nǐ}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{什么|shén me}{颜色|yán sè}？ (What colour do you like?). Answer with a colour: {我|wǒ}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{绿色|lǜ sè}.

questions.stem: Listen. What is Grandma doing?
questions.explanation: You heard {奶奶|nǎi nai}{坐|zuò}{着|zhe}{看|kàn}{电视|diàn shì}: verb + {着|zhe} + verb, the first saying how the second is done: watching TV sitting down.

questions.stem: Listen. Whose is the watch?
questions.explanation: You heard {这|zhè}{块|kuài}{手表|shǒu biǎo}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{爷爷|yé ye}{的|de}: this watch is my grandpa's. {爷爷|yé ye}{的|de} is a {的|de} phrase standing for "grandpa's (watch)".

questions.stem: Read the message: "{王芳|Wáng Fāng}，{你好|nǐ hǎo}！{明天|míng tiān}{下午|xià wǔ}{三|sān}{点|diǎn}{我们|wǒ men}{在|zài}{书店|shū diàn}{见|jiàn}{吧|ba}。{我|wǒ}{哥哥|gē ge}{也|yě}{来|lái}，{他|tā}{穿|chuān}{黑色|hēi sè}{的|de}{衣服|yī fu}{和|hé}{白色|bái sè}{的|de}{裤子|kù zi}。{我|wǒ}{穿|chuān}{红色|hóng sè}{的|de}{衣服|yī fu}，{你|nǐ}{呢|ne}？{你|nǐ}{的|de}{书|shū}{在|zài}{我|wǒ}{这儿|zhèr}，{书|shū}{上|shàng}{写|xiě}{着|zhe}{你|nǐ}{的|de}{名字|míng zi}。{我|wǒ}{现在|xiàn zài}{在|zài}{家|jiā}，{电视|diàn shì}{开|kāi}{着|zhe}，{哥哥|gē ge}{坐|zuò}{着|zhe}{看|kàn}{电视|diàn shì}{呢|ne}。{明天|míng tiān}{见|jiàn}！{安娜|Ān nà}" What will the brother wear?
choices: a white top and black trousers
a green watch and white trousers
a black top and white trousers
questions.explanation: {黑色|hēi sè}{的|de}{衣服|yī fu} is a black top and {白色|bái sè}{的|de}{裤子|kù zi} white trousers. The message uses plain {穿|chuān}, not {穿|chuān}{着|zhe}, because it's about tomorrow.

questions.stem: Read the message: "{王芳|Wáng Fāng}，{你好|nǐ hǎo}！{明天|míng tiān}{下午|xià wǔ}{三|sān}{点|diǎn}{我们|wǒ men}{在|zài}{书店|shū diàn}{见|jiàn}{吧|ba}。{我|wǒ}{哥哥|gē ge}{也|yě}{来|lái}，{他|tā}{穿|chuān}{黑色|hēi sè}{的|de}{衣服|yī fu}{和|hé}{白色|bái sè}{的|de}{裤子|kù zi}。{我|wǒ}{穿|chuān}{红色|hóng sè}{的|de}{衣服|yī fu}，{你|nǐ}{呢|ne}？{你|nǐ}{的|de}{书|shū}{在|zài}{我|wǒ}{这儿|zhèr}，{书|shū}{上|shàng}{写|xiě}{着|zhe}{你|nǐ}{的|de}{名字|míng zi}。{我|wǒ}{现在|xiàn zài}{在|zài}{家|jiā}，{电视|diàn shì}{开|kāi}{着|zhe}，{哥哥|gē ge}{坐|zuò}{着|zhe}{看|kàn}{电视|diàn shì}{呢|ne}。{明天|míng tiān}{见|jiàn}！{安娜|Ān nà}" How does Anna know the book is Wang Fang's?
choices: Wang Fang's name is written in it.
Wang Fang is writing in it now.
questions.explanation: {书|shū}{上|shàng}{写|xiě}{着|zhe}{你|nǐ}{的|de}{名字|míng zi}: the name is written in the book, a lasting state ({着|zhe}), not someone writing now. Grandma is watching TV ({坐|zuò}{着|zhe}{看|kàn}{电视|diàn shì}).

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese.
questions.prompt: Grandma is sitting down watching TV.
questions.explanation: {奶奶|nǎi nai}{坐|zuò}{着|zhe}{看|kàn}{电视|diàn shì}。 The first verb + {着|zhe} says how the second action is done. {在|zài} isn't needed: {着|zhe} already describes the scene.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {颜色|yán sè}, colour: a rising second tone, then a falling fourth (2+4).

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {手表|shǒu biǎo}, wristwatch: two third tones (3+3). Third-tone sandhi: you hear 2+3 (shóu biǎo); both answers count.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I get up at seven every day."?
choices: {我|wǒ}{每天|měi tiān}{都|dōu}{七|qī}{点|diǎn}{起床|qǐ chuáng}。
{我|wǒ}{都|dōu}{每天|měi tiān}{七|qī}{点|diǎn}{起床|qǐ chuáng}。
questions.explanation: {每天|měi tiān} is a time phrase, so it goes before the verb, and {都|dōu} comes after it, right before the rest of the predicate: {我|wǒ}{每天|měi tiān}{都|dōu}{七|qī}{点|diǎn}{起床|qǐ chuáng}。 {天|tiān} takes no measure word (not {每|měi}{个|gè}{天|tiān}), and {都|dōu} never comes before the {每|měi} phrase.

questions.stem: Where does {经常|jīng cháng} (often) usually go? {我们|wǒ men} A {在|zài} B {家|jiā} C {吃|chī}{饭|fàn} D。
questions.explanation: A frequency adverb usually goes after the subject and before {在|zài} + place: {我们|wǒ men}{经常|jīng cháng}{在|zài}{家|jiā}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}。 It can't split {在|zài}{家|jiā}, and it never goes at the end as "often" can in English. (After {在|zài}{家|jiā} it's heard too, with {在|zài}{家|jiā} as the setting: "at home, we often…", but A is the usual place.)

questions.stem: Choose the measure word: {每|měi} ___ {人|rén}{都|dōu}{有|yǒu}{自己|zì jǐ}{的|de}{房间|fáng jiān}。
questions.explanation: {每|měi} needs a measure word before most nouns, and people take {个|gè}: {每|měi}{个|gè}{人|rén} (everyone). {本|běn} is for books, {件|jiàn} for clothes and matters, {块|kuài} for pieces (and watches).

questions.stem: What does "{我|wǒ}{有时|yǒu shí}{在|zài}{家|jiā}{做饭|zuò fàn}，{有时|yǒu shí}{在|zài}{饭店|fàn diàn}{吃|chī}。" mean?
choices: Sometimes I cook at home, sometimes I eat in a restaurant.
I often work in a restaurant.
questions.explanation: {有时|yǒu shí}…，{有时|yǒu shí}… is "sometimes…, sometimes…": two different habits. "Always" would be {每天|měi tiān}{都|dōu}, "often" {经常|jīng cháng}.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese.
questions.prompt: Everyone has their own name.
questions.explanation: {每|měi}{个|gè}{人|rén}{都|dōu}{有|yǒu}{自己|zì jǐ}{的|de}{名字|míng zi}。 {每|měi} + measure word + noun, then {都|dōu} before the verb; {自己|zì jǐ}{的|de} is "one's own".

questions.stem: Which phrase means "give your hands a quick wash"?
questions.explanation: With a verb + object, only the verb doubles (AAB): {洗洗|xǐ xi}{手|shǒu}. The object still follows the verb, and doubling the whole phrase ({洗手洗手|xǐ shǒu xǐ shǒu}) is wrong.

questions.stem: Type the Chinese for "often", in pinyin with its tones or in characters: ___
questions.explanation: "Often" is 经常 jīng cháng (type jing1 chang2): level, then rising. It goes before the verb: {他|tā}{经常|jīng cháng}{做饭|zuò fàn}.

questions.stem: Match each character to its meaning.
questions.explanation: 丈 and 夫 make {丈夫|zhàng fu} (husband); 妻 has 女; 每 has 母; 经 has 纟 (its first meaning was the warp of a cloth); 洗 has 氵 (water). "Day" is 天.

questions.stem: Which pinyin is right for 女孩儿 (girl)?
questions.explanation: 女孩儿 is nǚ háir: 儿 adds an -r to the syllable before it and isn't a syllable of its own. In speech the i drops (said nǚ hár). After n, ü keeps its two dots.

questions.stem: What is the pinyin of 妻子 (wife)?
questions.explanation: 妻子 is qī zi: a level first tone, then a light zi, as in {孩子|hái zi}. q is a puffed sound with the tongue flat; j has no puff.

questions.stem: Which character completes ___ {夫|fu} (zhàng fu, husband)?
questions.explanation: Husband is 丈夫: 丈 has only three strokes (horizontal, left-falling, right-falling). 大 and 太 are its look-alikes (big, too), and 文 is the wén of {中文|Zhōng wén}.

questions.stem: Which of these is 天 (tiān, day)?
questions.explanation: In 天 the extra horizontal sits on top and doesn't cross; in 夫 (man, husband) the left-falling stroke crosses both horizontals. 大 has one horizontal, and 太 has a dot underneath.

questions.stem: What does the radical on the left of 洗 (to wash) mean?
questions.explanation: 洗 has 氵, the three drops of water, as 汉, 没 and 漂 do. Ice is 冫 (two drops, in {冷|lěng}), a person 亻, silk 纟. The right side, 先, gives the sound.

questions.stem: Listen. Who is a doctor?
questions.explanation: You heard {我|wǒ}{妻子|qī zi}{是|shì}{医生|yī shēng}: my wife is a doctor. Husband is {丈夫|zhàng fu}.

questions.stem: Listen. Which is true?

audio.text: 他们有两个孩子，一个男孩儿，一个女孩儿。

choices: They have a boy and a girl.
questions.explanation: You heard {两|liǎng}{个|gè}{孩子|hái zi}，{一|yí}{个|gè}{男孩儿|nán háir}，{一|yí}{个|gè}{女孩儿|nǚ háir}: two children, one boy and one girl.

questions.stem: Listen. How often does the speaker's mum do the washing?
questions.explanation: You heard {我|wǒ}{妈妈|mā ma}{每天|měi tiān}{都|dōu}{洗|xǐ}{衣服|yī fu}: every day. Often is {经常|jīng cháng}, sometimes {有时|yǒu shí}, seldom {很|hěn}{少|shǎo}.

questions.stem: Listen to the question. Which is the best reply?
questions.explanation: The question was {星期天|xīng qī tiān}{你|nǐ}{经常|jīng cháng}{做|zuò}{什么|shén me}？ (What do you often do on Sundays?). Answer with the activity: {我|wǒ}{经常|jīng cháng}{去|qù}{看|kàn}{电影|diàn yǐng}.

questions.stem: Read: "{在|zài}{我|wǒ}{家|jiā}，{早上|zǎo shang}{我|wǒ}{丈夫|zhàng fu}{做|zuò}{早饭|zǎo fàn}，{晚上|wǎn shang}{我|wǒ}{做饭|zuò fàn}，{他|tā}{洗|xǐ}{碗|wǎn}。{我|wǒ}{丈夫|zhàng fu}{叫|jiào}{刘东|Liú Dōng}，{他|tā}{每天|měi tiān}{都|dōu}{很|hěn}{忙|máng}，{有时|yǒu shí}{晚上|wǎn shang}{也|yě}{工作|gōng zuò}，{很|hěn}{少|shǎo}{在|zài}{家|jiā}{吃|chī}{晚饭|wǎn fàn}。{我们|wǒ men}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{女孩儿|nǚ háir}，{今年|jīn nián}{六|liù}{岁|suì}，{她|tā}{很|hěn}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{爷爷|yé ye}{奶奶|nǎi nai}。{星期六|xīng qī liù}{我们|wǒ men}{经常|jīng cháng}{去|qù}{看|kàn}{他们|tā men}，{有时|yǒu shí}{星期天|xīng qī tiān}{也|yě}{去|qù}。" ({碗|wǎn}: bowl) Who makes breakfast?
questions.explanation: {早上|zǎo shang}{我|wǒ}{丈夫|zhàng fu}{做|zuò}{早饭|zǎo fàn}: the husband makes breakfast. In the evening the writer cooks and he does the dishes ({洗|xǐ}{碗|wǎn}).

questions.stem: Read: "{在|zài}{我|wǒ}{家|jiā}，{早上|zǎo shang}{我|wǒ}{丈夫|zhàng fu}{做|zuò}{早饭|zǎo fàn}，{晚上|wǎn shang}{我|wǒ}{做饭|zuò fàn}，{他|tā}{洗|xǐ}{碗|wǎn}。{我|wǒ}{丈夫|zhàng fu}{叫|jiào}{刘东|Liú Dōng}，{他|tā}{每天|měi tiān}{都|dōu}{很|hěn}{忙|máng}，{有时|yǒu shí}{晚上|wǎn shang}{也|yě}{工作|gōng zuò}，{很|hěn}{少|shǎo}{在|zài}{家|jiā}{吃|chī}{晚饭|wǎn fàn}。{我们|wǒ men}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{女孩儿|nǚ háir}，{今年|jīn nián}{六|liù}{岁|suì}，{她|tā}{很|hěn}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{爷爷|yé ye}{奶奶|nǎi nai}。{星期六|xīng qī liù}{我们|wǒ men}{经常|jīng cháng}{去|qù}{看|kàn}{他们|tā men}，{有时|yǒu shí}{星期天|xīng qī tiān}{也|yě}{去|qù}。" How often does Liu Dong have dinner at home?
questions.explanation: {很|hěn}{少|shǎo} + verb is "seldom": {很|hěn}{少|shǎo}{在|zài}{家|jiā}{吃|chī}{晚饭|wǎn fàn}. He's busy every day ({每天|měi tiān}{都|dōu}{很|hěn}{忙|máng}) and sometimes works in the evening.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese.
questions.prompt: We often eat at home.
questions.explanation: Subject, frequency adverb, place, verb: {我们|wǒ men}{经常|jīng cháng}{在|zài}{家|jiā}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}。 {每|měi} would need a measure word and {都|dōu}.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {经常|jīng cháng}, often: a high level first tone, then a rising second (1+2).

questions.stem: Listen. Which tone is it?
questions.explanation: {洗|xǐ}, to wash: the third tone, low and dipping. It sounds exactly like the {喜|xǐ} of {喜欢|xǐ huan}.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
choices: {因为|yīn wèi}{我|wǒ}{头|tóu}{疼|téng}，{我|wǒ}{所以|suǒ yǐ}{没|méi}{去|qù}{上课|shàng kè}。
{因为|yīn wèi}{我|wǒ}{头|tóu}{疼|téng}，{所以|suǒ yǐ}{我|wǒ}{没|méi}{去|qù}{上课|shàng kè}。
{所以|suǒ yǐ}{我|wǒ}{头|tóu}{疼|téng}，{因为|yīn wèi}{我|wǒ}{没|méi}{去|qù}{上课|shàng kè}。
{我|wǒ}{没|méi}{去|qù}{上课|shàng kè}，{所以|suǒ yǐ}{因为|yīn wèi}{我|wǒ}{头|tóu}{疼|téng}。
questions.explanation: {因为|yīn wèi} introduces the cause, {所以|suǒ yǐ} the result, and {所以|suǒ yǐ} starts its clause, before the subject: {所以|suǒ yǐ}{我|wǒ}{没|méi}{去|qù}. The third choice swaps cause and result; when the reason comes second, use {因为|yīn wèi} alone, without {所以|suǒ yǐ}.

questions.stem: Complete: {我|wǒ}{今天|jīn tiān}{没|méi}{去|qù}{学校|xué xiào}，___ {我|wǒ}{生病|shēng bìng}{了|le}。
questions.explanation: The result comes first and the reason second, so the reason takes {因为|yīn wèi}: "I didn't go to school today because I'm ill." {所以|suǒ yǐ} would make the illness the result; {和|hé} joins nouns, not clauses.

questions.stem: How do you say "I have a headache."?
questions.explanation: A topic-comment sentence: {我|wǒ} (topic), {头|tóu}{疼|téng} (head aches). The body part comes before {疼|téng}, and {疼|téng} is the verb, so no {是|shì}.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese.
questions.prompt: I have a headache, so I'm taking some medicine.
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{头|tóu}{疼|téng}，{所以|suǒ yǐ}{吃|chī}{药|yào}。 Medicine is usually "eaten" in Chinese: {吃|chī}{药|yào} ({喝|hē}{药|yào} only for medicine you drink). The second clause can drop its subject when it's the same person.

questions.stem: You're too ill to go to class. Which sentence says "I can't go to class today."?
choices: {我|wǒ}{今天|jīn tiān}{不|bú}{会|huì}{去|qù}{上课|shàng kè}。
{我|wǒ}{今天|jīn tiān}{不|bù}{想|xiǎng}{去|qù}{上课|shàng kè}{吗|ma}。
{我|wǒ}{今天|jīn tiān}{不|bù}{能|néng}{去|qù}{上课|shàng kè}。
{我|wǒ}{今天|jīn tiān}{不|bù}{能|néng}{上课|shàng kè}{去|qù}。
questions.explanation: {不|bù}{能|néng} is "can't" because of circumstances, such as being ill: {我|wǒ}{今天|jīn tiān}{不|bù}{能|néng}{去|qù}{上课|shàng kè}。 {不|bú}{会|huì} would mean "won't" or "don't know how"; {去|qù} comes before what you go to do.

questions.stem: What does "{我|wǒ}{有点儿|yǒu diǎnr}{不|bù}{舒服|shū fu}。" mean?
choices: I'm a little tired of this.
questions.explanation: {不|bù}{舒服|shū fu} is "unwell", and {有点儿|yǒu diǎnr} softens it to "a bit", as it does for things you'd rather not have. Tired is {累|lèi}.

questions.stem: Type the Chinese for "tired", in pinyin with its tone or in characters: ___
questions.explanation: "Tired" is 累 lèi (type lei4), falling. It also means "tiring": {这|zhè}{个|gè}{工作|gōng zuò}{很|hěn}{累|lèi}.

questions.stem: Match each character to its meaning.
questions.explanation: 因 is 大 inside 囗; 所 is 户 + 斤; 疼 has 疒 (illness); 药 has 艹 (herbs); 店 has 广 (a building). "Tired" is 累.

questions.stem: What is the pinyin of 舒服 (comfortable, well)?
questions.explanation: 舒服 is shū fu: sh with the tongue curled back, a level first tone, then a light fu.

questions.stem: 药 (medicine) sounds exactly like which word?
questions.explanation: 药 is yào, the same syllable and tone as {要|yào}. In {你|nǐ}{要|yào}{吃|chī}{药|yào} you hear yào twice: "you should" and "medicine".

questions.stem: Which character completes {因|yīn} ___ (yīn wèi, because)?
questions.explanation: Because is 因为. {=为 has four strokes: the dot, the long left-falling stroke, the turning hook and the inner dot last. 办 (to do, HSK 3) has two dots outside, 力 (strength) none=}; 头 is "head". {=为=} is one to know by hand (its traditional form is {+为+}).

questions.stem: Which radical do 疼 (to ache) and 病 (ill) share?
questions.explanation: 疒 is the illness radical, a 广 with two extra strokes on the left. 广 alone (a building) is the radical of 店; 冬 is the sound part of 疼.

questions.stem: Which HSK 1 word has the character 店 (shop)?
questions.explanation: {饭店|fàn diàn} (restaurant) ends in 店, like {商店|shāng diàn}, {书店|shū diàn} and now {药店|yào diàn}. {电视|diàn shì} and {点|diǎn} have the same sound or close to it, but other characters.

questions.stem: Listen. How does the speaker feel?
choices: a headache, and a bit tired
questions.explanation: You heard {我|wǒ}{头|tóu}{疼|téng}，{也|yě}{有点儿|yǒu diǎnr}{累|lèi}: I have a headache, and I'm also a bit tired.

questions.stem: Listen. What is outside the school?
questions.explanation: You heard {学校|xué xiào}{外边|wài bian}{有|yǒu}{一|yì}{家|jiā}{药店|yào diàn}: there's a pharmacy outside the school. A bookshop is {书店|shū diàn}, a restaurant {饭店|fàn diàn}, a hospital {医院|yī yuàn}.

questions.stem: Listen. Why is he resting at home?

audio.text: 因为今天很冷，所以他在家休息。

questions.explanation: You heard {因为|yīn wèi}{今天|jīn tiān}{很|hěn}{冷|lěng}，{所以|suǒ yǐ}{他|tā}{在|zài}{家|jiā}{休息|xiū xi}: the cause after {因为|yīn wèi} is the cold weather.

questions.stem: Listen to the question. Which is the best reply?
questions.explanation: The question was {你|nǐ}{哪儿|nǎr}{不|bù}{舒服|shū fu}？ (Where don't you feel well? What's wrong?). Answer with the part that hurts: {我|wǒ}{头|tóu}{疼|téng}. {我|wǒ}{在|zài}{家|jiā} answers "where are you?".

questions.stem: Read the message: "{王|Wáng}{老师|lǎo shī}：{您好|nín hǎo}！{我|wǒ}{是|shì}{安娜|Ān nà}。{因为|yīn wèi}{我|wǒ}{生病|shēng bìng}{了|le}，{头|tóu}{很|hěn}{疼|téng}，{所以|suǒ yǐ}{今天|jīn tiān}{不|bù}{能|néng}{去|qù}{上课|shàng kè}{了|le}。{医生|yī shēng}{说|shuō}{我|wǒ}{要|yào}{多|duō}{休息|xiū xi}，{一|yì}{天|tiān}{吃|chī}{三|sān}{次|cì}{药|yào}。{我|wǒ}{的|de}{同学|tóng xué}{李明|Lǐ Míng}{也|yě}{不|bù}{舒服|shū fu}：{他|tā}{昨天|zuó tiān}{晚上|wǎn shang}{一|yī}{点|diǎn}{睡觉|shuì jiào}，{所以|suǒ yǐ}{今天|jīn tiān}{很|hěn}{累|lèi}。{我们|wǒ men}{明天|míng tiān}{想|xiǎng}{去|qù}{上课|shàng kè}。{真|zhēn}{对不起|duì bu qǐ}，{谢谢|xiè xie}{您|nín}！{安娜|Ān nà}" ({次|cì}: times) Why is Anna writing?
choices: to say she can't come to class because she's ill
to ask the teacher to see a doctor
questions.explanation: {因为|yīn wèi}{我|wǒ}{生病|shēng bìng}{了|le}，{所以|suǒ yǐ}{今天|jīn tiān}{不|bù}{能|néng}{去|qù}{上课|shàng kè}{了|le}: she's ill, so she can't come to class today. The doctor told her to rest more ({要|yào}{多|duō}{休息|xiū xi}).

questions.stem: Read the message: "{王|Wáng}{老师|lǎo shī}：{您好|nín hǎo}！{我|wǒ}{是|shì}{安娜|Ān nà}。{因为|yīn wèi}{我|wǒ}{生病|shēng bìng}{了|le}，{头|tóu}{很|hěn}{疼|téng}，{所以|suǒ yǐ}{今天|jīn tiān}{不|bù}{能|néng}{去|qù}{上课|shàng kè}{了|le}。{医生|yī shēng}{说|shuō}{我|wǒ}{要|yào}{多|duō}{休息|xiū xi}，{一|yì}{天|tiān}{吃|chī}{三|sān}{次|cì}{药|yào}。{我|wǒ}{的|de}{同学|tóng xué}{李明|Lǐ Míng}{也|yě}{不|bù}{舒服|shū fu}：{他|tā}{昨天|zuó tiān}{晚上|wǎn shang}{一|yī}{点|diǎn}{睡觉|shuì jiào}，{所以|suǒ yǐ}{今天|jīn tiān}{很|hěn}{累|lèi}。{我们|wǒ men}{明天|míng tiān}{想|xiǎng}{去|qù}{上课|shàng kè}。{真|zhēn}{对不起|duì bu qǐ}，{谢谢|xiè xie}{您|nín}！{安娜|Ān nà}" ({次|cì}: times) Why is Li Ming tired?
questions.explanation: {他|tā}{昨天|zuó tiān}{晚上|wǎn shang}{一|yī}{点|diǎn}{睡觉|shuì jiào}，{所以|suǒ yǐ}{今天|jīn tiān}{很|hěn}{累|lèi}: he went to bed at one in the morning, and {所以|suǒ yǐ} introduces the result, being tired. Anna is the one who is ill.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese.
questions.prompt: Because I'm tired, I'm resting at home.
questions.explanation: {因为|yīn wèi}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{累|lèi}，{所以|suǒ yǐ}{在|zài}{家|jiā}{休息|xiū xi}。 {因为|yīn wèi} may also follow the subject ({我|wǒ}{因为|yīn wèi}{很|hěn}{累|lèi}…). {所以|suǒ yǐ} starts the second clause, and the place with {在|zài} comes before the verb.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {药店|yào diàn}, pharmacy: two falling fourth tones (4+4).

questions.stem: Listen. Which tone is it?
questions.explanation: {疼|téng}, to ache: the second tone, rising.

questions.stem: You get into a taxi. How do you address the driver politely?
questions.explanation: {师傅|shī fu} ("master of a trade") is the usual polite word for drivers, repair people and other skilled workers. {同学|tóng xué} is for students, {小朋友|xiǎo péng you} for children, and {小姐|xiǎo jie} is avoided with strangers on the mainland.

questions.stem: In a restaurant on the mainland, which is the usual way to call a waiter or waitress over?
questions.explanation: {服务员|fú wù yuán} (server) is the standard word, and many people simply say {你好|nǐ hǎo}！ {小姐|xiǎo jie}！ is avoided because of its slang sense; {师父|shī fu} (with 父) is a martial-arts or religious master.

questions.stem: You visit a classmate's home. How do you greet the parents?
questions.explanation: Young people greet a friend's parents as {叔叔|shū shu} (uncle) and {阿姨|ā yí} (auntie). {爷爷|yé ye} and {奶奶|nǎi nai} are for the grandparents' generation, and {老王|Lǎo Wáng} / {小王|Xiǎo Wáng} are for colleagues and friends you know well.

questions.stem: What do you call your father's sister?
questions.explanation: Your father's sister is {姑姑|gū gu}. {阿姨|ā yí} is your mother's sister (and a friendly title for women of your parents' age), {舅舅|jiù jiu} your mother's brother, {奶奶|nǎi nai} your father's mother.

questions.stem: Who is your {堂哥|táng gē}?
questions.explanation: {堂|táng} cousins are the children of your father's brothers, who traditionally share your family name. All other cousins, on your mother's side or through your father's sisters, are {表|biǎo}: {表哥|biǎo gē}, {表姐|biǎo jiě}.

questions.stem: Why is calling out {小姐|xiǎo jie}！ to a young waitress or a stranger avoided on the mainland?
choices: It's an old word few people know.
In slang it has come to refer to women in the sex industry.
questions.explanation: The word has picked up that slang sense, which is one reason {服务员|fú wù yuán} became the usual word for staff. With a family name in formal service settings ({王|Wáng}{小姐|xiǎo jie}) it's still heard, and in Taiwan it's ordinary.

questions.stem: In many workplaces, which title can you use politely for a colleague whose role or age you aren't sure of?
questions.explanation: {老师|lǎo shī} has spread well beyond schools as a respectful title ({王|Wáng}{老师|lǎo shī}). {美女|měi nǚ} is informal and can sound over-familiar, {小朋友|xiǎo péng you} is for children, and {师父|shī fu} is a martial-arts master.

questions.stem: Listen. Who is the speaker most likely talking to?
questions.explanation: You heard {师傅|shī fu}，{去|qù}{北京|Běi jīng}{大学|dà xué}: "Beijing University, please", said to a driver addressed as {师傅|shī fu}.

questions.stem: Listen. Who is the speaker most likely greeting?
choices: a female colleague a little older than the speaker
questions.explanation: You heard {李|Lǐ}{姐|jiě}，{你好|nǐ hǎo}！ Family name + {姐|jiě} is a warm title for a woman a few years older, often a colleague. Your own sister is just {姐姐|jiě jie}, without the family name.

questions.stem: Listen. Who lives in Shanghai?
questions.explanation: You heard {我|wǒ}{外婆|wài pó}{住|zhù}{在|zài}{上海|Shàng hǎi}: {外婆|wài pó} is the mother's mother (in the north often {姥姥|lǎo lao}). The father's mother is {奶奶|nǎi nai}.

questions.stem: Read: "{我|wǒ}{妈妈|mā ma}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{哥哥|gē ge}，{他|tā}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{女儿|nǚ ér}，{今年|jīn nián}{二十|èr shí}{岁|suì}。{我|wǒ}{十八|shí bā}{岁|suì}。" What does the writer call this cousin?
questions.explanation: She is the daughter of the mother's brother, so a {表|biǎo} cousin, and older than the writer (20 vs 18), so {姐|jiě}: {表姐|biǎo jiě}. {堂|táng} is only for the children of the father's brothers.

questions.stem: Read: "{安娜|Ān nà}{去|qù}{王芳|Wáng Fāng}{家|jiā}。{王芳|Wáng Fāng}{的|de}{妈妈|mā ma}{说|shuō}：“{叔叔|shū shu}{在|zài}{做饭|zuò fàn}{呢|ne}。”" Who is cooking?
questions.explanation: Wang Fang's mother calls her husband {叔叔|shū shu} because that's what Anna, the guest, would call him. So it's Wang Fang's father who is cooking.

questions.stem: At the Spring Festival, money for children is given in …
questions.explanation: A {红包|hóng bāo} ("red packet") holds money given as a gift at New Year, weddings and other happy occasions. Red is the colour of joy and luck; white is linked with mourning.

questions.stem: Which colour is traditionally linked with mourning in China?
questions.explanation: White: a funeral is a {白事|bái shì}, a "white event". Mourning colours also include black and other plain shades, depending on the region.

questions.stem: On Chinese share-price displays, what does red mean?
questions.explanation: Red marks a rise and green a fall, the opposite of the usual convention in the United States. Red as good news fits its meaning of joy and luck.

questions.stem: Why shouldn't you give a Chinese man a green hat?
choices: "Wearing a green hat" means one's partner has been unfaithful.
questions.explanation: {戴|dài}{绿帽子|lǜ mào zi}, "to wear a green hat", means a man's partner has been unfaithful, so a green hat as a present is a bad joke. Green clothes are fine.

questions.stem: In the Ming and Qing dynasties, which colour was reserved for the emperor and the imperial family?
questions.explanation: A bright "imperial yellow" was reserved for the imperial family, which is why almost all the roofs of the Forbidden City have yellow tiles.

questions.stem: What does {眼红|yǎn hóng} ("red eyes") mean?
questions.explanation: {眼红|yǎn hóng} is "jealous, envious": English says "green with envy", Chinese "red-eyed". To blush is {脸红|liǎn hóng}, a red face.

questions.stem: What is a {黑车|hēi chē} ("black car")?
questions.explanation: {黑|hēi} can mean "unofficial, illegal", so a {黑车|hēi chē} is an unlicensed taxi, whatever its colour.

questions.stem: What do many brides in China wear today?
choices: a white Western-style dress, then a red outfit later in the day
questions.explanation: The old taboo on white has largely faded: many brides wear a white dress for the photos or the ceremony and change into a red {旗袍|qí páo} or another red outfit. Red is still the wedding colour.

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker giving you?
questions.explanation: You heard {这|zhè}{是|shì}{给|gěi}{你|nǐ}{的|de}{红包|hóng bāo}: this red envelope is for you. A red top would be {红色|hóng sè}{的|de}{衣服|yī fu}, black tea {红茶|hóng chá}.

questions.stem: Listen. Which colour does the speaker recommend?

audio.text: 红色的很好，爷爷会很高兴的。

questions.explanation: You heard {红色|hóng sè}{的|de}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}，{爷爷|yé ye}{会|huì}{很|hěn}{高兴|gāo xìng}{的|de}: the red one is good, Grandpa will be pleased.

questions.stem: Read: "{春节|Chūn jié}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{很|hěn}{多|duō}{人|rén}{穿|chuān}{红色|hóng sè}{的|de}{衣服|yī fu}。" ({春节|Chūn jié}: the Spring Festival) What do many people wear?
questions.explanation: {红色|hóng sè}{的|de}{衣服|yī fu}: red clothes, the colour of celebration at the Spring Festival.

questions.stem: Read the expression {红白喜事|hóng bái xǐ shì} ("red and white happy events"). What does it refer to?
questions.explanation: Red stands for weddings ({喜事|xǐ shì}) and white for funerals ({白事|bái shì}): together, the big family occasions.

questions.stem: How do you say "to the left of the school"?
questions.explanation: The thing you measure from comes first, then the position: {学校|xué xiào}{左边|zuǒ bian} (or {学校|xué xiào}{的|de}{左边|zuǒ bian}). English puts "left" first; Chinese puts it last, as in {杯子|bēi zi}{里|lǐ} (in the cup).

questions.stem: Which sentence means "There's a pharmacy next to the hospital."?
choices: {医院|yī yuàn}{旁边|páng biān}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{药店|yào diàn}。
{医院|yī yuàn}{旁边|páng biān}{在|zài}{一|yí}{个|gè}{药店|yào diàn}。
{一|yí}{个|gè}{药店|yào diàn}{有|yǒu}{医院|yī yuàn}{旁边|páng biān}。
{药店|yào diàn}{有|yǒu}{医院|yī yuàn}{旁边|páng biān}。
questions.explanation: "There is" is place + {有|yǒu} + thing: {医院|yī yuàn}{旁边|páng biān}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{药店|yào diàn}. {在|zài} goes the other way round ({药店|yào diàn}{在|zài}{医院|yī yuàn}{旁边|páng biān}, the pharmacy is next to the hospital), and the place can't come after {有|yǒu} here.

questions.stem: Choose the word: {超市|chāo shì}{左边|zuǒ bian} ___ {我|wǒ}{的|de}{学校|xué xiào}。 (To the left of the supermarket is my school.)
questions.explanation: Saying which known thing is in a place uses {是|shì}: {超市|chāo shì}{左边|zuǒ bian}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{学校|xué xiào}. {有|yǒu} introduces something new ("there's a…", usually with {一|yí}{个|gè}), so it doesn't fit a particular thing like "my school", and {在|zài} needs the thing first: {我|wǒ}{的|de}{学校|xué xiào}{在|zài}{超市|chāo shì}{左边|zuǒ bian}.

questions.stem: How do you ask "Where's the pharmacy?"
questions.explanation: thing + {在|zài} + place, with {哪儿|nǎr} in the place slot: {药店|yào diàn}{在|zài}{哪儿|nǎr}？ The question word stays where the answer goes ({药店|yào diàn}{在|zài}{超市|chāo shì}{旁边|páng biān}).

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT a word?
questions.explanation: -{面|miàn} makes {前面|qián miàn}, {后面|hòu miàn}, {左面|zuǒ miàn}, {里面|lǐ miàn} and more, but {旁|páng} only takes {边|biān}: {旁边|páng biān}. {前面|qián miàn} and {后面|hòu miàn} are this lesson's words, and {左边|zuǒ bian} is "on the left".

questions.stem: How do you say "Sit next to me."?
questions.explanation: "Next to me" is {我|wǒ}{旁边|páng biān}: the person first, then the position, as with any noun. It goes after {坐|zuò} like a place: {你|nǐ}{坐|zuò}{我|wǒ}{旁边|páng biān}{吧|ba}. {吧|ba} makes it a friendly suggestion.

questions.stem: Which character is yòu, "right (not left)"?
questions.explanation: {右|yòu} has {口|kǒu} under the top. {有|yǒu} (to have) has {月|yuè} there and is yǒu, third tone. {石|shí} (stone) and {古|gǔ} (old) aren't course words.

questions.stem: Which character completes the word? ___ {边|biān} (next to)
questions.explanation: {旁边|páng biān}: {旁|páng} has a dot and a short horizontal on top and {方|fāng} at the bottom. {房|fáng} is in {房间|fáng jiān} (room); {方|fāng} is only the bottom part; {傍|bàng} (with 亻) isn't a course character.

questions.stem: Match each character to its meaning.
questions.explanation: {左|zuǒ} left, {右|yòu} right, {旁|páng} side ({旁边|páng biān}, next to), {笑|xiào} laugh or smile. "Front" is {前|qián} ({前面|qián miàn}).

questions.stem: Listen. Where is the bookshop?
choices: to the left of the supermarket
to the right of the supermarket
questions.explanation: {书店|shū diàn}{在|zài}{超市|chāo shì}{的|de}{右边|yòu bian}: the bookshop is to the right of the supermarket. Left would be {左边|zuǒ bian}, behind {后面|hòu miàn}, in front {前面|qián miàn}.

questions.stem: Listen. What is next to the speaker's home?
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{旁边|páng biān}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{药店|yào diàn}: there's a pharmacy ({药店|yào diàn}) next to my home. A hospital is {医院|yī yuàn}, a supermarket {超市|chāo shì} and a bookshop {书店|shū diàn}.

questions.stem: Listen. Which is the right reply?
questions.explanation: "Excuse me, is there a supermarket here?" asks whether there is one, so the answer starts with {有|yǒu} and says where: {有|yǒu}，{在|zài}{前面|qián miàn} (yes, up ahead). {不客气|bú kè qi} answers a thank-you.

questions.stem: Listen. Which is true?

audio.text: 医院在学校后面，不在学校前面。

choices: The hospital is next to the school.
The hospital is in front of the school.
The hospital is behind the school.
The hospital is to the left of the school.
questions.explanation: {医院|yī yuàn}{在|zài}{学校|xué xiào}{后面|hòu miàn}，{不|bú}{在|zài}{学校|xué xiào}{前面|qián miàn}: behind the school, not in front of it. {后面|hòu miàn} is behind, {前面|qián miàn} in front.

questions.stem: Read: "{我|wǒ}{叫|jiào}{李明|Lǐ Míng}。{我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{旁边|páng biān}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{超市|chāo shì}，{超市|chāo shì}{左边|zuǒ bian}{是|shì}{一|yí}{个|gè}{书店|shū diàn}，{右边|yòu bian}{是|shì}{一|yí}{个|gè}{饭店|fàn diàn}。{那个|nà ge}{饭店|fàn diàn}{的|de}{菜|cài}{很|hěn}{好吃|hǎo chī}，{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{喜欢|xǐ huan}。{医院|yī yuàn}{不|bú}{在|zài}{我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{旁边|páng biān}，{在|zài}{学校|xué xiào}{后面|hòu miàn}。{我|wǒ}{爸爸|bà ba}{在|zài}{那个|nà ge}{医院|yī yuàn}{工作|gōng zuò}，{他|tā}{每天|měi tiān}{坐|zuò}{出租车|chū zū chē}{去|qù}{医院|yī yuàn}。" Which is true?
choices: The bookshop is to the left of the supermarket.
The restaurant is to the left of the supermarket.
The hospital is next to Li Ming's home.
Li Ming's father works in the supermarket.
questions.explanation: {超市|chāo shì}{左边|zuǒ bian}{是|shì}{一|yí}{个|gè}{书店|shū diàn}: the bookshop is on the supermarket's left, and the restaurant ({饭店|fàn diàn}) on its right. The hospital is behind the school ({在|zài}{学校|xué xiào}{后面|hòu miàn}), not next to his home, and his father works at the hospital.

questions.stem: Read: "{我们|wǒ men}{学校|xué xiào}{的|de}{前面|qián miàn}{是|shì}{商店|shāng diàn}，{后面|hòu miàn}{是|shì}{医院|yī yuàn}。{商店|shāng diàn}{的|de}{左边|zuǒ bian}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{药店|yào diàn}，{右边|yòu bian}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{超市|chāo shì}。" What is behind the school?
questions.explanation: {后面|hòu miàn}{是|shì}{医院|yī yuàn}: behind the school is the hospital. The shop ({商店|shāng diàn}) is in front, with a pharmacy on its left and a supermarket on its right.

questions.stem: Read the message: "{安娜|Ān nà}，{我|wǒ}{在|zài}{书店|shū diàn}，{书店|shū diàn}{在|zài}{药店|yào diàn}{后面|hòu miàn}。{你|nǐ}{也|yě}{来|lái}{吧|ba}！——{王芳|Wáng Fāng}" Where is Wang Fang?
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{在|zài}{书店|shū diàn}: she's in the bookshop, which is behind the pharmacy ({书店|shū diàn}{在|zài}{药店|yào diàn}{后面|hòu miàn}). She asks Anna to come too.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese.
questions.prompt: There's a bookshop to the left of my home.
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{左边|zuǒ bian}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{书店|shū diàn}。 Place first ({我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{左边|zuǒ bian}, with the position after the thing), then {有|yǒu}, then the new thing. {在|zài} isn't needed: the place opens the sentence by itself.

questions.stem: Anna asks where the pharmacy is. Write the answer word "on the right" (characters, or pinyin with tone marks): {药店|yào diàn}{在|zài}___。
questions.explanation: {药店|yào diàn}{在|zài}{右边|yòu bian}。 {右边|yòu bian} (or {右面|yòu miàn}): {右|yòu}, fourth tone, and a light {边|biān}. "On the left" would be {左边|zuǒ bian}.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tone is it?
questions.explanation: {左|zuǒ}, left: the third tone, a dip. It is not {坐|zuò} (to sit), which falls.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tone is it?
questions.explanation: {右|yòu}, right: the fourth tone, falling. {有|yǒu} (to have) dips instead.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {旁边|páng biān}, next to: tones 2 + 1. Unlike the light {边|biān} of {左边|zuǒ bian}, this {边|biān} keeps its first tone.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "My home is very close to school."?
questions.explanation: Distance between two places is A {离|lí} B + adjective: {我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{离|lí}{学校|xué xiào}{很|hěn}{近|jìn}. {从|cóng} marks a starting point, the {离|lí} phrase comes before the adjective, and {近|jìn} is an adjective predicate, so no {是|shì}.

questions.stem: Choose the word: {我|wǒ} ___ {北京|Běi jīng}{来|lái}。 (I've come from Beijing.)
questions.explanation: A starting point takes {从|cóng}: {我|wǒ}{从|cóng}{北京|Běi jīng}{来|lái}. {离|lí} only measures a distance ({我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{离|lí}{北京|Běi jīng}{很|hěn}{远|yuǎn}), {往|wǎng} is "towards", and {在|zài}{北京|Běi jīng}{来|lái} makes no sense.

questions.stem: How do you say "Go left."?
questions.explanation: {往|wǎng} + direction + verb: {往|wǎng}{左|zuǒ}{走|zǒu}. The direction sits between {往|wǎng} and the verb, like {往|wǎng}{前|qián}{走|zǒu} (go straight ahead) and {往|wǎng}{右|yòu}{走|zǒu} (go right).

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I have classes from eight to twelve."?
choices: {我|wǒ}{从|cóng}{八|bā}{点|diǎn}{到|dào}{十二|shí èr}{点|diǎn}{上课|shàng kè}。
{我|wǒ}{离|lí}{八|bā}{点|diǎn}{到|dào}{十二|shí èr}{点|diǎn}{上课|shàng kè}。
{八|bā}{点|diǎn}{到|dào}{十二|shí èr}{点|diǎn}{我|wǒ}{从|cóng}{上课|shàng kè}。
{我|wǒ}{上课|shàng kè}{从|cóng}{八|bā}{点|diǎn}{十二|shí èr}{点|diǎn}。
questions.explanation: {从|cóng}…{到|dào}… works for times too, and like any time phrase it goes before the verb: {我|wǒ}{从|cóng}{八|bā}{点|diǎn}{到|dào}{十二|shí èr}{点|diǎn}{上课|shàng kè}. {离|lí} isn't used for a starting time, and {从|cóng} and {到|dào} must frame the two times.

questions.stem: What does "{他|tā}{走|zǒu}{了|le}。" mean?
questions.explanation: {走|zǒu} is "to walk" and also "to leave", and with {了|le} for the change it means "he's gone, he's left". Arriving is {到|dào}, coming back {回来|huí lái} (lesson 09).

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I walk to school every day."?
choices: {我|wǒ}{每天|měi tiān}{走路|zǒu lù}{去|qù}{学校|xué xiào}。
{我|wǒ}{走路|zǒu lù}{学校|xué xiào}{每天|měi tiān}。
{我|wǒ}{每天|měi tiān}{走路|zǒu lù}{学校|xué xiào}。
{我|wǒ}{每天|měi tiān}{去|qù}{学校|xué xiào}{走路|zǒu lù}。
questions.explanation: Time first ({每天|měi tiān}), then the means ({走路|zǒu lù}), then {去|qù} + place, as with {坐车|zuò chē}{去|qù}{学校|xué xiào}. {走路|zǒu lù} already has its object, so it can't take {学校|xué xiào} directly, and {去|qù}{学校|xué xiào}{走路|zǒu lù} means "go to school to walk".

questions.stem: How do you ask "How far is the hospital from here?"
choices: {医院|yī yuàn}{离|lí}{这儿|zhèr}{多少|duō shao}{远|yuǎn}？
questions.explanation: {离|lí} measures the distance, and {多|duō} + adjective asks "how…?": {医院|yī yuàn}{离|lí}{这儿|zhèr}{有|yǒu}{多|duō}{远|yuǎn}？ ({有|yǒu} is often said here, and can be left out). {多少|duō shao} counts things; it doesn't go before an adjective.

questions.stem: How is {路上|lù shang} (on the way) written in pinyin?
questions.explanation: {路|lù} falls (lù) and {上|shàng} is light here: lù shang. On its own {上|shàng} is shàng, as in {桌子|zhuō zi}{上|shàng}.

questions.stem: Which character is yuǎn, "far"?
questions.explanation: {={远|yuǎn} has {元|yuán} inside the walking radical, and {元|yuán} gives the sound; {近|jìn} (near) has {斤|jīn} inside.=} (Traditional {+{远|yuǎn}+} has {袁|yuán} inside instead.) {还|hái} is "still, also", and {运|yùn} is in {运动|yùn dòng} (sport, lesson 19).

questions.stem: Which character completes the word? {走|zǒu}___ (to go on foot)
questions.explanation: {走路|zǒu lù}: {路|lù}, road, with {各|gè} on the right. All four have the foot radical on the left: {跑|pǎo} is "run" (lesson 19), {跟|gēn} "with" (lesson 14) and {踢|tī} "kick" (lesson 19).

questions.stem: Match each character to its meaning.
questions.explanation: {离|lí} away from (A {离|lí} B {远|yuǎn}), {远|yuǎn} far, {近|jìn} near, {往|wǎng} towards ({往|wǎng}{前|qián}{走|zǒu}), {从|cóng} from ({从|cóng}{北京|Běi jīng}{来|lái}). "Arrive" is {到|dào}.

questions.stem: Listen. How far is the speaker's home?

audio.text: 我家离这儿不远，走路十分钟。

questions.explanation: {不|bù}{远|yuǎn}，{走路|zǒu lù}{十|shí}{分钟|fēn zhōng}: not far, ten minutes on foot. {走路|zǒu lù} is walking; a car would be {坐车|zuò chē} or {开车|kāi chē}.

questions.stem: Listen to the directions. Where do you turn left?

audio.text: 从这儿往前走，到了书店往左走。

questions.explanation: {往|wǎng}{前|qián}{走|zǒu}，{到|dào}{了|le}{书店|shū diàn}{往|wǎng}{左|zuǒ}{走|zǒu}: go straight ahead, and when you reach the bookshop ({书店|shū diàn}), go left.

questions.stem: Listen to the voice message. Which is true?
choices: The speaker is still at home.
The speaker is on the way and will arrive in twenty minutes.
The speaker arrived twenty minutes ago.
The speaker will arrive at two o'clock.
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{在|zài}{路上|lù shang} is "I'm on my way", and {二十|èr shí}{分钟|fēn zhōng}{到|dào} "(I'll) arrive in twenty minutes". Two o'clock would be {两|liǎng}{点|diǎn}.

questions.stem: Read: "{我|wǒ}{叫|jiào}{王芳|Wáng Fāng}，{是|shì}{大学生|dà xué shēng}。{我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{离|lí}{大学|dà xué}{很|hěn}{远|yuǎn}，{从|cóng}{我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{到|dào}{大学|dà xué}{坐|zuò}{出租车|chū zū chē}{要|yào}{四十|sì shí}{分钟|fēn zhōng}。{我|wǒ}{爸爸|bà ba}{每天|měi tiān}{开车|kāi chē}{去|qù}{公司|gōng sī}，{他|tā}{的|de}{公司|gōng sī}{在|zài}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{大学|dà xué}{旁边|páng biān}，{所以|suǒ yǐ}{我|wǒ}{坐|zuò}{他|tā}{的|de}{车|chē}{去|qù}。{我|wǒ}{的|de}{同学|tóng xué}{安娜|Ān nà}{住|zhù}{在|zài}{学校|xué xiào}{里|lǐ}，{她|tā}{走路|zǒu lù}{去|qù}{上课|shàng kè}，{路上|lù shang}{要|yào}{五|wǔ}{分钟|fēn zhōng}。" How does Wang Fang get to university?
questions.explanation: Her dad's company is next to her university, {所以|suǒ yǐ}{我|wǒ}{坐|zuò}{他|tā}{的|de}{车|chē}{去|qù}: so she goes in his car. A taxi would take forty minutes; it's Anna who walks ({走路|zǒu lù}{去|qù}{上课|shàng kè}).

questions.stem: Read the note: "{从|cóng}{学校|xué xiào}{往|wǎng}{前|qián}{走|zǒu}，{到|dào}{了|le}{医院|yī yuàn}{往|wǎng}{右|yòu}{走|zǒu}，{书店|shū diàn}{在|zài}{医院|yī yuàn}{后面|hòu miàn}。" Where is the bookshop?
choices: to the right of the school
questions.explanation: {书店|shū diàn}{在|zài}{医院|yī yuàn}{后面|hòu miàn}: behind the hospital. You walk ahead from the school and turn right at the hospital ({到|dào}{了|le}{医院|yī yuàn}{往|wǎng}{右|yòu}{走|zǒu}).

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese.
questions.prompt: It takes twenty minutes from my home to school.
questions.explanation: {从|cóng}{我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{到|dào}{学校|xué xiào}{要|yào}{二十|èr shí}{分钟|fēn zhōng}。 The {从|cóng}…{到|dào}… phrase comes first, then {要|yào} + time ("it takes"). {离|lí} measures a distance and isn't used with {到|dào} like this.

questions.stem: A friend asks if the station is far. Write the number "ten" (characters, or pinyin with tone marks): {不|bù}{远|yuǎn}，{走路|zǒu lù}___ {分钟|fēn zhōng}。
questions.explanation: {不|bù}{远|yuǎn}，{走路|zǒu lù}{十|shí}{分钟|fēn zhōng}。 {十|shí} is shí, second tone. In messages people also write digits: {走路|zǒu lù}10{分钟|fēn zhōng}.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tone is it?
questions.explanation: {远|yuǎn}, far: the third tone. {元|yuán} (yuan) rises.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tone is it?
questions.explanation: {近|jìn}, near: the fourth tone, the same syllable as {进|jìn} (to enter, lesson 09).

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {走路|zǒu lù}, to go on foot: tones 3 + 4, a dip and then a fall.

questions.stem: Your friend has just arrived. How do you ask "How did you get here?"
questions.explanation: The arrival is known; the question is about how, so it takes {是|shì}…{的|de}: {是|shì} before the detail ({怎么|zěn me}), {的|de} at the end. {你|nǐ}{怎么|zěn me}{来|lái}{了|le}？ sounds like "Why have you come?", and {是|shì}…{的|de} never takes {了|le}.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I came by metro."?
questions.explanation: {是|shì} goes before the detail ({坐|zuò}{地铁|dì tiě}, how), {的|de} at the end: {我|wǒ}{是|shì}{坐|zuò}{地铁|dì tiě}{来|lái}{的|de}. No {了|le} inside the frame, and {是|shì} can't sit between the detail and the verb.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I didn't come by plane."?
questions.explanation: The negative of {是|shì}…{的|de} is {不|bú}{是|shì}…{的|de}: {我|wǒ}{不|bú}{是|shì}{坐|zuò}{飞机|fēi jī}{来|lái}{的|de}. {是|shì} is never negated with {没|méi}, and in the negative it can't be dropped.

questions.stem: Which sentence is NOT correct?
choices: {我|wǒ}{明天|míng tiān}{是|shì}{坐|zuò}{火车|huǒ chē}{去|qù}{的|de}。
{他|tā}{是|shì}{坐|zuò}{出租车|chū zū chē}{来|lái}{的|de}。
questions.explanation: {是|shì}…{的|de} is only for things that have already happened, so it can't go with {明天|míng tiān}. A plan is a plain sentence: {我|wǒ}{明天|míng tiān}{坐|zuò}{火车|huǒ chē}{去|qù}. The other two {是|shì}…{的|de} sentences are about the past.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I bought the ticket at the airport."?
questions.explanation: {是|shì} before the detail ({在|zài}{机场|jī chǎng}), and {的|de} after the verb: before the object ({买|mǎi}{的|de}{票|piào}) or at the very end ({买|mǎi}{票|piào}{的|de}). Both are right; {我|wǒ}{是|shì}{在|zài}{机场|jī chǎng}{买|mǎi}{的|de}{票|piào} is the more common one in speech.

questions.stem: A friend messages you: "{我|wǒ}{到|dào}{北京|Běi jīng}{了|le}！" Which is the natural question to ask next?
choices: {你|nǐ}{是|shì}{什么|shén me}{时候|shí hou}{到|dào}{的|de}？
questions.explanation: Your friend has given the news with {了|le}; now you ask for a detail of a past event with {是|shì}…{的|de}: {你|nǐ}{是|shì}{什么|shén me}{时候|shí hou}{到|dào}{的|de}？ (when did you arrive?). The others ask whether or when they will arrive.

questions.stem: What does "{我们|wǒ men}{打车|dǎ chē}{去|qù}{吧|ba}。" mean?
questions.explanation: {打车|dǎ chē} is "to take a taxi". Driving is {开车|kāi chē}, the bus is {公交车|gōng jiāo chē} ({坐|zuò}{公交车|gōng jiāo chē}), and walking is {走路|zǒu lù}.

questions.stem: Choose the word: {坐|zuò}{三|sān} ___ {就|jiù}{到|dào}{了|le}。 (It's just three stops.)
questions.explanation: {站|zhàn} counts stops: {坐|zuò}{三|sān}{站|zhàn}, ride three stops. {场|chǎng} is in {机场|jī chǎng} (airport), {路|lù} numbers bus routes ({三|sān}{路|lù}, the No. 3), and {票|piào} is a ticket.

questions.stem: Which character completes the word? ___ {铁|tiě} (metro)
questions.explanation: {地铁|dì tiě} starts with {地|dì}: earth {土|tǔ} on the left, {也|yě} on the right. {他|tā} (he) has the person radical, {池|chí} (pool, not a course word) has water, and {也|yě} alone is "also".

questions.stem: Which character means "ticket"?
questions.explanation: {票|piào} is a flattened {西|xī} on top of {示|shì} (to show). {要|yào} (to want) has the same top over {女|nǚ}, {西|xī} is "west" (in {东西|dōng xi}), and {示|shì} alone is "to show".

questions.stem: Listen. How did the speaker come?
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{是|shì}{坐|zuò}{公交车|gōng jiāo chē}{来|lái}{的|de}: I came by bus. The metro is {地铁|dì tiě}, a taxi {出租车|chū zū chē} (or {打车|dǎ chē}), and on foot {走路|zǒu lù}.

questions.stem: Listen. When did he arrive?

audio.text: 他不是昨天到的，是今天到的。

questions.explanation: {不|bú}{是|shì}{昨天|zuó tiān}{到|dào}{的|de}，{是|shì}{今天|jīn tiān}{到|dào}{的|de}: not yesterday, today. {不|bú}{是|shì}…{的|de} corrects the detail, and the second half gives the right one.

questions.stem: Listen. Which is the right reply?
questions.explanation: "Where did you buy the ticket?" asks a detail with {是|shì}…{的|de}, and the answer keeps the frame: {我|wǒ}{是|shì}{在|zài}{机场|jī chǎng}{买|mǎi}{的|de} (I bought it at the airport). {我|wǒ}{买|mǎi}{了|le}{两张|liǎng zhāng} says how many ({张|zhāng} counts tickets).

questions.stem: Listen. Which is true?

audio.text: 从这儿到机场，坐地铁要四十分钟，打车要一个小时。

questions.explanation: {坐|zuò}{地铁|dì tiě}{要|yào}{四十|sì shí}{分钟|fēn zhōng}，{打车|dǎ chē}{要|yào}{一|yí}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}: forty minutes by metro, an hour by taxi. So the metro is faster.

questions.stem: Read Anna's message ({酒店|jiǔ diàn}: hotel): "{李明|Lǐ Míng}，{我|wǒ}{到|dào}{上海|Shàng hǎi}{了|le}！{我|wǒ}{是|shì}{昨天|zuó tiān}{下午|xià wǔ}{到|dào}{的|de}，{是|shì}{坐|zuò}{飞机|fēi jī}{来|lái}{的|de}。{从|cóng}{机场|jī chǎng}{到|dào}{酒店|jiǔ diàn}，{我|wǒ}{是|shì}{坐|zuò}{地铁|dì tiě}{去|qù}{的|de}，{坐|zuò}{了|le}{十|shí}{站|zhàn}。{酒店|jiǔ diàn}{离|lí}{地铁站|dì tiě zhàn}{很|hěn}{近|jìn}，{走路|zǒu lù}{三|sān}{分钟|fēn zhōng}。{明天|míng tiān}{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{去|qù}{书店|shū diàn}，{书店|shū diàn}{离|lí}{酒店|jiǔ diàn}{有点儿|yǒu diǎnr}{远|yuǎn}，{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{打车|dǎ chē}{去|qù}。" How did Anna get from the airport to the hotel?
questions.explanation: {从|cóng}{机场|jī chǎng}{到|dào}{酒店|jiǔ diàn}，{我|wǒ}{是|shì}{坐|zuò}{地铁|dì tiě}{去|qù}{的|de}: by metro, ten stops ({坐|zuò}{了|le}{十|shí}{站|zhàn}). She plans to take a taxi tomorrow, to the bookshop, and the walk is from the metro station to the hotel.

questions.stem: Read Anna's message again: "…{明天|míng tiān}{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{去|qù}{书店|shū diàn}，{书店|shū diàn}{离|lí}{酒店|jiǔ diàn}{有点儿|yǒu diǎnr}{远|yuǎn}，{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{打车|dǎ chē}{去|qù}。" How does she want to get to the bookshop tomorrow?
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{打车|dǎ chē}{去|qù}: she'd like to take a taxi, because the bookshop is a bit far from the hotel ({有点儿|yǒu diǎnr}{远|yuǎn}). Plans take no {是|shì}…{的|de}: {我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{打车|dǎ chē}{去|qù}, not {是|shì}…{的|de}.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese.
questions.prompt: I came by metro.
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{是|shì}{坐|zuò}{地铁|dì tiě}{来|lái}{的|de}。 {是|shì} before the detail ({坐|zuò}{地铁|dì tiě}), {的|de} at the end. In speech {是|shì} can be left out ({我|wǒ}{坐|zuò}{地铁|dì tiě}{来|lái}{的|de}), so that order is accepted too. {了|le} doesn't go inside {是|shì}…{的|de}.

questions.stem: Someone asks where you bought your ticket. Write the place "the airport" (characters, or pinyin with tone marks): {我|wǒ}{是|shì}{在|zài}___ {买|mǎi}{的|de}。
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{是|shì}{在|zài}{机场|jī chǎng}{买|mǎi}{的|de}。 {机场|jī chǎng}: {机|jī} as in {飞机|fēi jī}, and {场|chǎng}, an open area.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {地铁|dì tiě}, metro: tones 4 + 3, falling, then dipping.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {机场|jī chǎng}, airport: tones 1 + 3. {机|jī} is the {机|jī} of {飞机|fēi jī}.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the three syllables?
questions.explanation: {公交车|gōng jiāo chē}, bus: three first tones, high and level all the way.

questions.stem: You're in your room and a friend knocks. How do you say "Come in!"?
questions.explanation: You're inside and your friend moves towards you: {进|jìn} + {来|lái}, {请|qǐng}{进来|jìn lái}！ {进去|jìn qù} would be "go in" (away from you), and {出来|chū lái} / {出去|chū qù} are about coming or going out.

questions.stem: You and a friend are standing outside a shop. How do you say "Let's go in."?
questions.explanation: You're outside, moving into the shop, away from where you stand: {进去|jìn qù}. {进来|jìn lái} is for someone coming in towards a speaker who is inside.

questions.stem: How do you say "go back home" with {回|huí}, {家|jiā} and {去|qù}?
questions.explanation: The place goes between the verb and {去|qù}: {回家|huí jiā}{去|qù}. ~~{回去|huí qù}{家|jiā}~~ puts it at the end, English-style. Just {回家|huí jiā} is also correct and very common.

questions.stem: You're leaving home, and your mum asks "{你|nǐ}{几|jǐ}{点|diǎn}{回来|huí lái}？" Choose the word for your answer: {我|wǒ}{六|liù}{点|diǎn} ___。
questions.explanation: You'll come back here, to the home where you and your mum are talking: {我|wǒ}{六|liù}{点|diǎn}{回来|huí lái}. {回去|huí qù} would mean going back somewhere else.

questions.stem: What does "{他|tā}{出去|chū qù}{了|le}。" mean?
questions.explanation: {出去|chū qù} is "go out" (away from the speaker, who is inside), and {了|le} marks the change: he's gone out. He's back is {他|tā}{回来|huí lái}{了|le}, and he's come in {他|tā}{进来|jìn lái}{了|le}.

questions.stem: You open your own front door after school. What do many people call out?
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{回来|huí lái}{了|le}！ "I'm back! I'm home!": you've come back to where you are now. {我|wǒ}{回去|huí qù}{了|le} is what you'd say as you leave a friend's place to go home.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT correct?
questions.explanation: A place can't follow {来|lái} / {去|qù}: ~~{进来|jìn lái}{房间|fáng jiān}~~. It goes between ({进|jìn}{房间|fáng jiān}{来|lái}), or {来|lái} is left out ({进|jìn}{房间|fáng jiān}). {请|qǐng}{进|jìn} is a short "please come in".

questions.stem: Which character completes the word? ___ {来|lái} (to come in)
questions.explanation: {进来|jìn lái}: {={进|jìn} has {井|jǐng} inside the walking radical. {近|jìn} (near) sounds the same but has {斤|jīn} inside=} (traditional {+{进|jìn}+} has {隹|zhuī}); {这|zhè} is "this" and {还|hái} "still, also".

questions.stem: Which character is mén, "door"?
questions.explanation: {门|mén} is the door itself. {们|men} adds the person radical (plural suffix), {问|wèn} has {口|kǒu} inside (to ask), and {间|jiān} has {日|rì} inside (in {时间|shí jiān}, {房间|fáng jiān}).

questions.stem: Match each character to its meaning.
questions.explanation: {进|jìn} enter, {出|chū} exit (go or come out), {回|huí} return, {门|mén} door, {来|lái} come. "Near" is {近|jìn}, which sounds like {进|jìn}.

questions.stem: Listen. Where is the speaker's mother?
questions.explanation: {出去|chū qù}{了|le}，{不|bú}{在|zài}{家|jiā}: she's gone out and isn't at home. Coming back would be {回来|huí lái}{了|le}.

questions.stem: Listen. Which is the right reply?
questions.explanation: "What time will you be back?" asks for a time: {我|wǒ}{六|liù}{点|diǎn}{回来|huí lái}. The others say where you are, that you're not going in, and how you came.

questions.stem: Listen. Where is the speaker?

audio.text: 我在你家门口，你出来一下。

questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{在|zài}{你|nǐ}{家|jiā}{门口|mén kǒu}: I'm at your door. The speaker is outside, so the listener comes out towards them: {你|nǐ}{出来|chū lái}{一下|yí xià} (come out for a moment).

questions.stem: Listen. Which is true?
questions.explanation: {他|tā}{回来|huí lái}{了|le}，{在|zài}{房间|fáng jiān}{里|lǐ}: he's back and he's in the room. Not back yet would be {还没|hái méi}{回来|huí lái}.

questions.stem: Read Anna's note ({一起|yì qǐ}: together): "{大卫|Dà wèi}：{我|wǒ}{和|hé}{王芳|Wáng Fāng}{出去|chū qù}{了|le}，{去|qù}{书店|shū diàn}{买|mǎi}{书|shū}。{我们|wǒ men}{走路|zǒu lù}{去|qù}，{书店|shū diàn}{离|lí}{学校|xué xiào}{不|bù}{远|yuǎn}。{我们|wǒ men}{五|wǔ}{点|diǎn}{回来|huí lái}。{你|nǐ}{回来|huí lái}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{给|gěi}{我|wǒ}{打|dǎ}{个|gè}{电话|diàn huà}{吧|ba}。{晚上|wǎn shang}{我们|wǒ men}{一起|yì qǐ}{去|qù}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}，{饭店|fàn diàn}{在|zài}{学校|xué xiào}{门口|mén kǒu}。——{安娜|Ān nà}" When will Anna and Wang Fang be back?
questions.explanation: {我们|wǒ men}{五|wǔ}{点|diǎn}{回来|huí lái}: they'll be back at five. In the evening they'll eat together at the restaurant at the school gate ({在|zài}{学校|xué xiào}{门口|mén kǒu}).

questions.stem: Read the sign on a shop door ({关门|guān mén}: to close): "{九|jiǔ}{点|diǎn}{开门|kāi mén}，{二十二|èr shí èr}{点|diǎn}{关门|guān mén}。" When does the shop open?
questions.explanation: {九|jiǔ}{点|diǎn}{开门|kāi mén}: it opens at nine. {二十二|èr shí èr}{点|diǎn} (22:00, ten at night) is closing time: {关门|guān mén}.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese.
questions.prompt: He's gone back home.
questions.explanation: {他|tā}{回家|huí jiā}{去|qù}{了|le}。 The place {家|jiā} goes between {回|huí} and {去|qù}; {了|le} at the end for the change. {他|tā}{回家|huí jiā}{了|le} is also right (and very common). {来|lái} would mean he came back to where the speaker is.

questions.stem: Text a friend that you're waiting outside. Write the place word "at the door, the entrance" (characters, or pinyin with tone marks): {我|wǒ}{在|zài}___。
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{在|zài}{门口|mén kǒu}。 {门口|mén kǒu}, "the door's mouth": {门|mén} (door) + {口|kǒu} (mouth).

questions.stem: Listen. Which tone is it?
questions.explanation: {进|jìn}, to enter: the fourth tone, falling.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tone is it?
questions.explanation: {出|chū}, to exit: the first tone, high and level.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {门口|mén kǒu}, doorway: tones 2 + 3, a rise and then a dip. {们|men} (plural) is light; {门|mén} rises.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I've been to Beijing."?
questions.explanation: The experience particle goes straight after the verb, before the object: {去|qù}{过|guo}{北京|Běi jīng}. {过去|guò qù} is a different word (to go over; the past), and {过|guo} doesn't follow the object or come after {了|le}.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I've never been abroad."?
questions.explanation: Experiences are negated with {没|méi}, and {过|guo} stays. {出国|chū guó} is a verb with its own object, so {过|guo} goes in the middle: {没|méi}{出|chū}{过|guo}{国|guó}. {不|bù} isn't used with {过|guo}, and {了|le} would talk about one particular trip.

questions.stem: Choose the word: {他|tā}{去|qù} ___ {上海|Shàng hǎi}，{现在|xiàn zài}{在|zài}{上海|Shàng hǎi}{工作|gōng zuò}。 (He went to Shanghai and works there now.)
questions.explanation: He went and he's still there, so it's one completed event: {他|tā}{去|qù}{了|le}{上海|Shàng hǎi}. {他|tā}{去|qù}{过|guo}{上海|Shàng hǎi} would say the trip is over (he has been there and come back), which doesn't fit {现在|xiàn zài}{在|zài}{上海|Shàng hǎi}{工作|gōng zuò}.

questions.stem: How do you ask "Have you ever had dumplings?"
questions.explanation: Verb + {过|guo} + object + {吗|ma}: {你|nǐ}{吃|chī}{过|guo}{饺子|jiǎo zi}{吗|ma}？ (or {你|nǐ}{吃|chī}{过|guo}{饺子|jiǎo zi}{没有|méi yǒu}？). {过|guo} never goes before the verb or after the object, and no {了|le} goes between {过|guo} and the object.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I've been to Shanghai twice."?
questions.explanation: The number of times follows the verb and {过|guo}: {去|qù}{过|guo}{两|liǎng}{次|cì}{上海|Shàng hǎi} (with a place name, {去|qù}{过|guo}{上海|Shàng hǎi}{两|liǎng}{次|cì} is right too). {次|cì} is a measure word by itself, so no {个|gè}.

questions.stem: How do you say "This is my first time in China."?
questions.explanation: "The first time" is {第|dì}{一|yī}{次|cì}, kept together and placed before the verb phrase: {我|wǒ}{第|dì}{一|yī}{次|cì}{来|lái}{中国|Zhōng guó}. {一|yí}{次|cì} alone is "once", and {第|dì} can't be split from its number.

questions.stem: What is a {酒店|jiǔ diàn}?
questions.explanation: {酒店|jiǔ diàn} is a hotel. {酒|jiǔ} is alcohol, but the word has nothing to do with drinking. A restaurant is {饭馆|fàn guǎn} or {饭店|fàn diàn}, and some hotel names use {饭店|fàn diàn} too.

questions.stem: How is 一次 (once) said?
questions.explanation: {次|cì} is fourth tone, so {一|yī} before it rises: yí cì. {一|yī} stays yī only when counting, in numbers and in the ordinal {第|dì}{一|yī}{次|cì} (dì yī cì).

questions.stem: Which character completes the word? {去|qù}___ (have been)
questions.explanation: {去|qù}{过|guo}: {={过|guo} has {寸|cùn} inside the walking radical=} (traditional {+{过|guo}+} has {咼|guō}). {还|hái} (still), {这|zhè} (this) and {边|biān} (side) all have the same radical with a different inside.

questions.stem: Which character is lǚ, as in "to travel"?
questions.explanation: {旅|lǚ} (in {旅游|lǚ yóu}) has {方|fāng} on the left. {旁|páng} (in {旁边|páng biān}) has {方|fāng} at the bottom, {方|fāng} is the radical on its own, and {族|zú} (a people, a clan) isn't a course character.

questions.stem: Match each character to its meaning.
questions.explanation: {旅|lǚ} journey ({旅游|lǚ yóu}), {过|guò} pass (and the particle of experience), {次|cì} occurrence, time ({两|liǎng}{次|cì}), {酒|jiǔ} alcohol ({酒店|jiǔ diàn}), {门|mén} door ({门票|mén piào}). "Hotel" takes two characters: {酒店|jiǔ diàn}.

questions.stem: Listen. How many times has the speaker been to Shanghai?
questions.explanation: {去|qù}{过|guo}{三|sān}{次|cì}: three times. Twice would be {两|liǎng}{次|cì}, once {一|yí}{次|cì}, and never {没|méi}{去|qù}{过|guo}.

questions.stem: Listen. Which is true?

audio.text: 我没出过国，这是第一次。

choices: The speaker has been abroad many times.
This is the speaker's first time abroad.
The speaker went abroad last year.
The speaker doesn't want to travel.
questions.explanation: {没|méi}{出|chū}{过|guo}{国|guó}，{这|zhè}{是|shì}{第|dì}{一|yī}{次|cì}: never been abroad before, and this is the first time.

questions.stem: Listen. Which is the right reply?
questions.explanation: "Have you been to the Great Wall?" is answered with {去|qù}{过|guo} or {没|méi}{去|qù}{过|guo}: {去|qù}{过|guo}，{去|qù}{过|guo}{两|liǎng}{次|cì} (yes, twice).

questions.stem: Read: "{我|wǒ}{叫|jiào}{王芳|Wáng Fāng}。{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{旅游|lǚ yóu}，{可是|kě shì}{我|wǒ}{没|méi}{出|chū}{过|guo}{国|guó}。{上海|Shàng hǎi}{我|wǒ}{去|qù}{过|guo}{一|yí}{次|cì}，{西安|Xī'ān}{去|qù}{过|guo}{两|liǎng}{次|cì}。{去年|qù nián}{我|wǒ}{和|hé}{妈妈|mā ma}{去|qù}{了|le}{长城|Cháng chéng}，{门票|mén piào}{不|bú}{贵|guì}，{四十|sì shí}{块|kuài}。{我们|wǒ men}{在|zài}{那儿|nàr}{住|zhù}{了|le}{两|liǎng}{天|tiān}，{酒店|jiǔ diàn}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}。{明年|míng nián}{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{出国|chū guó}{旅游|lǚ yóu}，{坐|zuò}{飞机|fēi jī}{去|qù}{安娜|Ān nà}{家|jiā}{看|kàn}{看|kàn}。" ({西安|Xī'ān}: Xi'an; {可是|kě shì}: but) Which is true?
choices: Wang Fang has been abroad once.
Wang Fang has been to Xi'an twice.
Wang Fang went to the Great Wall alone.
questions.explanation: {西安|Xī'ān}{去|qù}{过|guo}{两|liǎng}{次|cì}: twice to Xi'an (and once to Shanghai). She has never been abroad ({没|méi}{出|chū}{过|guo}{国|guó}), went to the Great Wall with her mother, and the ticket wasn't expensive ({不|bú}{贵|guì}).

questions.stem: Read Li Ming's message: "{我|wǒ}{去|qù}{过|guo}{那个|nà ge}{酒店|jiǔ diàn}，{它|tā}{离|lí}{机场|jī chǎng}{很|hěn}{近|jìn}，{打车|dǎ chē}{十|shí}{分钟|fēn zhōng}。{可是|kě shì}{酒店|jiǔ diàn}{的|de}{饭|fàn}{不|bú}{太|tài}{好吃|hǎo chī}。" What does he say about the hotel?
questions.explanation: {离|lí}{机场|jī chǎng}{很|hěn}{近|jìn}，{打车|dǎ chē}{十|shí}{分钟|fēn zhōng}: close to the airport, ten minutes by taxi. He has been there ({去|qù}{过|guo}), and the food isn't very good ({不|bú}{太|tài}{好吃|hǎo chī}).

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese.
questions.prompt: I've been to Beijing twice.
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{去|qù}{过|guo}{两|liǎng}{次|cì}{北京|Běi jīng}。 Verb + {过|guo} + number + {次|cì}, with the place name after {次|cì} or before it ({我|wǒ}{去|qù}{过|guo}{北京|Běi jīng}{两|liǎng}{次|cì}). {了|le} would report one trip, not the experience.

questions.stem: Write how many times you've been: "twice" (characters, or pinyin with tone marks): {我|wǒ}{去|qù}{过|guo}___。
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{去|qù}{过|guo}{两|liǎng}{次|cì}。 {两|liǎng} (not {二|èr}) before a measure word, and {次|cì} counts the times.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {旅游|lǚ yóu}, to travel: tones 3 + 2. {旅|lǚ} has ü, written with its dots after l.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {酒店|jiǔ diàn}, hotel: tones 3 + 4, a dip and then a fall.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {出国|chū guó}, to go abroad: tones 1 + 2, high and level, then rising.

questions.stem: Which is true about the Great Wall?
choices: It is many walls, built and rebuilt over more than two thousand years.
It is one wall, built in a single reign.
It was built in the twentieth century.
questions.explanation: The first walls go back to about the 7th century BC; walls were linked around 220 BC under the first emperor, and many later dynasties repaired and extended them. It runs far beyond Beijing.

questions.stem: Most of the Great Wall that stands today, including the famous sections near Beijing, was rebuilt under which dynasty?
questions.explanation: The Ming dynasty ({明朝|Míng cháo}, 1368–1644) rebuilt much of the wall in brick and stone. The Qin linked earlier walls around 220 BC, but little of that work is what visitors see.

questions.stem: Which statement about seeing the Great Wall from space is closest to the facts?
choices: It can be seen clearly from the Moon.
It is the only human-made structure visible from space.
It can't be seen from the Moon, and from orbit it is very hard to see.
Every astronaut who has flown over China has seen it.
questions.explanation: No human-made structure can be seen with the naked eye from the Moon. From low orbit the wall is narrow and close in colour to the land: a few astronauts say they glimpsed it in low sunlight, and China's first astronaut, {杨利伟|Yáng Lì wěi}, said in 2003 that he didn't see it.

questions.stem: In 2012 a national survey gave a length for all the walls of all periods together. About how long?
questions.explanation: The 2012 survey counted 21,196 km for all walls of all periods. About 8,850 km is an earlier figure for the Ming walls alone: the two numbers measure different things.

questions.stem: What does {长城|Cháng chéng} mean, word for word?
questions.explanation: {长|cháng} is "long", the lesson 02 word, and {城|chéng} is a city wall: "the long wall". "Ten thousand" comes in the fuller name, {万里长城|Wàn lǐ Cháng chéng}.

questions.stem: How is 长城 (the Great Wall) written in pinyin?
questions.explanation: {长城|Cháng chéng} is Cháng chéng: {长|cháng} is read cháng, "long", as in lesson 02 (zhǎng, "to grow", is another word). Both syllables rise.

questions.stem: Which section near Beijing is the most famous and the busiest, the first one restored and opened to visitors?
questions.explanation: {八达岭|Bā dá lǐng} (Bā dá lǐng), about 70 km from the city, reachable by train. {慕田峪|Mù tián yù} has a cable car and is usually quieter; {金山岭|Jīn shān lǐng} and {司马台|Sī mǎ tái} are farther away and partly unrestored.

questions.stem: The Great Wall's fuller name is {万里长城|Wàn lǐ Cháng chéng}. What does {万|wàn} mean?
questions.explanation: {万|wàn} is ten thousand (lesson 23): "the long wall of ten thousand li". It means "endless", not an exact length.

questions.stem: Listen. How many times has the speaker been to the Great Wall?
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{去|qù}{过|guo}{两|liǎng}{次|cì}{长城|Cháng chéng}: twice. Once would be {一|yí}{次|cì}, and never {没|méi}{去|qù}{过|guo}.

questions.stem: Listen. How did they get to the Great Wall?

audio.text: 我们是坐火车去长城的。

questions.explanation: {我们|wǒ men}{是|shì}{坐|zuò}{火车|huǒ chē}{去|qù}{长城|Cháng chéng}{的|de}: they went by train. {是|shì}…{的|de} gives the detail of a trip that has happened.

questions.stem: Read: "{上|shàng}{个|gè}{星期|xīng qī}{六|liù}，{我|wǒ}{和|hé}{同学|tóng xué}{一起|yì qǐ}{去|qù}{了|le}{长城|Cháng chéng}。{我们|wǒ men}{是|shì}{坐|zuò}{火车|huǒ chē}{去|qù}{的|de}，{路上|lù shang}{要|yào}{一|yí}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}。{长城上|Cháng chéng shang}{的|de}{人|rén}{很|hěn}{多|duō}，{有|yǒu}{中国|Zhōng guó}{人|rén}，{也|yě}{有|yǒu}{外国人|wài guó rén}。{我们|wǒ men}{走|zǒu}{了|le}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}，{很|hěn}{累|lèi}，{可是|kě shì}{很|hěn}{高兴|gāo xìng}。" ({一起|yì qǐ}: together; {可是|kě shì}: but) Which is true?
questions.explanation: {我们|wǒ men}{是|shì}{坐|zuò}{火车|huǒ chē}{去|qù}{的|de}: by train, an hour's journey. They walked for two hours ({走|zǒu}{了|le}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}), and there were lots of people, Chinese and foreign.

questions.stem: Read the end of the text: "{这|zhè}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{第|dì}{一|yī}{次|cì}{去|qù}{长城|Cháng chéng}，{下|xià}{次|cì}{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{和|hé}{我|wǒ}{爸爸|bà ba}{妈妈|mā ma}{一起|yì qǐ}{去|qù}。" Who does the writer want to go with next time?
questions.explanation: {下|xià}{次|cì}{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{和|hé}{我|wǒ}{爸爸|bà ba}{妈妈|mā ma}{一起|yì qǐ}{去|qù}: next time with Mum and Dad. This time ({第|dì}{一|yī}{次|cì}, the first time) the writer went with classmates.

questions.stem: Train tickets in China are "real-name" tickets. What does that mean?
choices: Each ticket is tied to the passenger's ID.
The ticket shows the train driver's name.
Only Chinese citizens can buy them.
They can only be bought at the station.
questions.explanation: Each ticket is linked to an ID document: a {身份证|shēn fèn zhèng} (identity card) or, for foreign visitors, a passport ({护照|hù zhào}). Tickets can be bought online (12306) as well as at stations.

questions.stem: What does a foreign visitor show at the station instead of a Chinese identity card?
questions.explanation: {护照|hù zhào}, the passport. {身份证|shēn fèn zhèng} is the Chinese identity card, {门票|mén piào} an admission ticket and {机票|jī piào} a plane ticket.

questions.stem: What is the {候车室|hòu chē shì} at a station?
questions.explanation: {候车室|hòu chē shì}, "wait-for-train room", is the waiting hall. The platform is {站台|zhàn tái}, the ticket gate {检票口|jiǎn piào kǒu} and the security check {安检|ān jiǎn}.

questions.stem: Your train number starts with G. What kind of train is it?
questions.explanation: G trains are the high-speed trains, {高铁|gāo tiě}, the fastest kind. D trains ({动车|dòng chē}) are fast too; Z, T and K are conventional trains.

questions.stem: What is {春运|chūn yùn}?
choices: the travel season around the Spring Festival
questions.explanation: {春运|chūn yùn}, "spring transport", is the roughly forty days around the Spring Festival when hundreds of millions of people travel home and back.

questions.stem: On a conventional overnight train, which ticket gets you a bunk in an open bay of six?
questions.explanation: {硬卧|yìng wò}, the hard sleeper: six bunks in an open bay. {软卧|ruǎn wò} is a closed compartment of four, {硬座|yìng zuò} a hard seat, and {无座|wú zuò} a ticket with no seat at all.

questions.stem: What is {二等座|èr děng zuò} on a high-speed train?
questions.explanation: {二等座|èr děng zuò} is second class, the usual seat, five across. First class is {一等座|yī děng zuò}, business class {商务座|shāng wù zuò}.

questions.stem: Your ticket says {北京南站|Běi jīng Nán zhàn}. Where do you go?
questions.explanation: {南|nán} is "south": {北京南站|Běi jīng Nán zhàn} is Beijing South station. Beijing has several stations far apart ({北京站|Běi jīng zhàn}, {北京西站|Běi jīng Xī zhàn}…), so check the ticket.

questions.stem: Listen. When does the train leave?

audio.text: 我们的火车十点二十开。

questions.explanation: {十|shí}{点|diǎn}{二十|èr shí}: twenty past ten. {开|kāi} here is "to set off" for a train.

questions.stem: Listen. Where did the speaker buy the ticket?
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{是|shì}{在|zài}{网上|wǎng shàng}{买|mǎi}{的|de}{票|piào}: online ({网上|wǎng shàng}, lesson 24). {是|shì}…{的|de} gives the detail of a past purchase, with {的|de} before the object {票|piào}.

questions.stem: Read Li Ming's message: "{我们|wǒ men}{是|shì}{十二|shí èr}{月|yuè}{二十|èr shí}{号|hào}{早上|zǎo shang}{八|bā}{点|diǎn}{的|de}{火车|huǒ chē}，{从|cóng}{北京南站|Běi jīng Nán zhàn}{开|kāi}，{下午|xià wǔ}{一|yī}{点|diǎn}{到|dào}{上海|Shàng hǎi}。{是|shì}{二等座|èr děng zuò}，{五|wǔ}{号|hào}{车厢|chē xiāng}。" ({车厢|chē xiāng}: coach) When does the train arrive in Shanghai?
questions.explanation: {下午|xià wǔ}{一|yī}{点|diǎn}{到|dào}{上海|Shàng hǎi}: it arrives at one in the afternoon. It leaves at eight in the morning ({早上|zǎo shang}{八|bā}{点|diǎn}).

questions.stem: Read the end of the message: "{北京南站|Běi jīng Nán zhàn}{离|lí}{我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{有点儿|yǒu diǎnr}{远|yuǎn}，{我们|wǒ men}{坐|zuò}{地铁|dì tiě}{去|qù}{吧|ba}。{七|qī}{点|diǎn}{在|zài}{地铁站|dì tiě zhàn}{门口|mén kǒu}{见|jiàn}！" Where will they meet?
choices: at the entrance of the metro station
questions.explanation: {七|qī}{点|diǎn}{在|zài}{地铁站|dì tiě zhàn}{门口|mén kǒu}{见|jiàn}: at seven, at the metro station entrance ({门口|mén kǒu}). Then they'll take the metro to Beijing South, which is a bit far.

questions.stem: You knock on a door. Which sentence means "Is anyone in there?"
questions.explanation: {里面|lǐ miàn} can stand on its own as a place word, so it opens the sentence before {有|yǒu}: {里面|lǐ miàn}{有|yǒu}{人|rén}{吗|ma}？ The short form {里|lǐ} needs a noun in front ({房间|fáng jiān}{里|lǐ}). The place comes before {有|yǒu}, and {有|yǒu} before what there is.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "We live on the fifth floor."?
questions.explanation: A number before {楼|lóu} is already a floor: {五|wǔ}{楼|lóu} is "the fifth floor", with no {第|dì}. The number comes first, as in {三|sān}{月|yuè} (March), and {在|zài} + place goes after the subject.

questions.stem: Which sentence is wrong?
choices: {手机|shǒu jī}{在|zài}{桌子|zhuō zi}{上面|shàng miàn}。
{手机|shǒu jī}{在|zài}{上面|shàng miàn}{桌子|zhuō zi}。
{桌子|zhuō zi}{上面|shàng miàn}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{手机|shǒu jī}。
questions.explanation: The position word follows the noun: {桌子|zhuō zi}{上面|shàng miàn} or {桌子|zhuō zi}{上|shàng}, "the table's top". {上面|shàng miàn}{桌子|zhuō zi} copies English "on top of the table". The last sentence is a correct existential sentence: place + {有|yǒu} + thing.

questions.stem: Choose the measure word: {我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{有|yǒu}{三|sān} ___ {房间|fáng jiān}。
questions.explanation: {间|jiān} counts rooms: {三|sān}{间|jiān}{房间|fáng jiān} ({个|gè} works too). {件|jiàn} sounds almost the same but falls and counts clothes and matters; {本|běn} is for books; {口|kǒu} counts family members.

questions.stem: In a building in China, which floor is {一|yī}{楼|lóu}?
choices: the first floor above street level
questions.explanation: {一|yī}{楼|lóu} is the floor you walk in on from the street, as the first floor is in the US. A British "first floor" is {二|èr}{楼|lóu}.

questions.stem: What is the pinyin of 楼 (building, floor)?
questions.explanation: 楼 is lóu, second tone: it rises. In {六|liù}{楼|lóu} (sixth floor) you hear a fall, then a rise.

questions.stem: Which pinyin is right for 床 (bed)?
questions.explanation: 床 is chuáng: ch (curled tongue, with a puff of air), the final uang, and a rising tone. zh has no puff of air, and chuān (without the g) would be a different syllable.

questions.stem: Which character completes the word {洗|xǐ}{手|shǒu} ___ (xǐ shǒu jiān, toilet)?
questions.explanation: Toilet is {洗手间|xǐ shǒu jiān}: 间 is 门 (door) with 日 inside, "a space between doors", the measure word for rooms. 问 (to ask) has 口 inside 门, 门 alone is a door, and 们 (the plural suffix) has 亻 beside 门.

questions.stem: What is the radical of 楼?
questions.explanation: 楼 has 木 (wood) on the left as its radical: buildings were once built of timber. {=The right side (a flattened 米 over 女) gives the sound, lóu.=} (Traditional {+楼+} has the older form of the sound part, 婁, on the right; the radical is still 木.)

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explanation: {上面|shàng miàn}, {下面|xià miàn}, {里面|lǐ miàn} and {外面|wài miàn} are the -{面|miàn} forms of {上|shàng}, {下|xià}, {里|lǐ} and {外|wài}, and can stand on their own. "Next to" is {旁边|páng biān}.

questions.stem: Listen. Where are the toilets?
choices: on the ground floor, on the left
questions.explanation: You heard {洗手间|xǐ shǒu jiān}{在|zài}{二|èr}{楼|lóu}: the toilets are on the second floor. For floors, 2 is {二|èr}, never {两|liǎng}.

questions.stem: Listen. What did the speaker say?
choices: It's warm outside and cold inside.
It's cold outside and warm inside.
questions.explanation: You heard {外面|wài miàn}{很|hěn}{冷|lěng}，{里面|lǐ miàn}{很|hěn}{热|rè}: outside it's cold, inside it's warm. {外面|wài miàn} and {里面|lǐ miàn} open each half as place words.

questions.stem: Listen. Where is the cat?
questions.explanation: You heard {我|wǒ}{的|de}{床|chuáng}{下面|xià miàn}{有|yǒu}{一|yì}{只|zhī}{猫|māo}: under my bed there's a cat. On the bed would be {床|chuáng}{上|shàng}, next to it {床|chuáng}{旁边|páng biān}.

questions.stem: Listen to the question. Which is the best reply?
questions.explanation: The question was {你|nǐ}{家|jiā}{在|zài}{几|jǐ}{楼|lóu}？ (Which floor is your flat on?), so the answer is a floor: {八|bā}{楼|lóu}. {三|sān}{间|jiān} answers "how many rooms"; {在|zài}{北京|Běi jīng} (Beijing) answers "where".

questions.stem: Read the notice ({出租|chū zū}: for rent): "{出租|chū zū}：{三|sān}{号|hào}{楼|lóu}{十二|shí èr}{楼|lóu}，{两|liǎng}{间|jiān}{房间|fáng jiān}，{一|yí}{个|gè}{洗手间|xǐ shǒu jiān}。{楼下|lóu xià}{有|yǒu}{超市|chāo shì}，{旁边|páng biān}{是|shì}{地铁|dì tiě}{站|zhàn}。" How many rooms does the flat have?
questions.explanation: {两|liǎng}{间|jiān}{房间|fáng jiān}: two rooms (and one toilet). {三|sān}{号|hào}{楼|lóu} is building number 3, and {十二|shí èr}{楼|lóu} the twelfth floor.

questions.stem: Read: "{李明|Lǐ Míng}{的|de}{房间|fáng jiān}{在|zài}{十二|shí èr}{楼|lóu}。{房间|fáng jiān}{不|bú}{大|dà}，{里面|lǐ miàn}{有|yǒu}{床|chuáng}{和|hé}{桌子|zhuō zi}。{他|tā}{的|de}{猫|māo}{很|hěn}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{在|zài}{床|chuáng}{上面|shàng miàn}{睡觉|shuì jiào}，{不|bù}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{在|zài}{外面|wài miàn}。" Where does the cat like to sleep?
questions.explanation: {在|zài}{床|chuáng}{上面|shàng miàn}{睡觉|shuì jiào}: it sleeps on the bed. It doesn't like being outside ({不|bù}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{在|zài}{外面|wài miàn}). Under the bed would be {床|chuáng}{下面|xià miàn}.

questions.stem: Read: "{请问|qǐng wèn}，{洗手间|xǐ shǒu jiān}{在|zài}{哪儿|nǎr}？——{在|zài}{里面|lǐ miàn}，{电视|diàn shì}{右边|yòu bian}。" Where is the toilet?
choices: outside, to the left of the TV
inside, to the right of the TV
questions.explanation: {在|zài}{里面|lǐ miàn} is "inside", and {电视|diàn shì}{右边|yòu bian} "to the right of the TV". Left would be {左边|zuǒ bian}, behind {后面|hòu miàn}, upstairs {楼上|lóu shàng}.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese.
questions.prompt: There's a cat under the bed.
questions.explanation: Place, then {有|yǒu}, then what there is: {床|chuáng}{下面|xià miàn}{有|yǒu}{一|yì}{只|zhī}{猫|māo}. The position word {下面|xià miàn} follows the noun {床|chuáng}. With {在|zài} the order would be the other way round: {猫|māo}{在|zài}{床|chuáng}{下面|xià miàn}.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese.
questions.prompt: The toilet is on the second floor, on the left.
questions.explanation: {洗手间|xǐ shǒu jiān}{在|zài}{二|èr}{楼|lóu}{的|de}{左边|zuǒ bian}: "the toilet is at the second floor's left side". A floor takes no {第|dì}.

questions.stem: You're filling in a form. Type "the fifth floor" in Chinese characters (pinyin with tones is accepted too): ___
questions.explanation: {五|wǔ}{楼|lóu}: the number, then {楼|lóu}, with no {第|dì}. With a pinyin keyboard, type wulou and pick 五楼, or type wu3lou2 for the pinyin.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the three syllables?
questions.explanation: {洗手间|xǐ shǒu jiān}, toilet: tones 3 + 3 + 1. The first third tone rises before the second, so you hear 2 + 3 + 1; both answers count.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {楼下|lóu xià}, downstairs: a rise, then a fall (2 + 4).

questions.stem: You're on the fifth floor. You want your friend in the street to come up to you. You say: {你|nǐ} ___ {吧|ba}！
questions.explanation: Up, and towards you, the speaker: {上来|shàng lái}. {上去|shàng qù} would send your friend up somewhere away from you; {下来|xià lái} and {下去|xià qù} go down.

questions.stem: Your friend is waiting for you downstairs. You call out "I'm coming down!": {我|wǒ} ___ ！
questions.explanation: You are moving down and away from where you are now, so it's {下去|xià qù}, although English says "coming". Chinese measures {来|lái} and {去|qù} from the speaker's own position. (You may also hear {我|wǒ}{下来|xià lái}, from your friend's side: lesson 09's exception.) {上去|shàng qù} and {上来|shàng lái} go up, and {出来|chū lái} is "come out".

questions.stem: Your friend is on the other side of the room. "Come over here a moment!" {你|nǐ} ___ {一下|yí xià}！
questions.explanation: {过来|guò lái}: across the room, towards you. {过去|guò qù} is "go over (there)", {起来|qǐ lái} "get up", {出去|chū qù} "go out".

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct? (He walked into the room, towards the speaker.)
questions.explanation: A place goes between the direction word and {来|lái} / {去|qù}: {走|zǒu}{进|jìn}{房间|fáng jiān}{来|lái}. It can never follow {来|lái} or {去|qù} (the first sentence), and it can't come before the verb or between {走|zǒu} and {进|jìn}.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "Please open your books."?
questions.explanation: Books, boxes and bags are opened with {打开|dǎ kāi}: {请|qǐng}{打开|dǎ kāi}{书|shū}. {开|kāi} alone opens doors and switches things on, but {开|kāi}{书|shū} isn't said. The object follows the whole verb.

questions.stem: Which word means getting up from anywhere (a bed, a chair, the floor), not only out of bed?
questions.explanation: {起来|qǐ lái} is the movement up from anywhere. {起床|qǐ chuáng} (HSK 1) is only getting out of bed. {上来|shàng lái} is coming up (the stairs), {过来|guò lái} coming over.

questions.stem: What is the pinyin of 拿 (to take, to hold)?
questions.explanation: 拿 is ná, rising. With other tones the same syllable is other words: {那|nà} (that) falls, {哪|nǎ} (which) dips. And it starts with n, not l.

questions.stem: Which pinyin is right for 打开 (to open)?
questions.explanation: 打开 is dǎ kāi: a third tone, then a first. The third tone before a first stays low (a "half third"), so it isn't said rising like dá.

questions.stem: What is the radical of 拿?
questions.explanation: 拿 is 合 (join) over 手 (hand), and its radical is 手, written in full at the bottom. The side form 扌 is what you see on the left of 打 and 找.

questions.stem: Which character completes the word {打|dǎ} ___ (dǎ kāi, to open)?
questions.explanation: {=To open is {打开|dǎ kāi}, with 开 (open): two horizontals over two legs, the left one curving. 升 (rise) has a left-falling stroke on top, 井 (a well) has two verticals crossing two horizontals, and 并 has two dots on top.=} (Simplified forms: in traditional script the word is {+{打开|dǎ kāi}+}.)

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explanation: {来|lái} is towards the speaker ({上来|shàng lái}, {过来|guò lái}), {去|qù} away ({下去|xià qù}); {起来|qǐ lái} is rising up. "Go out" would be {出去|chū qù}.

questions.stem: Listen. Where is the speaker?
questions.explanation: You heard {你|nǐ}{下来|xià lái}{吧|ba}，{我|wǒ}{在|zài}{楼下|lóu xià}: "Come down, I'm downstairs." {下来|xià lái} (towards the speaker) already tells you the speaker is below.

questions.stem: Listen. What will the speaker do?
choices: bring a glass of water over
questions.explanation: You heard {我|wǒ}{拿|ná}{一|yì}{杯|bēi}{水|shuǐ}{过来|guò lái}: "I'll bring a glass of water over (here)". {拿|ná} is take or carry, and {过来|guò lái} brings it towards where the speaker is talking from.

questions.stem: Listen. Where would you most likely hear this?
questions.explanation: You heard {请|qǐng}{打开|dǎ kāi}{书|shū}: "Please open your books", a teacher's instruction.

questions.stem: Listen. What happened?
questions.explanation: You heard {妈妈|mā ma}{走|zǒu}{过来|guò lái}{了|le}: Mum walked over, towards the speaker. "Went over there" would be {走|zǒu}{过去|guò qù}, "came upstairs" {走|zǒu}{上来|shàng lái}, "went out" {出去|chū qù}.

questions.stem: Read the message: "{我|wǒ}{在|zài}{楼上|lóu shàng}。{你|nǐ}{的|de}{书|shū}{我|wǒ}{拿|ná}{下来|xià lái}{了|le}，{在|zài}{门口|mén kǒu}。" Where is the book now?
questions.explanation: {在|zài}{门口|mén kǒu}: at the door. The writer brought it down ({拿|ná}{下来|xià lái}{了|le}) and is now upstairs again ({我|wǒ}{在|zài}{楼上|lóu shàng}).

questions.stem: Read: "{妈妈|mā ma}：{我|wǒ}{七|qī}{点|diǎn}{起来|qǐ lái}{了|le}。{早饭|zǎo fàn}{在|zài}{桌子|zhuō zi}{上|shàng}。{我|wǒ}{现在|xiàn zài}{出去|chū qù}，{下午|xià wǔ}{四|sì}{点|diǎn}{回来|huí lái}。{王芳|Wáng Fāng}" When will Wang Fang be back?
questions.explanation: {下午|xià wǔ}{四|sì}{点|diǎn}{回来|huí lái}: she'll come back at four in the afternoon. Seven ({七|qī}{点|diǎn}) is when she got up.

questions.stem: Wang Fang, on the sixth floor, phones Li Ming in the street: "{你|nǐ}{上来|shàng lái}{吧|ba}！" Li Ming answers: "{好|hǎo}，{我|wǒ}{上去|shàng qù}。" Why does Li Ming say {上去|shàng qù}?
choices: Because he is moving away from where he is now.
Because {上去|shàng qù} is more polite.
questions.explanation: Each speaker measures from their own position. For Wang Fang, upstairs, Li Ming comes towards her: {上来|shàng lái}. For Li Ming, in the street, he goes up and away from where he is: {上去|shàng qù}. Neither is more polite.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese. (You're downstairs.)
questions.prompt: Let's walk upstairs.
questions.explanation: The place {楼|lóu} goes between {上|shàng} and {去|qù}: {我们|wǒ men}{走|zǒu}{上|shàng}{楼|lóu}{去|qù}{吧|ba}. You're downstairs, moving away from where you are, so {去|qù}, not {来|lái}. {吧|ba} at the end makes it a suggestion.

questions.stem: Type the Chinese for "to open" (a book or a box), in characters or in pinyin with tones: ___
questions.explanation: {打开|dǎ kāi} (type da3kai1 for the pinyin): {打开|dǎ kāi}{书|shū}, {打开|dǎ kāi}{电视|diàn shì}. {开|kāi} alone opens doors but not books.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {门口|mén kǒu}, doorway: a rise, then a low dip (2 + 3).

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {电视|diàn shì}, television: two falling tones (4 + 4), as in {打开|dǎ kāi}{电视|diàn shì}.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I'm giving her a book."?
questions.explanation: With two objects the person comes first, then the thing: {送|sòng}{她|tā}{一|yì}{本|běn}{书|shū}, just like {给|gěi}{她|tā}{一|yì}{本|běn}{书|shū}. The person can't simply go at the end as in English "give a book to her", and the measure word stays between the number and the noun.
