questions.stem: The story says {爷爷|yé ye}{都|dōu}{七十|qī shí}{岁|suì}{了|le}. What does {都|dōu}……{了|le} add?
questions.explanation: {都|dōu} + age + {了|le} is "already…", with a feeling that it's a lot: he's already seventy, but still runs every morning. "Nearly" would be {快|kuài}{七十|qī shí}{岁|suì}{了|le}.

questions.stem: What does {奶奶|nǎi nai}{的|de}{生日|shēng rì}{快要|kuài yào}{到|dào}{了|le} mean?
choices: Grandma doesn't have a birthday party.
questions.explanation: {快要|kuài yào}……{了|le} is "about to": Grandma's birthday is about to come. A birthday that has passed would be {已经|yǐ jīng}{过|guò}{了|le}.

questions.stem: At the start of the story, {他|tā}{还|hái}{没|méi}{上|shàng}{过|guo}{网|wǎng}. What does it tell you about Grandpa?
choices: He doesn't want to go online.
questions.explanation: {没|méi} + verb + {过|guo} says something has never happened: {没|méi}{上|shàng}{过|guo}{网|wǎng}, never been online. {还|hái} adds "yet": he hasn't yet.

questions.stem: Listen. What was Grandpa doing?

audio.text: 爷爷拿着手机，看了很长时间。

choices: looking at the phone for a long time
questions.explanation: {爷爷|yé ye}{拿|ná}{着|zhe}{手机|shǒu jī}，{看|kàn}{了|le}{很|hěn}{长|cháng}{时间|shí jiān} — Grandpa, holding the phone, looked at it for a long time. {拿|ná}{着|zhe} (holding) is a state with {着|zhe}; {很|hěn}{长|cháng}{时间|shí jiān} is how long.

questions.stem: Listen. What does Grandma say?

audio.text: 我们家每个人都有新衣服了。

choices: Nobody in the family needs new clothes.
She doesn't like the new clothes.
Now everyone in the family has new clothes.
questions.explanation: {我们|wǒ men}{家|jiā}{每|měi}{个|gè}{人|rén}{都|dōu}{有|yǒu}{新|xīn}{衣服|yī fu}{了|le} — now everyone in our family has new clothes. {每|měi} + measure word + {都|dōu}: every one of them; {了|le} marks the new situation.

questions.stem: Listen. What does Grandpa decide?
choices: to go to the shopping centre next time
to go to the shopping centre today
questions.explanation: {下|xià}{次|cì}{我|wǒ}{还是|hái shi}{去|qù}{商场|shāng chǎng}{吧|ba} — next time I'd better go to the shopping centre. {还是|hái shi}……{吧|ba} is a decision after weighing the choices; {下|xià}{次|cì} is "next time".

questions.stem: In the story, Grandpa buys ten red tops online by mistake, and on Grandma's birthday the whole family wears them. Type their colour, "red", in characters (or pinyin with tones), two characters ending in {色|sè}: ___
questions.explanation: All ten tops are {红色|hóng sè} (red): {十|shí}{件|jiàn}{红色|hóng sè}{的|de}{衣服|yī fu}. In Chinese, red is the colour of celebrations, so a family dressed in red for a birthday dinner is a happy sight.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {饭馆|fàn guǎn}, restaurant: a falling fourth tone, then a low third tone (4+3), as in {一起|yì qǐ}{去|qù}{饭馆|fàn guǎn}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}。

questions.stem: A friend messages: {明天|míng tiān}{三|sān}{点|diǎn}{见|jiàn}？ Which reply means "OK!"?
questions.explanation: {好|hǎo}{的|de} is the usual friendly "OK" in messages. {不客气|bú kè qi} answers a thank-you, {没关系|méi guān xi} an apology, and {对不起|duì bu qǐ} is an apology itself.

questions.stem: Which greeting do you send at the Spring Festival (Chinese New Year)?
questions.explanation: {春节|Chūn jié}{快乐|kuài lè}！ — Happy Spring Festival! {新年|xīn nián}{快乐|kuài lè} works too. {生日|shēng rì}{快乐|kuài lè} is for birthdays, {明天|míng tiān}{见|jiàn} is "see you tomorrow", and {不好意思|bù hǎo yì si} an apology.

questions.stem: How do you write "Thank you for the flowers!"?
questions.explanation: What you're thanking for comes after {谢谢|xiè xie}{你|nǐ}, here as a noun with {的|de}: {谢谢|xiè xie}{你|nǐ}{的|de}{花|huā}！ (literally "thank you for your flowers").

questions.stem: You forgot a friend's birthday. Which message is right?
choices: {没关系|méi guān xi}，{我|wǒ}{忘|wàng}{了|le}{你|nǐ}{的|de}{生日|shēng rì}。
{不客气|bú kè qi}，{我|wǒ}{忘|wàng}{了|le}{你|nǐ}{的|de}{生日|shēng rì}。
{对不起|duì bu qǐ}，{我|wǒ}{忘|wàng}{了|le}{你|nǐ}{的|de}{生日|shēng rì}。
questions.explanation: For something you did wrong, apologise with {对不起|duì bu qǐ}: {对不起|duì bu qǐ}，{我|wǒ}{忘|wàng}{了|le}{你|nǐ}{的|de}{生日|shēng rì}。 {没关系|méi guān xi} is what the other person answers (never mind), and {不客气|bú kè qi} answers a thank-you.

questions.stem: Your friend writes: {不好意思|bù hǎo yì si}，{我|wǒ}{来|lái}{晚|wǎn}{了|le}。 What is the usual reply?
questions.explanation: {没关系|méi guān xi} (never mind) or {没事|méi shì} (it's nothing) answers an apology. {不客气|bú kè qi} (you're welcome) answers {谢谢|xiè xie}.

questions.stem: In which order do you write on a Chinese envelope?
choices: the name, then the address from small to big
the address from small to big, then the postcode
the postcode, the address from big to small, then the name and {收|shōu}
the name and the postcode only
questions.explanation: The postcode goes in the boxes at the top left, then the address from big to small (city, road, number, building, room), and last the name with {收|shōu}: {王芳|Wáng Fāng}{收|shōu}.

questions.stem: An envelope says {王芳|Wáng Fāng}（{女士|nǚ shì}）{收|shōu}. What does {收|shōu} tell you?
choices: The letter is to be received by Wang Fang.
Wang Fang has already read it.
questions.explanation: {收|shōu} (to receive) after the name means "to be received by": the letter is for Wang Fang. {女士|nǚ shì} is a polite title, like "Ms".

questions.stem:
Read the chat.

{安娜|Ān nà}：{我|wǒ}{到|dào}{了|le}！{你|nǐ}{在|zài}{哪儿|nǎr}？
{大卫|Dà wèi}：{不好意思|bù hǎo yì si}，{我|wǒ}{还|hái}{在|zài}{地铁|dì tiě}{上|shàng}，{十|shí}{分钟|fēn zhōng}{就|jiù}{到|dào}。 {安娜|Ān nà}：{好|hǎo}{的|de}，{我|wǒ}{在|zài}{门口|mén kǒu}{等|děng}{你|nǐ}。

Which is true?
choices: David is waiting at the door.
Anna is still on the metro.
David is still on the metro.
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{还|hái}{在|zài}{地铁|dì tiě}{上|shàng} — I'm still on the metro; {十|shí}{分钟|fēn zhōng}{就|jiù}{到|dào} — I'll be there in ten minutes. Anna has arrived ({我|wǒ}{到|dào}{了|le}) and waits at the door ({我|wǒ}{在|zài}{门口|mén kǒu}{等|děng}{你|nǐ}).

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker doing?
questions.explanation: {谢谢|xiè xie}{您|nín}{的|de}{帮忙|bāng máng}！ — Thank you for your help! {您|nín} makes it polite. Asking for help would be {你|nǐ}{能|néng}{帮|bāng}{我|wǒ}{一下|yí xià}{吗|ma}？

questions.stem: Listen. Why is the speaker apologising?

audio.text: 真不好意思，让你等了这么长时间。

choices: They kept the listener waiting a long time.
They took too much time to eat.
questions.explanation: {真|zhēn}{不好意思|bù hǎo yì si}，{让|ràng}{你|nǐ}{等|děng}{了|le}{这么|zhè me}{长|cháng}{时间|shí jiān}。 — I'm so sorry I kept you waiting so long. {让|ràng} + person + verb: "made you wait".

questions.stem: Listen. When would you say this?
questions.explanation: {祝|zhù}{你|nǐ}{生日|shēng rì}{快乐|kuài lè}！ — (I wish you a) happy birthday! {祝|zhù} is "to wish", an HSK 3 word you'll see on every card. At New Year it's {新年|xīn nián}{快乐|kuài lè}.

questions.stem: Write the reply "no problem" in characters (three characters), or in pinyin with tones: ___
questions.explanation: {没问题|méi wèn tí} is {没|méi} (not have) + {问题|wèn tí} (problem): "no problem". It's one of the most common short replies in messages, with {好|hǎo}{的|de} and {收到|shōu dào}.

glossary.definition: The official spelling of Mandarin in the Latin alphabet, with tone marks over the vowels: {姓名|xìng míng}. This course shows it above every character; the Pinyin switch hides it.

The pitch pattern that belongs to every Mandarin syllable and changes its meaning: first (high, level) ā, second (rising) á, third (low) ǎ, fourth (falling) à, and the neutral tone (unmarked). {买|mǎi} (to buy) and {卖|mài} (to sell) differ only in tone.
A short, light syllable with no tone of its own, written without a mark: the second syllable of {爷爷|yé ye}, {眼睛|yǎn jing} and {舒服|shū fu}, and particles such as {着|zhe}.

A change of tone caused by the next syllable. Two third tones: the first is said as a second ({所以|suǒ yǐ} sounds like suó yǐ); this change is never written. {一|yī} and {不|bù} change too, and this course writes their changes: {一下|yí xià}, {不|bú}{姓|xìng}.
A written unit of Chinese: one syllable, usually one meaning, and a shape made of strokes. 姓, 位 and 自 are characters; a word can have one ({姓|xìng}) or several ({自己|zì jǐ}).
A smaller shape that recurs inside characters and often hints at meaning or sound: 姓 is built from the components 女 and 生.
The component a dictionary files a character under, often a hint at its meaning: 女 in 姓 and 妻, 目 in 眼 and 睛, 衤 (clothing) in 裤.
Who or what a sentence is about, usually first: {他|tā} in {他|tā}{很|hěn}{高|gāo}.
What a sentence says about its subject: the verb or adjective and what goes with it. In {他|tā}{很|hěn}{高|gāo} the predicate is {很|hěn}{高|gāo}.

A sentence that names a topic and then says something about it in a small sentence of its own: {他|tā}{个子|gè zi}{很|hěn}{高|gāo} (he's tall: "him, height very tall"), {我|wǒ}{头|tóu}{疼|téng} (I have a headache). Chinese uses it where English uses "have" or "'s".
A word between a number (or {这|zhè}, {那|nà}, {每|měi}) and a noun: {一|yí}{位|wèi}{老师|lǎo shī}, {两|liǎng}{条|tiáo}{裤子|kù zi}, {每|měi}{个|gè}{人|rén}. {位|wèi} is the polite one for people.
A word or phrase that describes a noun and comes before it, often with {的|de}: {大大|dà dà}{的|de}{眼睛|yǎn jing}, {红色|hóng sè}{的|de}{衣服|yī fu}, {中国|Zhōng guó}{菜|cài}.

A word before a verb or adjective that adds degree, frequency, time or the like: {很|hěn}, {太|tài}, {也|yě}, {都|dōu}, {经常|jīng cháng}. Chinese adverbs go after the subject and before the verb, not at the end.

An adverb that says how often: {经常|jīng cháng} (often), {有时|yǒu shí} (sometimes). It goes before the verb (and before {在|zài} + place): {我们|wǒ men}{经常|jīng cháng}{在|zài}{家|jiā}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}. {有时|yǒu shí} can also start the sentence.

A verb that goes before another verb to add ability, need, permission or wish: {会|huì}, {能|néng}, {可以|kě yǐ}, {要|yào}, {想|xiǎng}. {你|nǐ}{要|yào}{吃|chī}{药|yào} (you should take medicine); {我|wǒ}{不|bù}{能|néng}{去|qù} (I can't go).

A verb made of a verb and its object, which come apart when something goes between them: {洗澡|xǐ zǎo} (to have a bath) → {洗|xǐ}{个|gè}{澡|zǎo}; {睡觉|shuì jiào}. When doubled, only the verb part doubles: {洗洗|xǐ xi}{手|shǒu}.
A position word after a noun that turns it into a place: {上|shàng}, {下|xià}, {里|lǐ}, {外|wài}… {书|shū}{上|shàng} (in the book, on the book), {手|shǒu}{上|shàng} (on the hand, on the wrist).

Saying a word or syllable twice. Verbs double to mean "a little, briefly" ({看看|kàn kan}), adjectives to make a description vivid ({大大|dà dà}{的|de}), and a few measure words to mean "every" ({天天|tiān tiān}). Family words such as {爷爷|yé ye} are doubled too, with no change of meaning.

Doubling an action verb to make it short, casual or tentative, like verb + {一下|yí xià}: one syllable AA ({看看|kàn kan}, also {看|kàn}{一|yi}{看|kàn}), two syllables ABAB ({介绍介绍|jiè shào jiè shào}), verb + object AAB ({洗洗|xǐ xi}{手|shǒu}). Not for states such as {是|shì}, {有|yǒu}, {喜欢|xǐ huan}.

Doubling an adjective for a vivid description: AA + {的|de} ({高高|gāo gāo}{的|de}, {长长|cháng cháng}{的|de}) and AABB + {的|de} ({漂漂亮亮|piào piào liàng liàng}{的|de}). It already means "very", so it never takes {很|hěn}, {太|tài} or {不|bù}.

How an action unfolds (completed, in progress, lasting, experienced) rather than when. Chinese marks it with particles and adverbs instead of tenses: {了|le} (completed), {在|zài} (in progress), {着|zhe} (lasting state), {过|guo} (experience, lesson 10).

The particle {着|zhe} after a verb: the state the action leaves behind is there and lasting. {他|tā}{穿|chuān}{着|zhe}{红色|hóng sè}{的|de}{衣服|yī fu} (he's wearing red), {电视|diàn shì}{开|kāi}{着|zhe} (the TV is on). Compare {在|zài} + verb, the action itself: {他|tā}{在|zài}{穿|chuān}{衣服|yī fu} (he's getting dressed). Negative: {没|méi} + verb.

A sentence linking a cause to its result. Chinese uses {因为|yīn wèi} (because) for the cause and {所以|suǒ yǐ} (so) for the result, often both: {因为|yīn wèi}{我|wǒ}{头|tóu}{疼|téng}，{所以|suǒ yǐ}{没|méi}{去|qù}{上课|shàng kè}。 Either can stand alone; {所以|suǒ yǐ} starts its clause.

A frame for one detail of something that has already happened: {是|shì} goes before the detail (how, when, where, who with, from where) and {的|de} after the verb. {你|nǐ}{是|shì}{怎么|zěn me}{来|lái}{的|de}？ {我|wǒ}{是|shì}{坐|zuò}{地铁|dì tiě}{来|lái}{的|de}。 (How did you get here? I came by metro.) Everyone knows the event took place; the frame asks or tells about it. {是|shì} can be left out in a positive sentence, the negative is {不|bú}{是|shì}…{的|de}, the verb takes no {了|le}, and the frame is never used for plans.

A verb of movement or {来|lái} / {去|qù} placed after a verb to show which way the action goes. In the simple form, {来|lái} means towards the speaker and {去|qù} away from the speaker: {进来|jìn lái} (come in: the speaker is inside), {出去|chū qù} (go out: the speaker is inside), {回来|huí lái} (come back here). A place goes before {来|lái} / {去|qù}: {回家|huí jiā}{去|qù}, {进|jìn}{房间|fáng jiān}{来|lái}. Compound forms add a second direction ({拿|ná}{出来|chū lái}, take out: lesson 12). After a verb, {来|lái} and {去|qù} are often light.

The light particle {过|guo} straight after a verb, saying that something has happened at least once at some time in the past, as an experience: {我|wǒ}{去|qù}{过|guo}{中国|Zhōng guó} (I've been to China). The negative is {没|méi}({有|yǒu}) + verb + {过|guo}, and {过|guo} stays: {我|wǒ}{没|méi}{去|qù}{过|guo}. Compare completed-action {了|le}, which reports one particular event: {我|wǒ}{昨天|zuó tiān}{去|qù}{了|le}{超市|chāo shì}.

A number phrase after the verb that says how many times or for how long something happens: number + {次|cì} ({我|wǒ}{去|qù}{过|guo}{两|liǎng}{次|cì}, I've been twice) or a length of time ({我|wǒ}{学习|xué xí}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}, I studied for an hour). It goes after the verb and its {了|le} / {过|guo}, unlike time words for "when", which go before the verb. A pronoun object comes before it ({见|jiàn}{过|guo}{他|tā}{一|yí}{次|cì}); an ordinary noun object usually after it ({吃|chī}{过|guo}{两|liǎng}{次|cì}{饺子|jiǎo zi}).

A two-part direction after a verb: first the way the thing moves ({上|shàng} up, {下|xià} down, {进|jìn} in, {出|chū} out, {回|huí} back, {过|guò} over, {起|qǐ} up from below), then {来|lái} (towards the speaker) or {去|qù} (away from the speaker): {拿|ná}{下来|xià lái} (bring down), {走|zǒu}{过去|guò qù} (walk over there), {拿|ná}{起来|qǐ lái} (pick up). A place goes before {来|lái} / {去|qù}: {走|zǒu}{上|shàng}{楼|lóu}{去|qù}. A thing can go there too ({拿|ná}{出|chū}{一|yì}{本|běn}{书|shū}{来|lái}) or, after a completed action, at the end. After a verb both parts are usually light.

A sentence that compares A with B: A {比|bǐ} B + adjective, as in {他|tā}{比|bǐ}{我|wǒ}{高|gāo} (he's taller than me). The adjective takes no {很|hěn}, {非常|fēi cháng} or {太|tài}; the size of the difference follows it ({高|gāo}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}, {大|dà}{三|sān}{岁|suì}). For the top of a group, use {最|zuì}: {他|tā}{最|zuì}{高|gāo}. "Not as … as" ({没有|méi yǒu}) comes in HSK 3.

Two objects after one verb: the person first, then the thing. {送|sòng}{她|tā}{花|huā} (give her flowers), {告诉|gào su}{我|wǒ}{你|nǐ}{的|de}{生日|shēng rì} (tell me your birthday), {给|gěi}{他|tā}{一|yì}{本|běn}{书|shū}, {问|wèn}{老师|lǎo shī}{一|yí}{个|gè}{问题|wèn tí}. The person can't simply move to the end as in English "give a book to him" (not {送|sòng}{花|huā}{她|tā}); with {送|sòng} you can also say {送给|sòng gěi} + person.

Saying that one thing is true and yet another is true too: {虽然|suī rán}…，{但是|dàn shì}… (although…, still…), as in {虽然|suī rán}{很|hěn}{累|lèi}，{但是|dàn shì}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{高兴|gāo xìng}. Chinese normally uses both words, where English uses only "although" or "but". {虽然|suī rán} goes before or after the first subject; {但是|dàn shì} (or {但|dàn}) starts the second half.

A verb or adjective placed right after the main verb to say what the action led to: {看完|kàn wán} (read to the end), {听懂|tīng dǒng} (understand what you hear), {做错|zuò cuò} (do wrong), {找到|zhǎo dào} (find). Nothing goes between the two parts; an object follows them ({看完|kàn wán}{那|nà}{本|běn}{书|shū}). Because a result either happened or didn't, the negative is {没|méi} + verb + complement, with no {了|le}: {我|wǒ}{没|méi}{听懂|tīng dǒng}.

A description after a verb, joined to it by {得|de}, saying how well, fast or early the action is done: {她|tā}{说|shuō}{得|de}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo} (she speaks well), {你|nǐ}{来|lái}{得|de}{真|zhēn}{早|zǎo} (you're early). The part after {得|de} works like an adjective predicate (usually with {很|hěn}), and it carries the negative: {说|shuō}{得|de}{不|bù}{好|hǎo}. With an object, the verb is said twice ({说|shuō}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{说|shuō}{得|de}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}) or the object goes first ({他|tā}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{说|shuō}{得|de}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}).

The particle {地|de} after a description and before the verb, saying how the action is done, like English -ly: {慢慢|màn màn}{地|de}{说|shuō} (speak slowly), {高高兴兴|gāo gāo xìng xìng}{地|de}{回|huí}{家|jiā} (go home happily). The three particles said *de* are told apart by position: {的|de} before a noun, {地|de} before a verb, {得|de} after a verb.

A sentence in which one person is both the object of the first verb and the subject of the second: {老师|lǎo shī}{让|ràng}{我们|wǒ men}{读|dú}{书|shū} (the teacher has us read): {我们|wǒ men} is let or made by the teacher, and does the reading. The first verb is usually {让|ràng} (let, make), {请|qǐng} (invite, ask) or {教|jiāo} (teach); {不|bù} or {没|méi} goes before it: {妈妈|mā ma}{不|bú}{让|ràng}{我|wǒ}{看|kàn}{电视|diàn shì}.

A separable verb (verb + object, like {帮忙|bāng máng}, {跳舞|tiào wǔ}, {游泳|yóu yǒng}, {睡觉|shuì jiào}) with an amount, a person or {了|le} placed between its two halves: {帮|bāng}{我|wǒ}{一|yí}{个|gè}{忙|máng} (do me a favour), {帮|bāng}{了|le}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{忙|máng}, {跳|tiào}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}{的|de}{舞|wǔ} (danced for an hour). The whole word can't take an object: say {帮|bāng}{我|wǒ}, never {帮忙|bāng máng} + a person.

A question that offers options and asks the listener to pick one, with {还是|hái shi} ("or") between them: {你|nǐ}{喝|hē}{咖啡|kā fēi}{还是|hái shi}{喝|hē}{茶|chá}？ (Are you having coffee or tea?). It takes no {吗|ma}; the answer names the choice. In statements, "or" is {或者|huò zhě} (HSK 3).

Ways to give a number roughly: {几|jǐ} for "a few" or "-odd" ({十几|shí jǐ}{个|gè}, 11–19; {几十|jǐ shí}{个|gè}, dozens), {多|duō} after a round number for "and a bit" ({二十多|èr shí duō}{块|kuài}, twenty-odd kuai) or after the measure word below ten ({一|yí}{个|gè}{多|duō}{小时|xiǎo shí}), and two neighbouring numbers ({两三|liǎng sān}{个|gè}, two or three).

Telling someone not to do something: {别|bié} + verb, as in {别|bié}{走|zǒu}！ (Don't go!). With {了|le} at the end it means "stop…, don't bother": {别|bié}{说|shuō}{了|le}！ {不要|bú yào} + verb means the same and sounds a little firmer; {不|bù} and {没|méi} alone don't give orders.

A two-part frame that always goes together, with words filled in between: {快要|kuài yào}……{了|le} (about to), {都|dōu}……{了|le} ("already!"), {还是|hái shi}……{吧|ba} (we'd better), {还|hái}{没|méi}……{呢|ne} (not yet), {因为|yīn wèi}……{所以|suǒ yǐ}, {虽然|suī rán}……{但是|dàn shì}. {什么|shén me}{的|de} at the end of a list (and so on) is a fixed phrase of the same kind. Learn the frame whole: {快要|kuài yào}{下雨|xià yǔ}{了|le}, {都|dōu}{十|shí}{点|diǎn}{了|le}, {我们|wǒ men}{还是|hái shi}{坐|zuò}{地铁|dì tiě}{吧|ba}.

Reading a whole text quickly for its general idea: what kind of text it is, who wrote it and to whom. With a notice, the title ({通知|tōng zhī}) and the name and date at the bottom tell you most of this before you read the middle.

Looking through a text for one fact, such as a time, a place, a name or a price, without reading everything. Read the question first, then look for the characters that carry that fact: {点|diǎn} and {号|hào} for times, {在|zài} and {楼|lóu} for places, {元|yuán} and {块|kuài} for prices.

The official test of Chinese for speakers of other languages ({汉语水平考试|Hàn yǔ shuǐ píng kǎo shì}). Its new version, often called HSK 3.0, has nine levels; its syllabus has been in force since July 2026. Level 2 covers 500 words and 371 characters, with 60 questions in about 60 minutes: listening, reading and a short writing part, as reported from the sample paper (no speaking test at this level).

references.title: The 125 characters of HSK 2
references.body:
Every new character of this course in the order it is taught. With the 246 of HSK 1 they make the 371 characters of the level. Pinyin gives the readings our words use ("and others" when the character has more readings in later levels). Radical is the one the stroke-order data (Make Me a Hanzi) gives, which is usually but not always the radical a dictionary files it under. Strokes follow mainland stroke order. ✎ marks the characters HSK expects you to write by hand at levels 1–2; all 100 are listed in the second table.

The list shows the simplified forms the course teaches, so it stays in simplified characters when the script switch is on Traditional; the Traditional column gives the Taiwan form the switch shows ("same" when the two scripts write it alike, and the form each of our words uses when a character has two). Radicals and stroke counts are those of the simplified form.

references.title: Comparing (比, 最, 跟…一起)
references.body:
## A {比|bǐ} B + adjective

| Pattern | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| A {比|bǐ} B + adjective | {哥哥|gē ge}{比|bǐ}{我|wǒ}{高|gāo}。 | My brother is taller than me. |
| … + {一点儿|yì diǎnr} | {这个|zhè ge}{比|bǐ}{那个|nà ge}{贵|guì}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}。 | This one is a little more expensive than that one. |
| … + number + measure word | {他|tā}{比|bǐ}{我|wǒ}{大|dà}{三|sān}{岁|suì}。 | He's three years older than me. |
| … + amount of money | {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{比|bǐ}{那|nà}{件|jiàn}{便宜|pián yi}{五十|wǔ shí}{块|kuài}。 | This one is fifty yuan cheaper than that one. |
| question with {吗|ma} | {今天|jīn tiān}{比|bǐ}{昨天|zuó tiān}{热|rè}{吗|ma}？ | Is today hotter than yesterday? |
| question word | {谁|shéi}{比|bǐ}{你|nǐ}{高|gāo}？ | Who is taller than you? |
| {不比|bù bǐ} (contradicting) | {他|tā}{不|bù}{比|bǐ}{你|nǐ}{高|gāo}。 | He's no taller than you. |

- Nothing goes before the adjective: no {很|hěn}, {非常|fēi cháng}, {真|zhēn} or {太|tài}.
  ~~{他|tā}{比|bǐ}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{高|gāo}~~.
- The difference goes **after** the adjective: {大|dà}{三|sān}{岁|suì}, not ~~{三|sān}{岁|suì}{大|dà}~~.
- Ages: {大|dà} (older) and {小|xiǎo} (younger).
- Coming in HSK 3: {多了|duō le} / {得多|de duō} (much more), {没有|méi yǒu} (not as … as:
  {他|tā}{没有|méi yǒu}{你|nǐ}{高|gāo}), {跟|gēn}…{一样|yí yàng} (the same as).

## {最|zuì}: the most

| Pattern | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| {最|zuì} + adjective | {哪个|nǎ ge}{最|zuì}{便宜|pián yi}？ | Which one is the cheapest? |
| {最|zuì} + verb of liking | {你|nǐ}{最|zuì}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{什么|shén me}{颜色|yán sè}？ | What's your favourite colour? |
| group as topic + {最|zuì} | {我们|wǒ men}{家|jiā}{我|wǒ}{最|zuì}{高|gāo}。 | I'm the tallest in our family. |
| {最|zuì}{好|hǎo} | {这个|zhè ge}{最|zuì}{好|hǎo}。 | This one is the best. |

{最|zuì} takes no {很|hěn}.

## Words for comparing (lesson 14)

| Word | Meaning | Opposite |
|---|---|---|
| {快|kuài} | fast; quickly ({快|kuài}{来|lái}！) | {慢|màn} slow ({慢慢|màn màn}{说|shuō}, {慢|màn}{走|zǒu}！) |
| {好|hǎo} | good | {坏|huài} bad; broken ({坏|huài}{了|le}) |
| {对|duì} | right | {错|cuò} wrong |
| {不错|bú cuò} | pretty good (real praise) | |
| {高|gāo}, {大|dà}, {贵|guì}, {多|duō} | tall, big / older, expensive, many | {矮|ǎi} (HSK 3), {小|xiǎo}, {便宜|pián yi}, {少|shǎo} |

## {跟|gēn}: with

| Pattern | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| {跟|gēn} + person + verb | {我|wǒ}{跟|gēn}{妈妈|mā ma}{去|qù}{超市|chāo shì}。 | I'm going to the supermarket with Mum. |
| {跟|gēn} + person + {一起|yì qǐ} + verb | {我|wǒ}{跟|gēn}{朋友|péng you}{一起|yì qǐ}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}。 | I'm eating with friends. |
| {跟|gēn} + person + {说|shuō} | {你|nǐ}{跟|gēn}{他|tā}{说|shuō}{吧|ba}。 | You tell him. |
| {跟|gēn} + person (follow) | {跟|gēn}{我|wǒ}{来|lái}。 / {跟|gēn}{我|wǒ}{读|dú}。 | Come with me. / Repeat after me. |

{跟|gēn} + person goes before the verb, like {在|zài} + place. {和|hé} can replace it in the first
two patterns; {跟|gēn} sounds more spoken. {一起|yì qǐ} (together) is lesson 20's word.

references.title: Direction complements
references.body:
## The rule: {来|lái} towards the speaker, {去|qù} away

A direction complement follows a verb and says which way the action goes. {来|lái} means "towards the
speaker (or the place the story is told from)", {去|qù} "away from the speaker". Measure from where the
speaker is. One exception is common: for your own movement towards the person you're speaking to,
you can measure from where they are ({我|wǒ}{马上|mǎ shàng}{出来|chū lái}, "I'll be right out", to a friend waiting outside;
{马上|mǎ shàng}, right away, is HSK 3).

| Speaker is | Someone comes in | Someone goes out | Someone returns |
|---|---|---|---|
| inside / at home | {进来|jìn lái} ({请|qǐng}{进来|jìn lái}！) | {出去|chū qù} ({他|tā}{出去|chū qù}{了|le}。) | {回来|huí lái} ({我|wǒ}{回来|huí lái}{了|le}！) |
| outside / away | {进去|jìn qù} ({我们|wǒ men}{进去|jìn qù}{吧|ba}。) | {出来|chū lái} ({你|nǐ}{出来|chū lái}{吧|ba}！) | {回去|huí qù} ({我|wǒ}{明天|míng tiān}{回去|huí qù}。) |

## Simple direction complements: verb + {来|lái} / {去|qù}

| Verb | + {来|lái} | + {去|qù} | Lesson |
|---|---|---|---|
| {进|jìn} enter | {进来|jìn lái} come in | {进去|jìn qù} go in | 09 |
| {出|chū} exit | {出来|chū lái} come out | {出去|chū qù} go out | 09 |
| {回|huí} return | {回来|huí lái} come back | {回去|huí qù} go back | 09 |
| {上|shàng} go up | {上来|shàng lái} come up | {上去|shàng qù} go up | 12 |
| {下|xià} go down | {下来|xià lái} come down | {下去|xià qù} go down | 12 |
| {过|guò} pass | {过来|guò lái} come over | {过去|guò qù} go over | 12 |
| {起|qǐ} rise | {起来|qǐ lái} get up | — | 12 |

There is no ~~{起|qǐ}{去|qù}~~: rising is always {起来|qǐ lái}.

## Where the place goes

A place goes **between** the verb and {来|lái} / {去|qù}, never after them:

| Right | Wrong |
|---|---|
| {回家|huí jiā}{去|qù}, {回家|huí jiā}{来|lái} | ~~{回去|huí qù}{家|jiā}~~ |
| {进|jìn}{房间|fáng jiān}{来|lái} | ~~{进来|jìn lái}{房间|fáng jiān}~~ |
| {回|huí}{中国|Zhōng guó}{去|qù} | ~~{回去|huí qù}{中国|Zhōng guó}~~ |

With a place named, {来|lái} / {去|qù} can be left out: {回家|huí jiā}, {进|jìn}{商店|shāng diàn}, {出门|chū mén}.

## Compound direction complements: verb + direction + {来|lái} / {去|qù}

The words in the table above can follow another verb, so the verb says *how* and the complement
says *which way* (lesson 12):

| Verb | + {进来|jìn lái} / {进去|jìn qù} | + {出来|chū lái} / {出去|chū qù} | + {上来|shàng lái} / {上去|shàng qù} | + {下来|xià lái} / {下去|xià qù} | + {回来|huí lái} / {回去|huí qù} | + {过来|guò lái} / {过去|guò qù} | + {起来|qǐ lái} |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| {走|zǒu} walk | {走|zǒu}{进来|jìn lái} | {走|zǒu}{出去|chū qù} | {走|zǒu}{上去|shàng qù} | {走|zǒu}{下来|xià lái} | {走|zǒu}{回去|huí qù} | {走|zǒu}{过来|guò lái} | — |
| {拿|ná} take | {拿|ná}{进去|jìn qù} | {拿|ná}{出来|chū lái} | {拿|ná}{上去|shàng qù} | {拿|ná}{下来|xià lái} | {拿|ná}{回来|huí lái} | {拿|ná}{过来|guò lái} | {拿|ná}{起来|qǐ lái} (pick up) |

- A place goes before the final {来|lái} / {去|qù}: {走|zǒu}{进|jìn}{房间|fáng jiān}{来|lái}, {走|zǒu}{回家|huí jiā}{去|qù}.
- An ordinary object can go before the final {来|lái} / {去|qù} or after the whole complement:
  {拿|ná}{出|chū}{一|yì}{本|běn}{书|shū}{来|lái} / {拿|ná}{出来|chū lái}{一|yì}{本|běn}{书|shū} (take out a book). Lesson 12 teaches the first.

## Tones, negatives and {了|le}

- After a verb, {来|lái} and {去|qù} are usually light: jìn lai, chū qu, ná chu lai. Dictionaries and this
  course write the full tones.
- Negative of a past movement: {没|méi} + verb + complement: {他|tā}{没|méi}{回来|huí lái} (he didn't come back / hasn't come
  back). For a decision or the future: {不|bù}: {他|tā}{不|bù}{回来|huí lái}{了|le} (he isn't coming back after all).
- {了|le} for a change: {他|tā}{出去|chū qù}{了|le} (he's gone out), {他|tā}{回来|huí lái}{了|le} (he's back).

references.title: Result and degree complements (看完, 说得很好, 的 / 地 / 得)
references.body:
## Result complements: verb + result

The second word says how the action came out. Nothing goes between the two parts.

| Complement | Result | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| {完|wán} | finished, to the end | {看完|kàn wán}, {做完|zuò wán}, {写完|xiě wán}, {吃完|chī wán}, {考完|kǎo wán} |
| {懂|dǒng} | understood | {听懂|tīng dǒng} (by listening), {看懂|kàn dǒng} (by reading) |
| {错|cuò} | wrong | {做错|zuò cuò}, {写错|xiě cuò}, {听错|tīng cuò}, {说错|shuō cuò} |
| {对|duì} | right | {做对|zuò duì}, {说对|shuō duì} |
| {好|hǎo} | done properly, ready | {写好|xiě hǎo}, {做好|zuò hǎo}, {准备好|zhǔn bèi hǎo} |
| {到|dào} | reached, got | {找到|zhǎo dào} (find), {买到|mǎi dào}, {看到|kàn dào}, {听到|tīng dào} |
| {见|jiàn} | perceived | {看见|kàn jiàn}, {听见|tīng jiàn} |
| {会|huì} | now able | {学会|xué huì} |
| {开|kāi} | open | {打开|dǎ kāi} |

| Form | Pattern | Example |
|---|---|---|
| statement | verb + result ({了|le}) | {我|wǒ}{听懂|tīng dǒng}{了|le}。 I understood. |
| with an object | verb + result ({了|le}) + object | {我|wǒ}{看完|kàn wán}{了|le}{那|nà}{本|běn}{书|shū}。 I've finished that book. |
| object as topic | object + subject + verb + result | {那|nà}{本|běn}{书|shū}{我|wǒ}{看完|kàn wán}{了|le}。 |
| negative | {没|méi}({有|yǒu}) + verb + result, no {了|le} | {我|wǒ}{没|méi}{听懂|tīng dǒng}。 I didn't understand. |
| question | …{了|le}{吗|ma}？ / …{了|le}{没有|méi yǒu}？ | {你|nǐ}{做完|zuò wán}{了|le}{吗|ma}？ Have you finished? |

- {找|zhǎo} is "look for"; {找到|zhǎo dào} is "find". {听|tīng} is "listen"; {听懂|tīng dǒng} is "understand".
- ~~{我|wǒ}{不|bù}{听懂|tīng dǒng}~~ is wrong: a result that didn't happen takes {没|méi}. ({听不懂|tīng bu dǒng},
  "can't understand", is a different form, taught in HSK 3.)

## Degree complements: verb + {得|de} + description

| Form | Pattern | Example |
|---|---|---|
| statement | verb + {得|de} + ({很|hěn}) adjective | {她|tā}{说|shuō}{得|de}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}。 She speaks well. |
| negative | verb + {得|de} + {不|bù} + adjective | {他|tā}{说|shuō}{得|de}{不|bù}{好|hǎo}。 He doesn't speak well. |
| question | verb + {得|de} + A-not-A / {怎么样|zěn me yàng} | {他|tā}{唱|chàng}{得|de}{好|hǎo}{不|bu}{好|hǎo}？ {她|tā}{跳|tiào}{得|de}{怎么样|zěn me yàng}？ |
| with an object (1) | verb + object + verb + {得|de}… | {他|tā}{说|shuō}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{说|shuō}{得|de}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}。 |
| with an object (2) | object first, verb + {得|de}… | {他|tā}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{说|shuō}{得|de}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}。 |

- Never put the object between the verb and {得|de}: ~~{说|shuō}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{得|de}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}~~.
- With separable verbs, use the plain verb ({游|yóu}{得|de}{很|hěn}{快|kuài}, {跑|pǎo}{得|de}{很|hěn}{快|kuài}) or say it
  twice ({跳舞|tiào wǔ}{跳|tiào}{得|de}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}).

| Result complement | Degree complement |
|---|---|
| {写好|xiě hǎo}{了|le}: finished writing it (it's ready) | {写|xiě}{得|de}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}: writes well |
| negative {没|méi}{写好|xiě hǎo} | negative {写|xiě}{得|de}{不|bù}{好|hǎo} |

## Manner before the verb: description + {地|de} + verb

| Example | Meaning |
|---|---|
| {慢慢|màn màn}{地|de}{说|shuō} | speak slowly |
| {高高兴兴|gāo gāo xìng xìng}{地|de}{回|huí}{家|jiā} | go home happily |
| {很|hěn}{快|kuài}{地|de}{吃|chī}{完|wán} | eat up quickly |

## The three *de*

| Particle | Position | Joins | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| {的|de} | before a noun | description + noun | {漂亮|piào liang}{的|de}{衣服|yī fu} pretty clothes |
| {地|de} | before a verb | description + verb | {慢慢|màn màn}{地|de}{走|zǒu} walk slowly |
| {得|de} | after a verb | verb + description | {走|zǒu}{得|de}{很|hěn}{慢|màn} walks slowly |

All three are said *de*, with a light tone.

## Duration and times after the verb

| Pattern | Example |
|---|---|
| verb + {了|le} + duration | {我|wǒ}{游|yóu}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}。 I swam for an hour. |
| verb + duration ({的|de}) + object | {他们|tā men}{踢|tī}{了|le}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}{的|de}{足球|zú qiú}。 |
| verb + object + verb + duration | {他们|tā men}{踢|tī}{足球|zú qiú}{踢|tī}{了|le}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}。 |
| separable verb with a quantity | {帮|bāng}{我|wǒ}{一|yí}{个|gè}{忙|máng}, {跳|tiào}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}{的|de}{舞|wǔ} |
| a short while | {等|děng}{一会儿|yí huìr}, {休息|xiū xi}{一会儿|yí huìr} |

references.title: 过, 着 and 了
references.body:
## Three particles after the verb

All three are light syllables that go straight after a verb. None of them is a tense: they say how
an action is seen, not when it happened.

| Particle | Says | Example | Lesson |
|---|---|---|---|
| {了|le} | the action happened, as one completed event | {我|wǒ}{昨天|zuó tiān}{买|mǎi}{了|le}{一|yì}{本|běn}{书|shū}。 I bought a book yesterday. | HSK 1, 25 |
| {过|guo} | it has happened at least once: an experience | {我|wǒ}{去|qù}{过|guo}{北京|Běi jīng}。 I've been to Beijing. | 10 |
| {着|zhe} | the state it leaves is still there | {门|mén}{开|kāi}{着|zhe}。 The door is open. | 03 |

And at the end of a sentence: {了|le} for a change or a new situation ({下雨|xià yǔ}{了|le}, it's started raining; {他|tā}
{回来|huí lái}{了|le}, he's back), HSK 1 lesson 20.

## Negatives and questions

| | {了|le} | {过|guo} | {着|zhe} |
|---|---|---|---|
| Statement | {我|wǒ}{买|mǎi}{了|le}。 | {我|wǒ}{去|qù}{过|guo}。 | {门|mén}{开|kāi}{着|zhe}。 |
| Negative | {我|wǒ}{没|méi}{买|mǎi}。 ({了|le} drops) | {我|wǒ}{没|méi}{去|qù}{过|guo}。 ({过|guo} stays) | {门|mén}{没|méi}{开|kāi}。 ({着|zhe} usually drops) |
| Question | {你|nǐ}{买|mǎi}{了|le}{吗|ma}？ / {你|nǐ}{买|mǎi}{了|le}{没有|méi yǒu}？ | {你|nǐ}{去|qù}{过|guo}{吗|ma}？ / {你|nǐ}{去|qù}{过|guo}{没有|méi yǒu}？ | {门|mén}{开|kāi}{着|zhe}{吗|ma}？ / {门|mén}{开|kāi}{着|zhe}{没有|méi yǒu}？ |

All three are negated with {没|méi}, never {不|bù}.

## {了|le} or {过|guo}?

| | {了|le} | {过|guo} |
|---|---|---|
| Thinks of | one particular event | your experience, life so far |
| Time words | usually definite: {昨天|zuó tiān}, {上午|shàng wǔ}, {八|bā}{点|diǎn} | often none, or loose: {去年|qù nián}, {以前|yǐ qián} |
| Still true? | {他|tā}{去|qù}{了|le}{上海|Shàng hǎi}。 He went to Shanghai (and may be there now). | {他|tā}{去|qù}{过|guo}{上海|Shàng hǎi}。 He has been to Shanghai (the trip is over). |
| Negative | {没|méi}{去|qù} (didn't go, that time) | {没|méi}{去|qù}{过|guo} (has never been) |

## With a number of times or a length of time

A quantity complement follows the verb and its {了|le} / {过|guo}:

- {我|wǒ}{去|qù}{过|guo}{两|liǎng}{次|cì}。 I've been twice.
- {我|wǒ}{在|zài}{北京|Běi jīng}{住|zhù}{了|le}{三|sān}{天|tiān}。 I stayed in Beijing for three days.
- {我|wǒ}{见|jiàn}{过|guo}{他|tā}{一|yí}{次|cì}。 I've met him once. (a pronoun object comes before the number)
- {我|wǒ}{吃|chī}{过|guo}{一|yí}{次|cì}{饺子|jiǎo zi}。 I've had dumplings once. (an ordinary noun comes after it)

## {是|shì}…{的|de}: asking about the details

When an event is known to have happened, {是|shì}…{的|de} frames one detail (how, when, where, who with). The
verb inside takes no {了|le} or {过|guo} (lesson 08):

| News: did it happen? | Detail: how / when / where? |
|---|---|
| {他|tā}{来|lái}{了|le}。 He's come. | {他|tā}{是|shì}{坐|zuò}{飞机|fēi jī}{来|lái}{的|de}。 He came by plane. |
| {你|nǐ}{到|dào}{了|le}{吗|ma}？ Have you arrived? | {你|nǐ}{是|shì}{什么|shén me}{时候|shí hou}{到|dào}{的|de}？ When did you arrive? |

## Which one? A quick test

- "Have you ever…?", "I've never…" → {过|guo}.
- "I did it (that time)" → {了|le} after the verb; "now it's different" → {了|le} at the end.
- "It's on / open / written / being worn" → {着|zhe}.
- "How / when / where did it happen?" → {是|shì}…{的|de}.

references.title: Numbers in HSK 2
references.body:
## Big numbers: counting in {万|wàn}

Chinese groups digits in fours. After {千|qiān} (1,000) comes {万|wàn} (10,000); count four digits
from the right and put {万|wàn} there.

| Number | Chinese | Note |
|---|---|---|
| 10,000 | {一万|yí wàn} | {一|yī} → *yí* before the fourth tone |
| 12,000 | {一万|yí wàn}{两千|liǎng qiān} | 1 \| 2000 |
| 20,000 | {两万|liǎng wàn} | {两|liǎng} before {万|wàn}, as before {千|qiān} |
| 25,000 | {两万|liǎng wàn}{五千|wǔ qiān} | said short: {两万五|liǎng wàn wǔ} |
| 10,500 | {一万|yí wàn}{零|líng}{五百|wǔ bǎi} | {零|líng} fills the empty thousands place |
| 38,600 | {三万|sān wàn}{八千|bā qiān}{六百|liù bǎi} | |
| 100,000 | {十万|shí wàn} | "ten ten-thousands" |
| 150,000 | {十五万|shí wǔ wàn} | |
| 990,000 | {九十九万|jiǔ shí jiǔ wàn} | |
| 1,000,000 | {一百万|yì bǎi wàn} | "a hundred ten-thousands" |

## Approximate numbers

| Pattern | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| {几|jǐ} + measure word | {几|jǐ}{个|gè}{人|rén} | a few people (statement) |
| {十几|shí jǐ} + measure word | {十几|shí jǐ}{个|gè}{人|rén} | 11–19 people, a dozen or so |
| {几十|jǐ shí} + measure word | {几十|jǐ shí}{个|gè}{人|rén} | dozens of people |
| {几|jǐ}{百|bǎi} / {几|jǐ}{千|qiān} / {几|jǐ}{万|wàn} | {几|jǐ}{百|bǎi}{块|kuài} | a few hundred kuai |
| round number + {多|duō} + measure word | {二十多|èr shí duō}{个|gè}{人|rén} | twenty-odd people (21–29) |
| | {一百多|yì bǎi duō}{块|kuài} | a hundred-odd kuai |
| | {三万多|sān wàn duō}{块|kuài} | thirty thousand-odd kuai |
| number 1–9 + measure word + {多|duō} | {一|yí}{个|gè}{多|duō}{小时|xiǎo shí} | an hour and a bit |
| | {三|sān}{块|kuài}{多|duō} | three kuai and a bit (3.10–3.90) |
| | {半|bàn}{个|gè}{多|duō}{小时|xiǎo shí} | over half an hour |
| two neighbouring numbers | {两三|liǎng sān}{个|gè}{人|rén} | two or three people |
| | {三四|sān sì}{天|tiān} | three or four days |
| | {七八|qī bā}{个|gè}{菜|cài} | seven or eight dishes |

Compare: {十多|shí duō}{块|kuài} is 11–19 kuai; {十|shí}{块|kuài}{多|duō} is 10.10–10.90.

## Prices

| Written | Said | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| ¥15 | {十五|shí wǔ}{块|kuài}（{钱|qián}） | 15 kuai |
| ¥960 | {九百六十|jiǔ bǎi liù shí}{块|kuài} / {九百六|jiǔ bǎi liù} | 960 kuai |
| ¥1,200 | {一千两百|yì qiān liǎng bǎi}{块|kuài} / {一千二|yì qiān èr} | 1,200 kuai |
| ¥10,500 | {一万|yí wàn}{零|líng}{五百|wǔ bǎi}{块|kuài} | 10,500 kuai |
| ¥31–39 | {三十多|sān shí duō}{块|kuài} | thirty-something kuai |

- In speech {块|kuài}; on tags, menus and receipts {元|yuán} or ¥.
- A final round place is often dropped: {一千二|yì qiān èr} = 1,200, {两万五|liǎng wàn wǔ} = 25,000.
- 1,200 in full: {一千两百|yì qiān liǎng bǎi} and {一千二百|yì qiān èr bǎi} are both heard.

## Discounts: {打|dǎ}…{折|zhé}

The number is the part you **pay**, in tenths.

| Sign | You pay | Discount |
|---|---|---|
| {打|dǎ}{九|jiǔ}{折|zhé} | 90% | 10% off |
| {打|dǎ}{八|bā}{折|zhé} | 80% | 20% off |
| {打|dǎ}{五|wǔ}{折|zhé} | 50% | half price |

references.title: Reduplication
references.body:
## Doubling words: four kinds

Chinese says many words twice. What doubling does depends on the kind of word.

| Kind | Pattern | Example | Effect | Lesson |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Action verb | AA, A一A, ABAB, AAB | {看看|kàn kan}, {看|kàn}{一|yi}{看|kàn}, {介绍介绍|jiè shào jiè shào}, {洗洗|xǐ xi}{手|shǒu} | a little, briefly, casually | 01, 04 |
| Adjective | AA的, AABB的 | {大大|dà dà}{的|de}, {漂漂亮亮|piào piào liàng liàng}{的|de} | vivid description ("nice and big") | 02 |
| Measure word or time noun | AA | {天天|tiān tiān}, {人人|rén rén}, {年年|nián nián} | every | 04 |
| Family word | AA (fixed) | {爷爷|yé ye}, {奶奶|nǎi nai}, {妈妈|mā ma}, {哥哥|gē ge} | no change: it's the word itself | 01 |

## Verbs: "do it a little"

| Verb | Doubled | With {一|yi} | Done (with {了|le}) |
|---|---|---|---|
| {看|kàn} (one syllable) | {看看|kàn kan} | {看|kàn}{一|yi}{看|kàn} | {看|kàn}{了|le}{看|kàn} |
| {想|xiǎng} | {想想|xiǎng xiang} | {想|xiǎng}{一|yi}{想|xiǎng} | {想|xiǎng}{了|le}{想|xiǎng} |
| {问|wèn} | {问问|wèn wen} | {问|wèn}{一|yi}{问|wèn} | {问|wèn}{了|le}{问|wèn} |
| {介绍|jiè shào} (two syllables) | {介绍介绍|jiè shào jiè shào} | none | {介绍|jiè shào}{了|le}{介绍|jiè shào} |
| {休息|xiū xi} | {休息休息|xiū xi xiū xi} | none | {休息|xiū xi}{了|le}{休息|xiū xi} |
| {洗|xǐ}{手|shǒu} (verb + object) | {洗洗|xǐ xi}{手|shǒu} | {洗|xǐ}{一|yi}{洗|xǐ}{手|shǒu} | {洗|xǐ}{了|le}{洗|xǐ}{手|shǒu} |
| {唱歌|chàng gē} (verb + object) | {唱唱|chàng chang}{歌|gē} | none | {唱|chàng}{了|le}{唱|chàng}{歌|gē} |

- Same meaning as verb + {一下|yí xià}: {看看|kàn kan} = {看|kàn}{一下|yí xià}. Both soften a request:
  {你|nǐ}{看看|kàn kan}{这|zhè}{本|běn}{书|shū} (have a look at this book).
- The second syllable of AA is light: *kàn kan*. In A一A the {一|yi} is light too.
- Two-syllable verbs double as a whole word (ABAB), never ~~{介介绍绍|jiè jiè shào shào}~~.
- Verb + object words double only the verb (AAB): {洗洗|xǐ xi}{手|shǒu}, not ~~{洗手洗手|xǐ shǒu xǐ shǒu}~~.
- Only for actions someone does on purpose. Not for {是|shì}, {有|yǒu}, {在|zài}, {喜欢|xǐ huan},
  {知道|zhī dào}, and not with a large amount or a long time.

## Adjectives: "nice and …"

| Adjective | Doubled | Before a noun | As a predicate |
|---|---|---|---|
| {大|dà} | {大大|dà dà}{的|de} | {大大|dà dà}{的|de}{眼睛|yǎn jing} | {她|tā}{眼睛|yǎn jing}{大大|dà dà}{的|de}。 |
| {高|gāo} | {高高|gāo gāo}{的|de} | {高高|gāo gāo}{的|de}{个子|gè zi} | {他|tā}{个子|gè zi}{高高|gāo gāo}{的|de}。 |
| {长|cháng} | {长长|cháng cháng}{的|de} | {长长|cháng cháng}{的|de}{头发|tóu fa} | {她|tā}{头发|tóu fa}{长长|cháng cháng}{的|de}。 |
| {红|hóng} | {红红|hóng hóng}{的|de} | {红红|hóng hóng}{的|de}{苹果|píng guǒ} | {苹果|píng guǒ}{红红|hóng hóng}{的|de}。 |
| {漂亮|piào liang} | {漂漂亮亮|piào piào liàng liàng}{的|de} | {漂漂亮亮|piào piào liàng liàng}{的|de}{衣服|yī fu} | {她|tā}{今天|jīn tiān}{漂漂亮亮|piào piào liàng liàng}{的|de}。 |
| {高兴|gāo xìng} | {高高兴兴|gāo gāo xìng xìng}{的|de} | {高高兴兴|gāo gāo xìng xìng}{的|de}{孩子|hái zi} | {孩子们|hái zi men}{高高兴兴|gāo gāo xìng xìng}{的|de}。 |

- One syllable: AA{的|de}. Two syllables: AABB{的|de} (each syllable doubled in place). A light
  syllable gets its tone back: *piào piào liàng liàng*.
- Never with {很|hěn}, {太|tài}, {非常|fēi cháng} or {不|bù}: the doubling already says "very".
- In Beijing speech you may hear the second syllable as a first tone with -r: {好好儿|hǎo hāor}{的|de}.

## Every: {天天|tiān tiān}, {人人|rén rén}

A few measure words and time nouns double to mean "every", with {都|dōu} before the verb:
{他|tā}{天天|tiān tiān}{都|dōu}{喝|hē}{茶|chá} (he drinks tea every day), {人人|rén rén}{都|dōu}{知道|zhī dào}
(everybody knows). {每天|měi tiān}, {每|měi}{个|gè}{人|rén} (lesson 04) are the everyday forms.

## Common mistakes

| Wrong | Right | Why |
|---|---|---|
| ~~{很|hěn}{高高|gāo gāo}{的|de}~~ | {高高|gāo gāo}{的|de} | doubled adjectives take no degree adverb |
| ~~{漂亮漂亮|piào liang piào liang}{的|de}~~ | {漂漂亮亮|piào piào liàng liàng}{的|de} | adjectives: AABB |
| ~~{介介绍绍|jiè jiè shào shào}~~ | {介绍介绍|jiè shào jiè shào} | verbs: ABAB |
| ~~{喜欢喜欢|xǐ huan xǐ huan}~~ | {很|hěn}{喜欢|xǐ huan} | states don't double |
| ~~{看看|kàn kan}{了|le}~~ (for "had a look") | {看|kàn}{了|le}{看|kàn} | {了|le} goes between |

language.name: Chinese
language.vocabSource: covers the words and characters of HSK 3.0 level 2 (2025 exam syllabus; 500 words and 371 characters with level 1); grouping, glosses and examples are our own

vocab.note: yī when you count and inside numbers ({十一|shí yī}, eleven). Before other words its tone changes, and this app writes the change: {一|yí}{个|gè} (one, of something), {一起|yì qǐ} (together).
For counting and inside numbers ({十二|shí èr}, twelve). Before a measure word Chinese says {两|liǎng} instead: {两|liǎng}{个|gè}{人|rén}, two people (Chinese HSK 1).
Tens are built with it: {二十|èr shí} (20 = two tens), {十二|shí èr} (12 = ten and two).
After a country it gives the people: {中国|Zhōng guó}{人|rén}, a Chinese person, Chinese people.
Also used for age: {你|nǐ}{多|duō}{大|dà}？ How old are you? (Chinese HSK 1). Its opposite is {小|xiǎo}.
Fourth tone, falling. Don't confuse it with {十|shí} (ten, rising): {四十四|sì shí sì} is 44.
Spelled liù, a short form of liòu: you hear a light o before the u. The tone mark goes on the u.
q is said like the ch of "cheese", with a puff of air.
To one person: a friend, a classmate, anyone your age. The polite form for older people and strangers is {您|nín} (Chinese HSK 1).
One word for "I" and "me": {我|wǒ} doesn't change.
Said ní hǎo (two third tones: the first rises). Answer with {你好|nǐ hǎo} too.
Alone it also means "OK, all right": {好|hǎo}！
bù, but bú before a fourth tone: {不|bú}{是|shì}, {不客气|bú kè qi}. This app writes the change; most dictionaries write bù everywhere.
Links two nouns: A {是|shì} B. It never changes for I, you or they. Its negative is {不|bú}{是|shì}.
Before a surname it's a friendly way to address a younger person: {小|xiǎo}{王|Wáng}, "young Wang".
Literally "middle country". A capital Z in pinyin, as for every name.
The second xie is light and short (neutral tone). Reply: {不客气|bú kè qi}.
The reply to {谢谢|xiè xie}. Literally "don't be so polite". 不 is bú here, before the fourth tone kè.
An apology for something you did. The 不 in the middle is light (neutral tone). Reply: {没关系|méi guān xi}.
vocab.example: {对不起|duì bu qǐ}，{我|wǒ}{不|bú}{是|shì}{王芳|Wáng Fāng}。

vocab.note: The reply to {对不起|duì bu qǐ}. Literally "there's no connection".
vocab.example: — {对不起|duì bu qǐ}！— {没关系|méi guān xi}。

vocab.note: Literally "again see". Two fourth tones: both fall.
Sounds the same as {她|tā} (she); only the writing differs: 亻 "person" here, 女 "woman" in 她.
Sounds the same as {他|tā} (he). The radical 女 "woman" shows it means a woman.
For teachers, older people, customers and strangers; {你|nǐ} for friends and people your age.
Stays where the answer goes: {你|nǐ}{叫|jiào}{什么|shén me}？ — {我|wǒ}{叫|jiào}{安娜|Ān nà}。 Second syllable neutral.
Second syllable neutral: míng zi.
At the end of a statement, makes a yes-or-no question. Not used with question words such as {什么|shén me}.
Before an adjective in a plain statement, usually unstressed: {我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo} is just "I'm fine".
Also a title after a family name: {王老师|Wáng lǎo shī}, Teacher Wang.
Second syllable neutral in mainland speech: xué sheng.
vocab.example: {他|tā}{是|shì}{学生|xué sheng}，{不|bú}{是|shì}{老师|lǎo shī}。
vocab.exampleEn: He's a student, not a teacher.

vocab.note: Only for people, never after a number: {三|sān}{个|gè}{学生|xué sheng}, not 三个学生们.
Sounds the same as {她们|tā men} (they, all women). Used for any mixed group.
Only when everyone in the group is a woman; otherwise {他们|tā men}.
In country names: {中国|Zhōng guó}, {美国|Měi guó}. {哪|nǎ}{国|guó}{人|rén}: a person of which country?
Third tone. Don't confuse with {那|nà} (that), fourth tone.
vocab.exampleEn: Where is he from? (Which country is he from?)

vocab.note: The usual word in classes and textbooks. {中文|Zhōng wén} means the same, especially written Chinese.
Used for the language in general and for written Chinese: a menu or a website in Chinese.
A skill you have learned: {会|huì}{说|shuō}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}. Also "will (probably)" later in the course.
After a noun or pronoun: {你|nǐ}{呢|ne}？ "And you?" Neutral tone.
Before the verb, never at the end: {我|wǒ}{也|yě}{是|shì}{学生|xué sheng}. With {不|bù}: "not ... either".
After the plural subject, before the verb. With {也|yě}: {也|yě}{都|dōu}, never 都也.
vocab.example: {我们|wǒ men}{都|dōu}{是|shì}{美国人|Měi guó rén}。

vocab.note: Negative {没有|méi yǒu}, never 不有. "There is" comes in lesson 17.
The negative of {有|yǒu}. Later also "didn't" (lesson 25).
vocab.exampleEn: I don't have an older sister.

vocab.note: Owner + {的|de} + thing: {老师|lǎo shī}{的|de}{名字|míng zi}. Usually dropped with family and home: {我|wǒ}{妈妈|mā ma}.
Also said zhèi in speech, especially before a measure word.
Fourth tone. {哪|nǎ} (which) has the third tone. Also said nèi in speech.
Joins nouns and pronouns only, never sentences or verbs.
vocab.example: {爸爸|bà ba}{和|hé}{妈妈|mā ma}{都|dōu}{是|shì}{老师|lǎo shī}。
vocab.exampleEn: Dad and Mum are both teachers.

vocab.note: No {的|de} after a pronoun: {我|wǒ}{家|jiā}, my home or my family. Later also a measure word for shops and companies.
vocab.exampleEn: How many people are there in your family?
Do you have an older brother?

vocab.note: For a small number you expect, with a measure word: {几|jǐ}{个|gè}. For any number: {多少|duō shao}.
vocab.exampleEn: How many older sisters do you have?

vocab.note: Between a number and a noun: {一|yí}{个|gè}{人|rén}. Often light in speech. {一|yī} becomes yí before it.
vocab.exampleEn: There are five people in my family.

vocab.note: Said once for each gap inside a number: {一千零五|yì qiān líng wǔ} (1,005).
Always with a number in front: {一百|yì bǎi}, never 百 alone for 100.
vocab.example: {三百四十五|sān bǎi sì shí wǔ}
{两千零二十六|liǎng qiān líng èr shí liù}

vocab.note: Before a measure word: {两|liǎng}{个|gè}{人|rén}. In counting and inside numbers it's {二|èr}: {十二|shí èr}.
Age needs no {是|shì}: {我|wǒ}{二十|èr shí}{岁|suì}. Ask children {几岁|jǐ suì}, adults {多大|duō dà}.
Usually with {很|hěn}: {很多|hěn duō}{人|rén}. Before an adjective it asks "how": {多大|duō dà}, how old.
vocab.exampleEn: China has a lot of people.

vocab.note: For any number; the measure word is optional. {几|jǐ} is for small numbers and needs one.
vocab.exampleEn: How many people does China have?

vocab.note: Both syllables keep their tones: nǚ ér.

vocab.exampleEn: How many children do you have?
How old is your younger sister?

meanings: mouth (also: measure word for family members)
vocab.note: As a measure word for people, only for the size of a family: {我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{有|yǒu}{五|wǔ}{口|kǒu}{人|rén}.
vocab.exampleEn: How many people are there in your family?

vocab.note: Also before a verb, for where it happens: {我|wǒ}{在|zài}{公司|gōng sī}{工作|gōng zuò}. Sounds like {再|zài} (again).
Verb and noun: {我|wǒ}{在|zài}{大学|dà xué}{工作|gōng zuò} (I work at a university); {你|nǐ}{有|yǒu}{工作|gōng zuò}{吗|ma}？ (Do you have a job?)

vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{爸爸|bà ba}{在|zài}{公司|gōng sī}{工作|gōng zuò}。
vocab.exampleEn: My dad works for a company.

vocab.example: {我们|wǒ men}{在|zài}{学校|xué xiào}{说|shuō}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}。
{王老师|Wáng lǎo shī}{在|zài}{大学|dà xué}{工作|gōng zuò}。
vocab.exampleEn: Teacher Wang works at a university.

vocab.note: {生|shēng} keeps its first tone here, unlike {学生|xué sheng}.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{哥哥|gē ge}{是|shì}{大学生|dà xué shēng}。
vocab.exampleEn: My older brother is a university student.

vocab.note: Before a noun: {男|nán}{老师|lǎo shī}, a male teacher. Not used alone as "a man".
vocab.example: {我们|wǒ men}{的|de}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{老师|lǎo shī}{是|shì}{男|nán}{老师|lǎo shī}。
vocab.exampleEn: Our Chinese teacher is a man.

vocab.note: Before a noun: {女|nǚ}{医生|yī shēng}, a female doctor. Not used alone as "a woman".
Counts without {个|gè}: {一天|yì tiān}, {两天|liǎng tiān}. Also "sky", as in {天气|tiān qì} (weather, lesson 20). Can be a measure word too.
vocab.example: {他|tā}{在|zài}{中国|Zhōng guó}{工作|gōng zuò}{三天|sān tiān}。
vocab.exampleEn: He's working in China for three days.

vocab.note: Takes {个|gè} when counted: {两个星期|liǎng gè xīng qī}. Add {一|yī} to {六|liù} for Monday to Saturday: {星期一|xīng qī yī}, {星期六|xīng qī liù}.
vocab.example: {一个星期|yí gè xīng qī}{有|yǒu}{七天|qī tiān}。

vocab.note: The written and more formal word, seen on calendars and timetables; in everyday speech {星期天|xīng qī tiān}.
vocab.example: {星期日|xīng qī rì}{学校|xué xiào}{没有|méi yǒu}{人|rén}。
vocab.exampleEn: There's nobody at the school on Sunday.

vocab.note: The everyday spoken word; {星期日|xīng qī rì} is the written one. There is no {星期七|xīng qī qī}.
vocab.example: {星期天|xīng qī tiān}{我|wǒ}{不|bù}{工作|gōng zuò}。

vocab.note: Month names are number + {月|yuè}: {一月|yī yuè} (January), {十二月|shí èr yuè} (December). "One month" is {一个月|yí gè yuè}.
Number + {号|hào} in speech: {十六号|shí liù hào} (the 16th); writing uses {日|rì}. Also "number", as in {手机号|shǒu jī hào} (mobile number, lesson 10). Can be a measure word too.
Written and formal: 11{月|yuè}16{日|rì}. In speech, {号|hào}. As a noun, {日|rì} is also "sun".
Counts without {个|gè}: {两年|liǎng nián}. Years are read digit by digit: 2026{年|nián}, èr líng èr liù nián.
vocab.example: {一年|yì nián}{有|yǒu}{十二个月|shí èr gè yuè}。

vocab.note: Two o'clock is {两点|liǎng diǎn}. An amount of hours is {小时|xiǎo shí}. Also "a little" in {一点儿|yì diǎnr} (lesson 12).
Clock minutes: {八点十分|bā diǎn shí fēn} (8:10). An amount of minutes is {分钟|fēn zhōng}. Also a fen, a hundredth of a yuan.
vocab.example: {现在|xiàn zài}{九点二十分|jiǔ diǎn èr shí fēn}。

vocab.note: An amount of time, with no {个|gè}: {十分钟|shí fēn zhōng} (ten minutes). On the clock, {分|fēn}.
After the hour, half past: {八点半|bā diǎn bàn}. Half an hour: {半个小时|bàn gè xiǎo shí}.
Usually with {个|gè}: {两个小时|liǎng gè xiǎo shí} (two hours). Two o'clock is {两点|liǎng diǎn}.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{一天|yì tiān}{工作|gōng zuò}{八个小时|bā gè xiǎo shí}。
vocab.exampleEn: I work eight hours a day.

vocab.note: Time you have or spend: {有时间|yǒu shí jiān} (to have time). To ask the clock time, use {几点|jǐ diǎn}.
The whole morning up to noon. Goes before the clock time: {上午|shàng wǔ}{十点|shí diǎn} (10 a.m.).
vocab.example: {王老师|Wáng lǎo shī}{上午|shàng wǔ}{在|zài}{学校|xué xiào}。
vocab.exampleEn: Teacher Wang is at school in the morning.

vocab.note: Before the clock time: {下午|xià wǔ}{三点|sān diǎn} (3 p.m.).
vocab.exampleEn: I'm at home at three in the afternoon.
I'm at the office at noon.

vocab.note: The early part of the morning, getting up and breakfast; {上午|shàng wǔ} is the whole morning until noon.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{早上|zǎo shang}{六点|liù diǎn}{起床|qǐ chuáng}。
vocab.exampleEn: I get up at six in the morning.

vocab.note: From about six until bedtime: {晚上|wǎn shang}{十一点|shí yī diǎn} is 11 p.m.
vocab.exampleEn: I'm at home in the evening.

vocab.note: A separable verb: {起|qǐ} (rise) + {床|chuáng} (bed).
vocab.exampleEn: What time do you get up?

vocab.note: A separable verb: {睡|shuì} (sleep) + {觉|jiào} (a sleep), so no object follows it. "Sleep eight hours" uses {睡|shuì} alone (lesson 21).
vocab.example: {他|tā}{晚上|wǎn shang}{十一点|shí yī diǎn}{睡觉|shuì jiào}。
vocab.exampleEn: He goes to bed at eleven at night.

vocab.note: A separable verb: {上|shàng} (go on) + {班|bān} (a shift). The opposite is {下班|xià bān}.

vocab.exampleEn: What time do you finish work?

vocab.note: With {吃|chī} (to eat, lesson 11): {吃早饭|chī zǎo fàn}, to have breakfast.

vocab.exampleEn: I have lunch at the office.

vocab.example: {我们|wǒ men}{七点|qī diǎn}{吃|chī}{晚饭|wǎn fàn}。

vocab.note: Also a morning greeting: {早|zǎo}！ or {你早|nǐ zǎo}！ (Morning!). Opposite: {晚|wǎn}.

vocab.example: {晚上|wǎn shang}{十二点|shí èr diǎn}{很|hěn}{晚|wǎn}。

vocab.note: Away from the speaker. No word for "to" before the place: {去|qù}{学校|xué xiào}.
Towards the speaker: if you aren't there yourself, use {去|qù}.
vocab.exampleEn: Are you coming to my place?

vocab.note: Back to where you belong: {回家|huí jiā} (go home), {回国|huí guó} (go back to your country).
vocab.exampleEn: I go home in the evening.

vocab.note: A wish, gentle and polite. Also "to think" and "to miss" someone. Negative: {不想|bù xiǎng}.
vocab.exampleEn: I'd like to go to China.

vocab.note: More decided than {想|xiǎng}; also takes a noun ("I'd like…"). "Don't want to" is {不想|bù xiǎng}: {不要|bú yào} + verb means "don't!" (lesson 21).
{做什么|zuò shén me}: (to) do what. Not {坐|zuò} (to sit, lesson 18), which sounds the same.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{星期六|xīng qī liù}{做|zuò}{什么|shén me}？
vocab.exampleEn: What are you doing on Saturday?

vocab.note: {有事|yǒu shì}: to be busy, have something on. A thing you can hold is {东西|dōng xi}.
Neutral second syllable. With full tones, {东西|dōng xī} means "east and west". {买东西|mǎi dōng xi}: to go shopping.
Third tone; {卖|mài} (to sell, lesson 13) is the same syllable with the fourth tone.
vocab.exampleEn: What would you like to buy?

vocab.note: Also "to go and see, visit" a person: {看|kàn}{妈妈|mā ma}. "To see, catch sight of" is {看见|kàn jiàn} (lesson 24).
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{星期天|xīng qī tiān}{去|qù}{看|kàn}{妈妈|mā ma}。
vocab.exampleEn: On Sunday I'm going to see my mum.

vocab.note: One syllable with erhua. {哪里|nǎ lǐ} (lesson 16) means the same and is used everywhere. Not {那儿|nàr} (there).
Said wéi, rising, when you answer the phone; a sharp falling wèi is "Hey!".
{打|dǎ} (strike) + {电话|diàn huà}. "To phone someone" needs {给|gěi} (lesson 23).

vocab.exampleEn: We don't have a phone at home.

vocab.note: Literally "hand machine". {手机号|shǒu jī hào}: mobile number.
Before a verb: the action is going on right now. {在|zài} alone and a final {呢|ne} do the same job.
On the phone or at a door, {我|wǒ}{找|zhǎo} + person means "I'd like to speak to…".
Often said zhīdao, with a light second syllable. Knowing a person is {认识|rèn shi} (lesson 23).
Also said shuí. {谁|shéi}{的|de}: whose.
{说|shuō} (speak) + {话|huà} (words): takes no object. For a language, use {说|shuō}: {说|shuō}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}.
Listening on purpose. "To hear" is {听见|tīng jiàn} (lesson 24).
For food; drinks take {喝|hē}. {吃|chī}{饭|fàn} is "to have a meal", whatever is eaten.
vocab.exampleEn: I have steamed buns in the morning.

vocab.note: Every drink takes {喝|hē}: {喝|hē}{水|shuǐ}, {喝|hē}{茶|chá}. Not the English "he": the e is said far back in the mouth.
vocab.exampleEn: Would you like some tea? / Do you drink tea?

vocab.note: Cooked rice, and so a meal in general: {吃|chī}{饭|fàn} (to eat), {早饭|zǎo fàn}, {午饭|wǔ fàn}, {晚饭|wǎn fàn}. The rice itself is {米饭|mǐ fàn}.
{米|mǐ} is the grain, {米饭|mǐ fàn} the cooked rice on your plate.
vocab.example: {中午|zhōng wǔ}{我|wǒ}{吃|chī}{米饭|mǐ fàn}{和|hé}{菜|cài}。
vocab.exampleEn: At noon I have rice and a dish.

vocab.note: Also {面条|miàn tiáo} without the northern -r. Traditional {麵|miàn} (noodles, flour), not {面|miàn} (face, side).
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{妈妈|mā ma}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{吃|chī}{面条儿|miàn tiáor}。

vocab.note: The character {饺|jiǎo} is HSK 3's: recognise the word now.

vocab.example: {他|tā}{早上|zǎo shang}{吃|chī}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{包子|bāo zi}。
vocab.exampleEn: He has two steamed buns in the morning.

vocab.note: Rising tone, chá; {菜|cài} (dish) falls.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{爸爸|bà ba}{很|hěn}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{喝|hē}{茶|chá}。

vocab.exampleEn: I don't want tea; I'd like water.

vocab.note: Also "vegetable". {中国|Zhōng guó}{菜|cài} is Chinese food; {买|mǎi}{菜|cài} is doing the food shopping.
+ noun or + verb: {喜欢|xǐ huan}{茶|chá}, {喜欢|xǐ huan}{喝|hē}{茶|chá}. Negative {不|bù}{喜欢|xǐ huan} (never {没|méi}{喜欢|xǐ huan}). Neutral second syllable.
In names often a hotel: {北京饭店|Běi jīng Fàn diàn} (the Beijing Hotel). {店|diàn} is an HSK 2 character.
vocab.example: {我们|wǒ men}{去|qù}{饭店|fàn diàn}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}{吧|ba}。
vocab.exampleEn: Let's go and eat at a restaurant.

vocab.note: {请|qǐng} + verb: please (do). {我|wǒ}{请|qǐng}{你|nǐ} is "it's my treat".
Ends a suggestion: {我们|wǒ men}{去|qù}{吧|ba} (let's go). Compare {吗|ma}, which asks.
For food; a drink that tastes good is {好喝|hǎo hē}.
Traditional {麵|miàn} (flour), not {面|miàn} (face).
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{早上|zǎo shang}{吃|chī}{面包|miàn bāo}，{喝|hē}{茶|chá}。
vocab.exampleEn: In the morning I have bread and tea.

vocab.note: {杯|bēi} alone counts cupfuls: {一|yì}{杯|bēi}{茶|chá}, a cup of tea.
After a verb, softens it: {看|kàn}{一下|yí xià} (have a look), {等|děng}{一下|yí xià} (wait a moment). {一|yí} rises before the 4th tone.
After the verb: {喝|hē}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}{水|shuǐ}. Not {有点儿|yǒu diǎnr} (lesson 21), which goes before adjectives.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{会|huì}{说|shuō}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}。
vocab.exampleEn: I can speak a little Chinese.

vocab.note: {太|tài}…{了|le}: {太|tài}{好|hǎo}{了|le}！ (great!), {太|tài}{多|duō}{了|le} (too much). {不|bú}{太|tài} = not very.
After the surname: {王|Wáng}{先生|xiān sheng}, Mr Wang. Also "husband".
Polite and formal, after the surname: {李|Lǐ}{女士|nǚ shì}, Ms Li.
Second tone; {千|qiān} (thousand) is first.
The spoken word for {元|yuán}: {十|shí}{块|kuài}{钱|qián}. Also a piece: {一|yí}{块|kuài}{面包|miàn bāo}.
On price tags, menus and receipts (also ¥); people say {块|kuài}.
Fourth tone; {买|mǎi} (to buy) is third. {=The character 卖 has 十 on top of 买=}; in traditional script {+卖+} has 士 on top of {+买+}.
{便|pián} is pián here (biàn in {方便|fāng biàn}, convenient).
{店|diàn} is an HSK 2 character.
vocab.exampleEn: I'm going to the shops to buy some things.

vocab.example: {大学|dà xué}{的|de}{书店|shū diàn}{很|hěn}{便宜|pián yi}。

meanings: measure word for clothes and matters
vocab.note: Clothes (especially tops and coats) and matters: {一|yí}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}, {一|yí}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}.
vocab.exampleEn: I'd like to buy a piece of clothing.

vocab.note: Ends the names of kinds of shops: {书店|shū diàn}, {饭店|fàn diàn}, {商店|shāng diàn}. An HSK 2 character.
Often said zhèige in northern speech. Before a noun: {这个|zhè ge}{人|rén}, this person.
Often said nèige. Falling tone; {哪个|nǎ ge} (which one) dips.
Often said něige. A question word: no {吗|ma}.
{些|xiē} replaces the measure word: {这些|zhè xiē}{书|shū}.
vocab.example: {这些|zhè xiē}{苹果|píng guǒ}{很|hěn}{便宜|pián yi}。

vocab.exampleEn: Which fruits would you like to buy?

meanings: some (measure word for a number of things)
vocab.note: Makes plurals after {这|zhè}, {那|nà}, {哪|nǎ} and {一|yì}: {这些|zhè xiē}, {一些|yì xiē}.
Compare {一点儿|yì diǎnr}, a little (amount).
vocab.example: {我们|wǒ men}{买|mǎi}{一些|yì xiē}{鸡蛋|jī dàn}{吧|ba}。

vocab.note: Two third tones: said shuí guǒ.
{第|dì}{一|yī} first, {第|dì}{二|èr} second; {一|yī} stays yī, and second is never {第|dì}{两|liǎng}.

vocab.exampleEn: I drink milk in the morning.
I'd like to buy some eggs.

vocab.example: {我们|wǒ men}{去|qù}{超市|chāo shì}{买|mǎi}{东西|dōng xi}{吧|ba}。
vocab.exampleEn: Let's go to the supermarket to do some shopping.

vocab.note: Counted with {件|jiàn}: {一|yí}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}.
Straight before a noun: {新|xīn}{衣服|yī fu}, {新|xīn}{书|shū}.

vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{穿|chuān}{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}{真|zhēn}{漂亮|piào liang}。
vocab.exampleEn: You look really pretty in this.

vocab.note: Also for films and books worth watching or reading.
vocab.example: {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}{怎么样|zěn me yàng}？{很|hěn}{好看|hǎo kàn}！
vocab.exampleEn: What do you think of this top? It looks great!

vocab.note: Stronger than {很|hěn}; before the adjective.
vocab.example: {饺子|jiǎo zi}{非常|fēi cháng}{好吃|hǎo chī}。

vocab.note: Exclaims your feeling: {真|zhēn}{漂亮|piào liang}！ Not used in questions. Also an adjective, "real".
{不|bú}{对|duì}: wrong. Also a preposition, "to, towards" ({他|tā}{对|duì}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}).
vocab.exampleEn: A: Are you David? B: That's right.

vocab.note: A share of something; {半|bàn} is for times and with measure words ({八|bā}{点|diǎn}{半|bàn}).
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{吃|chī}{一半|yí bàn}，{你|nǐ}{吃|chī}{一半|yí bàn}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'll eat half, you eat half.

vocab.note: Asks for an opinion; after a suggestion, "how about it?".
vocab.example: {我们|wǒ men}{去|qù}{超市|chāo shì}，{怎么样|zěn me yàng}？
vocab.exampleEn: Let's go to the supermarket. How about it?

vocab.note: Said ná lǐ (two third tones). Means the same as {哪儿|nǎr}, which is northern speech.
The northern form of {这里|zhè lǐ}; same meaning.
vocab.exampleEn: Your book is with me. (I've got your book.)

vocab.note: Used everywhere and in writing; {这儿|zhèr} is the northern spoken form. {里|lǐ} is often light here.
vocab.example: {请问|qǐng wèn}，{这里|zhè lǐ}{是|shì}{大学|dà xué}{吗|ma}？
vocab.exampleEn: Excuse me, is this the university?

vocab.note: Fourth tone; {哪儿|nǎr} (third tone) asks "where?".
Fourth tone on {那|nà}; {哪里|nǎ lǐ} (third tone) asks "where?". {那儿|nàr} is the northern form.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{妈妈|mā ma}{在|zài}{那里|nà lǐ}{工作|gōng zuò}。

vocab.note: Goes after the noun: {杯子|bēi zi}{里|lǐ}, in the cup. Often said lightly (li).
vocab.exampleEn: The water is in the cup.

vocab.note: Also a noun of position: {书|shū}{上|shàng}, on the book. As a verb, "go up, go to": {上班|shàng bān}, {上课|shàng kè}.
vocab.exampleEn: My phone is on the book.

vocab.note: Also a noun of position ({衣服|yī fu}{下|xià}, under the clothes) and "next" before time words. As a verb, "come down": {下雨|xià yǔ}, {下课|xià kè}.
vocab.exampleEn: The phone is under the clothes.

vocab.note: After a noun, for place or time: {饭|fàn}{前|qián}, before meals. In speech, usually {前边|qián bian}. Not {钱|qián} (money): same sound, different character.
After a noun, for place or time: {饭|fàn}{后|hòu}, after meals. In speech, usually {后边|hòu bian}.
Alone after a noun it sounds compact ({学校|xué xiào}{外|wài}); in speech and on its own, use {外边|wài bian}.
vocab.exampleEn: There are lots of people outside the restaurant.

vocab.note: Opens a polite question to a stranger. To apologise, say {对不起|duì bu qǐ}.
Also a suffix for position words: {外边|wài bian}, {上边|shàng bian}, {前边|qián bian} (light bian).
Can stand alone, unlike one-syllable {外|wài}: {外边|wài bian}{有|yǒu}{人|rén}. {边|biān} is light.
vocab.exampleEn: There are lots of people outside.
Come and sit over here, please.

vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{的|de}{房间|fáng jiān}{里|lǐ}{没有|méi yǒu}{电视|diàn shì}。
vocab.exampleEn: There's no TV in my room.
There's a book on the table.

vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{的|de}{衣服|yī fu}{在|zài}{椅子|yǐ zi}{上|shàng}。
vocab.exampleEn: My clothes are on the chair.

vocab.note: Literally "electric brain".
vocab.exampleEn: Is there a computer in the room?

vocab.note: {看|kàn}{电视|diàn shì}: to watch TV. {开|kāi}{电视|diàn shì}: to turn the TV on.
vocab.example: {爸爸|bà ba}{晚上|wǎn shang}{看|kàn}{电视|diàn shì}。
vocab.exampleEn: Dad watches TV in the evening.

vocab.note: Usually {住|zhù}{在|zài} + place, with the place after the verb.
{坐|zuò} + vehicle + {去|qù} + place: go somewhere by. Same sound as {做|zuò} (to do) and the {作|zuò} of {工作|gōng zuò}.
vocab.exampleEn: I'm going to Beijing by train.

vocab.note: {开|kāi}{车|chē}, drive; {开|kāi}{电视|diàn shì}, switch on the TV; {开|kāi}{门|mén}, open the door.
Verb + object already: don't add another object.
{出租|chū zū} (rent out) + {车|chē}.
vocab.example: {妈妈|mā ma}{坐|zuò}{出租车|chū zū chē}{回|huí}{家|jiā}。
vocab.exampleEn: Mum is taking a taxi home.

vocab.note: "Fire vehicle", from the age of steam.
vocab.exampleEn: What time does the train arrive?

vocab.note: "Flying machine". A passenger {坐|zuò}{飞机|fēi jī}; a pilot {开|kāi}{飞机|fēi jī}.
Before a verb: {怎么|zěn me}{去|qù}？ (how do you get there?). Compare {怎么样|zěn me yàng}, "what is it like?".
vocab.exampleEn: How do you get to school?
I get to school at eight.

vocab.note: Takes a subject or a skill, even a verb: {学|xué}{开车|kāi chē}, learn to drive.
vocab.exampleEn: I'd like to learn to write Chinese characters.

vocab.note: A little more formal than {学|xué}, and fine on its own: {他|tā}{在|zài}{学习|xué xí}.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{在|zài}{北京|Běi jīng}{学习|xué xí}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}。

vocab.note: Verb + object: say {上|shàng}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{课|kè} for "have Chinese class".

vocab.exampleEn: What time do you finish class?

vocab.note: For pupils and students; teachers and office workers {上班|shàng bān}.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{儿子|ér zi}{早上|zǎo shang}{七|qī}{点|diǎn}{去|qù}{上学|shàng xué}。
vocab.exampleEn: My son goes to school at seven in the morning.

vocab.example: {今天|jīn tiān}{下午|xià wǔ}{没有|méi yǒu}{课|kè}。

vocab.note: A word is {词|cí} (HSK 2); {学生|xué sheng} is one word written with two {字|zì}.
vocab.exampleEn: How do you write this character?

vocab.note: Third tone; {谢|xiè} in {谢谢|xiè xie} is fourth.
Teachers call the class {同学们|tóng xué men}.
Ability, or the situation allows it. A learned skill is {会|huì}; permission is usually {可以|kě yǐ}.
Said ké yǐ (two third tones). Also an adjective, "not bad, OK".

vocab.example: {今天|jīn tiān}{天气|tiān qì}{怎么样|zěn me yàng}？

vocab.note: Verb + object, "come-down rain". Snow works the same way: {下雪|xià xuě}.
To snow: {下雪|xià xuě}.
vocab.example: {北京|Běi jīng}{下雪|xià xuě}{了|le}，{雪|xuě}{很|hěn}{漂亮|piào liang}。
vocab.exampleEn: It's snowing in Beijing, and the snow is beautiful.

meanings: change particle (something new: now, any more)
vocab.note: At the end of a sentence it marks a new situation ({下雨|xià yǔ}{了|le}); after a verb, a completed action (lesson 25). Always light.
Takes a whole clause: {我|wǒ}{觉得|jué de}{很|hěn}{冷|lěng}. For "think" as an opinion it is usually {觉得|jué de} rather than {想|xiǎng}.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{觉得|jué de}{这个|zhè ge}{房间|fáng jiān}{怎么样|zěn me yàng}？
vocab.exampleEn: What do you think of this room?

vocab.note: A verb ({我|wǒ}{病|bìng}{了|le}: I'm ill, I've fallen ill) and a noun (illness). {看病|kàn bìng} is to see a doctor.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{病|bìng}{了|le}，{今天|jīn tiān}{不|bú}{去|qù}{上班|shàng bān}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm ill, so I'm not going to work today.

vocab.note: A verb-object word: {生|shēng} (to get) + {病|bìng} (illness).
vocab.example: {他|tā}{生病|shēng bìng}{了|le}，{在|zài}{家|jiā}{休息|xiū xi}。
vocab.exampleEn: He's ill and resting at home.

vocab.note: Separable (verb + object). Said by the patient (I go and see a doctor) and of the doctor (who sees patients).
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{下午|xià wǔ}{去|qù}{医院|yī yuàn}{看病|kàn bìng}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm going to the hospital to see a doctor this afternoon.

vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{妈妈|mā ma}{在|zài}{医院|yī yuàn}{工作|gōng zuò}。
vocab.exampleEn: My mum works at a hospital.

vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{很|hěn}{忙|máng}，{休息|xiū xi}{一下|yí xià}{吧|ba}。
vocab.exampleEn: You're busy. Take a little break.

meanings: rather (a bit too, before an adjective)
vocab.note: Before an adjective, usually for something unwelcome: {有点儿|yǒu diǎnr}{冷|lěng} (a bit cold). Compare {一点儿|yì diǎnr}, which goes after a verb or adjective.
Also "to be free, to have nothing on": {我|wǒ}{今天|jīn tiān}{没事|méi shì} (I'm free today).

meanings: to sleep (on its own, with a time)
vocab.note: {睡觉|shuì jiào} is "to sleep, to go to bed" as a whole; {睡|shuì} on its own takes times and other words: {睡|shuì}{八|bā}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}, {睡|shuì}{一下|yí xià}.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{晚上|wǎn shang}{睡|shuì}{八|bā}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}。
vocab.exampleEn: I sleep eight hours at night.

vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{白天|bái tiān}{工作|gōng zuò}，{晚上|wǎn shang}{学习|xué xí}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}。
vocab.exampleEn: I work during the day and study Chinese in the evening.

vocab.note: Mostly an adjective, used without {是|shì}: {我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{忙|máng}. As a verb: {你|nǐ}{在|zài}{忙|máng}{什么|shén me}？ (What are you busy with?)
{不要|bú yào} + verb tells someone not to do something. {我|wǒ}{不要|bú yào} on its own is "I don't want it".
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{病|bìng}{了|le}，{不要|bú yào}{去|qù}{上班|shàng bān}。
vocab.exampleEn: You're ill. Don't go to work.

vocab.note: Stronger than {喜欢|xǐ huan}. With a verb: {爱|ài}{看|kàn}{书|shū} (loves reading).
{唱|chàng}{歌|gē}: to sing (songs).
Same syllable as {哥哥|gē ge} (older brother): different character.
vocab.exampleEn: I like listening to Chinese songs.

vocab.example: {这个|zhè ge}{电影|diàn yǐng}{很|hěn}{好看|hǎo kàn}。
{我们|wǒ men}{晚上|wǎn shang}{去|qù}{电影院|diàn yǐng yuàn}{看|kàn}{电影|diàn yǐng}{吧|ba}。
vocab.exampleEn: Let's go to the cinema this evening.

vocab.note: Both "to read (books)" and "to study, to be a student somewhere": {在|zài}{大学|dà xué}{读书|dú shū}.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{哥哥|gē ge}{在|zài}{大学|dà xué}{读书|dú shū}。
vocab.exampleEn: My older brother is studying at university.

vocab.note: Reading aloud, or reading as study. Reading silently for fun is usually {看|kàn}: {看|kàn}{书|shū}.
Often {玩儿|wánr} in northern speech. {去|qù}{北京|Běi jīng}{玩|wán} is "visit Beijing for fun".

vocab.example: {他|tā}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{中国|Zhōng guó}{朋友|péng you}。
{她|tā}{男朋友|nán péng you}{是|shì}{医生|yī shēng}。

meanings: little one (friendly word for a child)
vocab.note: Adults call children {小朋友|xiǎo péng you}; it means "child", not "a small friend".
vocab.exampleEn: How old are you, little one?
Hello, everyone! My name is Anna.

vocab.note: A verb with two objects ({给|gěi}{他|tā}{一|yì}{本|běn}{书|shū}) and a preposition before a verb ({给|gěi}{妈妈|mā ma}{打电话|dǎ diàn huà}: call Mum).
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{晚上|wǎn shang}{给|gěi}{你|nǐ}{打电话|dǎ diàn huà}。

vocab.note: Same sound as {在|zài} (at, in). {再|zài} is "again" for something that hasn't happened yet.
vocab.exampleEn: Could you say that again, please?
What time shall we meet tomorrow?

vocab.note: Can take two objects: the person, then the question.
Knowing people (and characters you can recognise). Knowing a fact is {知道|zhī dào}.
For animals and things. Sounds the same as {他|tā} and {她|tā}.
vocab.exampleEn: I have a cat. It's called Dabai ("Big White").

vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{有|yǒu}{两|liǎng}{只|zhī}{狗|gǒu}，{它们|tā men}{都|dōu}{很|hěn}{小|xiǎo}。
vocab.exampleEn: I have two dogs. They're both small.

meanings: measure word for animals and birds
vocab.note: Traditional {隻|zhī}. Simplified {={只|zhǐ}=}, read zhǐ, also means "only" (HSK 3), which stays {={只|zhǐ}=} in traditional.
vocab.exampleEn: How many cats do you have at home?

vocab.note: Often in pairs: {有的|yǒu de}…，{有的|yǒu de}… (some…, others…).
vocab.example: {有的|yǒu de}{人|rén}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{猫|māo}，{有的|yǒu de}{人|rén}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{狗|gǒu}。
vocab.exampleEn: Some people like cats, and others like dogs.

vocab.example: {有些|yǒu xiē}{同学|tóng xué}{不|bú}{会|huì}{写|xiě}{这|zhè}{个|gè}{字|zì}。
vocab.exampleEn: Some classmates can't write this character.

vocab.note: {看|kàn} (look) + {见|jiàn} (the result: perceive). {看|kàn} is the action; {看见|kàn jiàn} is actually seeing.
{听|tīng} is "to listen"; {听见|tīng jiàn} is actually hearing.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{听见|tīng jiàn}{有|yǒu}{人|rén}{在|zài}{说话|shuō huà}。

vocab.note: Also read {还|huán} (to give back) in HSK 3. {还有|hái yǒu}: and there's also…
vocab.exampleEn: I have a cat, and a dog too.

vocab.example: {明年|míng nián}{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{去|qù}{中国|Zhōng guó}{学习|xué xí}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}。
vocab.exampleEn: Next year I'd like to go to China to study Chinese.

vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{去年|qù nián}{买|mǎi}{了|le}{一个|yí gè}{新|xīn}{手机|shǒu jī}。
vocab.exampleEn: I bought a new phone last year.

vocab.note: {没|méi}{问题|wèn tí}: no problem.
vocab.example: {老师|lǎo shī}，{我|wǒ}{有|yǒu}{一个|yí gè}{问题|wèn tí}。
vocab.exampleEn: Excuse me (teacher), I have a question.

vocab.note: An adjective ({人|rén}{很|hěn}{少|shǎo} (there are few people)) and a verb (to be missing). The opposite of {多|duō}. Read {少|shào} in a few words (young: HSK 3 and later).
vocab.example: {今天|jīn tiān}{超市|chāo shì}{里|lǐ}{人|rén}{很|hěn}{少|shǎo}。
vocab.exampleEn: There are very few people in the supermarket today.

vocab.note: Covers both {初中|chū zhōng} (junior: about ages 12–15) and {高中|gāo zhōng} (senior: about 15–18).

vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{妹妹|mèi mei}{是|shì}{中学生|zhōng xué shēng}。
vocab.exampleEn: My younger sister is at secondary school.
My daughter has started primary school.

vocab.example: {小学生|xiǎo xué shēng}{八|bā}{点|diǎn}{上课|shàng kè}。
vocab.exampleEn: Primary-school pupils start lessons at eight.

meanings: the time when (as in "when I was little")
vocab.note: …{的|de}{时候|shí hou} means "when …". Clock time and amounts of time are {时间|shí jiān}.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{是|shì}{小学生|xiǎo xué shēng}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{很|hěn}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{唱|chàng}{歌|gē}。
vocab.exampleEn: When I was at primary school, I loved singing.

vocab.note: Takes the family name only: {我|wǒ}{姓|xìng}{王|Wáng}，{叫|jiào}{王芳|Wáng Fāng}. Also a noun, "family name". Polite question: {您|nín}{贵姓|guì xìng}？
The word on forms and lists. In conversation, say {名字|míng zi}.
Also a measure word for places in a ranking ({第一|dì yī}{名|míng}, first place) and, in notices, for people ({十|shí}{名|míng}{学生|xué sheng}).
Respectful: {这|zhè}{位|wèi}{老师|lǎo shī}, {哪|nǎ}{位|wèi}, {几|jǐ}{位|wèi}？ Never about yourself; {个|gè} is the neutral one.
After a pronoun ({我|wǒ}{自己|zì jǐ}, myself) or alone. Before a verb, "by oneself"; with {的|de}, "one's own".
{我|wǒ}{给|gěi}{你们|nǐ men}{介绍|jiè shào}{一下|yí xià} (let me introduce you). Doubled: {介绍介绍|jiè shào jiè shào}.
vocab.example: {请|qǐng}{你|nǐ}{介绍|jiè shào}{一下|yí xià}{你|nǐ}{自己|zì jǐ}。

vocab.note: Your mother's father is {外公|wài gōng} or {姥爷|lǎo ye}. Children also call any old man {爷爷|yé ye}.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{爷爷|yé ye}{今年|jīn nián}{八十|bā shí}{岁|suì}{了|le}。
vocab.exampleEn: My grandpa is eighty this year.

vocab.note: Your mother's mother is {外婆|wài pó} or {姥姥|lǎo lao}.
Usually in a topic-comment sentence: {他|tā}{个子|gè zi}{很|hěn}{高|gāo} (he's tall).
Tall for people, high for things. How tall: {多|duō}{高|gāo}？ The opposite for people, {矮|ǎi}, is HSK 3.
vocab.exampleEn: Your older brother is really tall!

vocab.note: For length and time. Not for tall people ({高|gāo}). Read {长|zhǎng}, the same character means "to grow" (HSK 3).
Also a measure word for cattle: {一|yì}{头|tóu}{牛|niú}. {头疼|tóu téng}: headache.
vocab.exampleEn: That child has a big head.

vocab.note: Light second syllable. One eye: {一|yì}{只|zhī}{眼睛|yǎn jing}.
In {手机|shǒu jī} (mobile phone) and {手表|shǒu biǎo} (wristwatch).
{身体|shēn tǐ}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}: in good health. {您|nín}{身体|shēn tǐ}{好|hǎo}{吗|ma}？ is a kind greeting to an older person.
vocab.exampleEn: My grandpa is in good health.

vocab.note: After a verb, a state that lasts: {穿着|chuān zhe} (wearing), {开着|kāi zhe} (on, open). Negative {没|méi} + verb. Traditional (Taiwan) {著|zhe}.
vocab.example: {他|tā}{穿|chuān}{着|zhe}{红色|hóng sè}{的|de}{衣服|yī fu}。

vocab.note: Ask: {什么|shén me}{颜色|yán sè}？
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{什么|shén me}{颜色|yán sè}？

vocab.note: Before a noun: {红色|hóng sè}{的|de}{衣服|yī fu}, or short {红|hóng}{衣服|yī fu}.

vocab.example: {白色|bái sè}{的|de}{裤子|kù zi}{很|hěn}{好看|hǎo kàn}。
{他|tā}{的|de}{手机|shǒu jī}{是|shì}{黑色|hēi sè}{的|de}。

vocab.note: Write the two dots: lǜ (type lv4). {路|lù} (road) is another word.
Counted with {条|tiáo}: {一|yì}{条|tiáo}{裤子|kù zi}. Worn with {穿|chuān}.
vocab.example: {他|tā}{穿|chuān}{着|zhe}{黑色|hēi sè}{的|de}{裤子|kù zi}。

vocab.note: Counted with {块|kuài}: {一|yí}{块|kuài}{手表|shǒu biǎo}. Traditional {手錶|shǒu biǎo} ({錶|biǎo} for watches, {表|biǎo} for tables and forms).
vocab.example: {这|zhè}{块|kuài}{手表|shǒu biǎo}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{爷爷|yé ye}{的|de}。

vocab.note: The neutral word. Also heard: {先生|xiān sheng}, {老公|lǎo gōng} (informal), {爱人|ài ren} (spouse).
The neutral word. Also heard: {太太|tài tai}, {老婆|lǎo po} (informal), {爱人|ài ren} (spouse).
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{妻子|qī zi}{在|zài}{大学|dà xué}{工作|gōng zuò}。
vocab.exampleEn: My wife works at a university.

vocab.note: Said xiǎo hár. Also {小孩|xiǎo hái} without the northern -r. {孩子|hái zi} is also someone's son or daughter.
vocab.example: {那|nà}{个|gè}{小孩儿|xiǎo háir}{真|zhēn}{漂亮|piào liang}！
{他们|tā men}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{男孩儿|nán háir}。
{那|nà}{个|gè}{女孩儿|nǚ háir}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{妹妹|mèi mei}。
vocab.exampleEn: That girl is my younger sister.

vocab.note: Before a measure word, with {都|dōu} before the verb: {每|měi}{个|gè}{人|rén}{都|dōu}…, {每天|měi tiān}{都|dōu}… ({天|tiān} and {年|nián} need no {个|gè}).
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{每天|měi tiān}{都|dōu}{七|qī}{点|diǎn}{起床|qǐ chuáng}。
vocab.exampleEn: I get up at seven every day.

vocab.note: After the subject, before the verb (and before {在|zài} + place).
vocab.example: {我们|wǒ men}{经常|jīng cháng}{在|zài}{家|jiā}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}。

vocab.note: Also {有时候|yǒu shí hou}. Before the verb or at the start: {有时|yǒu shí}…，{有时|yǒu shí}… (sometimes…, sometimes…).
vocab.example: {星期天|xīng qī tiān}{我|wǒ}{有时|yǒu shí}{在|zài}{家|jiā}{休息|xiū xi}。
vocab.exampleEn: On Sundays I sometimes stay at home and rest.

vocab.note: {洗|xǐ}{衣服|yī fu} (do the washing), {洗|xǐ}{手|shǒu} (wash your hands). Doubled: {洗洗|xǐ xi}{手|shǒu}.
vocab.exampleEn: You should wash your hands before eating.

vocab.note: Often paired with {所以|suǒ yǐ}: {因为|yīn wèi}…，{所以|suǒ yǐ}…. Answers {为什么|wèi shén me} (why).
vocab.example: {因为|yīn wèi}{我|wǒ}{头|tóu}{疼|téng}，{所以|suǒ yǐ}{没|méi}{去|qù}{上课|shàng kè}。
vocab.exampleEn: I had a headache, so I didn't go to class.

vocab.note: Starts its clause, before the subject. Said suó yǐ (two third tones).
vocab.example: {今天|jīn tiān}{很|hěn}{冷|lěng}，{所以|suǒ yǐ}{我|wǒ}{在|zài}{家|jiā}。
vocab.exampleEn: It's cold today, so I'm staying at home.

vocab.note: {不|bù}{舒服|shū fu}: unwell. {你|nǐ}{哪儿|nǎr}{不|bù}{舒服|shū fu}？ (What's wrong?)
Both "tired" and "tiring": {我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{累|lèi}, {这|zhè}{个|gè}{工作|gōng zuò}{很|hěn}{累|lèi}.
Body part + {疼|téng}: {我|wǒ}{头|tóu}{疼|téng} (I have a headache). Also "to dote on": {奶奶|nǎi nai}{很|hěn}{疼|téng}{我|wǒ}.
Taken with {吃|chī}: {吃|chī}{药|yào}. Same sound as {要|yào} (want; should).

vocab.example: {学校|xué xiào}{外边|wài bian}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{药店|yào diàn}。
vocab.exampleEn: There's a pharmacy outside the school.

vocab.note: One word for both. {笑|xiào}{着|zhe}{说|shuō}: said with a smile.
Third tone; {坐|zuò} (to sit) and {做|zuò} (to do) fall. Mostly in words and directions: {左边|zuǒ bian}, {左手|zuǒ shǒu}, {往|wǎng}{左|zuǒ}{走|zǒu}.
vocab.example: {他|tā}{的|de}{左手|zuǒ shǒu}{有点儿|yǒu diǎnr}{疼|téng}。
vocab.exampleEn: His left hand hurts a bit.

vocab.note: Fourth tone; {有|yǒu} (to have) dips. {右|yòu} has {口|kǒu} under the top, {有|yǒu} has {月|yuè}.
vocab.exampleEn: What's wrong with your right hand?

vocab.note: {边|biān} is light. "To the left of X" is X ({的|de}) {左边|zuǒ bian}: {学校|xué xiào}{左边|zuǒ bian}. {左面|zuǒ miàn} means the same.
vocab.example: {超市|chāo shì}{在|zài}{学校|xué xiào}{左边|zuǒ bian}。
vocab.exampleEn: The supermarket is to the left of the school.

vocab.note: {边|biān} is light. "To the right of X" is X ({的|de}) {右边|yòu bian}. {右面|yòu miàn} means the same.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{右边|yòu bian}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{同学|tóng xué}。
vocab.exampleEn: On my right is my classmate.

vocab.note: Unlike {左边|zuǒ bian}, its {边|biān} keeps the first tone. No -{面|miàn} form.
vocab.example: {药店|yào diàn}{在|zài}{医院|yī yuàn}{旁边|páng biān}。
vocab.exampleEn: The pharmacy is next to the hospital.

vocab.note: The same as {前边|qián bian}; {面|miàn} is often light in speech. "In front of X" is X ({的|de}) {前面|qián miàn}.
The same as {后边|hòu bian}. {={后|hòu}=} becomes {後|hòu} in traditional script; {面|miàn} stays {面|miàn}.
